name: 's-Gravelandse Veer
en: The quay used to be the mooring place of the scheduled passenger barges (beurtschepen) to this village in Het Gooi, where a number of Amsterdam regent families had their country residences. Before 1913 the quay was called Binnen-Amstel.

name: 's-Gravendijkdreef
en: Name of a farm in Noordwijkerhout (Zuid-Holland).

name: 's-Gravenhekje
en: Until the eighteenth century this was a timber storage yard. According to a bylaw (keur) of 1663, this timber yard could only be closed off with a hek (gate). It is assumed that a timber merchant named De Graaf had his timber yard here, hence De Graafs hek and later 's-Gravenhek. The name first appears towards the end of the eighteenth century.

name: 's-Gravesandeplein
en: Willem Jan van 's-Gravesande (1688-1742), professor of mathematics and astronomy at Leiden. He was the first follower of Newton in the Netherlands.

name: 's-Gravesandestraat
en: Willem Jan van 's-Gravesande (1688-1742), professor of mathematics and astronomy at Leiden. He was the first follower of Newton in the Netherlands.

name: 't Kleine Loopveld
en: The name recalls the history of Amstelland. In the sixteenth century many inhabitants of the area made their living by dredging. Dredging up the deep peat layer created large lakes, between which strips of land called loopvelden (walking fields) were left so that people could get from one village to another. One of these was the Kleine Loopveld, which was later called Kalfjeslaan. The name has now been given to a strip of parkland. The Grote Loopveld is now the Ouderkerkerlaan in Amstelveen.

name: 't Nopeind
en: Old local name, formed by contraction and corruption of 'op 't einde' (at the end).

name: 't Voorwerf
en: Old local name. Werf (yard) is used to denote a site where work is carried out.

name: 1e Glanshof
en: The name belongs to the theme 'Sociaal en tevreden wonen' (Social and contented living) for the G-buurt Grunder/Grubbehoeve.

name: 1e Kekerstraat
en: A legume. The Middle Dutch word keker is borrowed from the Latin cicer(a), meaning 'grey pea'. Because the vowel was shortened, keker came to sound like kikker. A kikkererwt (chickpea) is therefore really a 'pea pea'.

name: 2e Glanshof
en: The name belongs to the theme 'Sociaal en tevreden wonen' (Social and contented living) for the G-buurt Grunder/Grubbehoeve.

name: 2e Kekerstraat
en: A legume. The Middle Dutch word keker is borrowed from the Latin cicer(a), meaning 'grey pea'. Because the vowel was shortened, keker came to sound like kikker. A kikkererwt (chickpea) is therefore really a 'pea pea'.

name: 3e Kekerstraat
en: A legume. The Middle Dutch word keker is borrowed from the Latin cicer(a), meaning 'grey pea'. Because the vowel was shortened, keker came to sound like kikker. A kikkererwt (chickpea) is therefore really a 'pea pea'.

name: A. Eversplein
en: Adriaan Evers (1914-1997), architect. Together with Geert Sarlemijn he designed churches, schools and housing. He was an exponent of the conservative Bossche School, which is associated with Catholicism.

name: A. Moenstraat
en: Adriaan Moen (1879-1950), Amsterdam architect. He designed various factory buildings, villas and shops in the style of the Amsterdamse School. He built the Betlehemkerk on the Zwanenplein.

name: A. Reitsmakade
en: Auguste Chrétien Joseph Reitsma (1922-1943), resistance fighter. He worked for the underground press and was one of the nine people involved in the attack on the Amsterdam population registry (Amsterdams Bevolkingsregister) on 27 March 1943. He was executed by firing squad in Overveen on 1 July 1943.

name: A.A. de Lannoy-Willemsstraat
en: Angela Altagracia de Lannoy-Willems (1913-1983), born on Curaçao. From the founding of the Nationale Volkspartij onwards, she was active in the party's women's section. In 1949 she became the first woman to be sworn in as a member of the Staten van de Nederlandse Antillen, and in 1951 she was also elected a member of the Eilandsraad van Curaçao.

name: A.J. Koejemansstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1903-1982), editor-in-chief of the underground newspaper 'De Waarheid' (The Truth). He worked for broad cooperation within the resistance.

name: A.J. Krophollerstraat
en: Alexander Jacobus Kropholler (1881-1973), architect. He mainly built churches and town halls, and was known for his brickwork, sturdy furniture, heavy doors and generous timber roofs.

name: A.M. de Jongstraat
en: Adrianus M. de Jong (1888-1943), novelist, murdered by the occupiers in his home in Blaricum. He is best known for his Merijntje Gijzen cycle.

name: A.S. Onderwijzerhof
en: Abraham Samson Onderwijzer (1862-1934), rabbi from 1888 and chief rabbi of the Joodse Gemeente Amsterdam (Jewish Community of Amsterdam) from 1917. The courtyard was laid out on a site behind three former synagogues (since 1987 the Joods Historisch Museum).

name: Aaf Bouberstraat
en: Aafje ten Hoope (1885-1974), actress, wife of Herman Bouber. She started out in 1911 with Colnot and Poons, and from 1920 she and her husband ran their own company: Het Volkstoneel. She acted in 'De Jantjes' and in 'Op hoop van Zegen'.

name: Aagtdorperpad
en: Village in Noord-Holland, part of the municipality of Schoorl.

name: Aakhof
en: An aak is a flat-bottomed inland vessel.

name: Aakstraat
en: An aak is a flat-bottomed inland vessel.

name: Aalbersestraat
en: Petrus Josephus Mattheus Aalberse (1871-1948). Roman Catholic politician and statesman, professor at Delft. Minister of Labour, Commerce and Industry from 1918 to 1925.

name: Aalsmeerplein
en: Town in Noord-Holland, the largest flower centre in Europe.

name: Aalsmeerweg
en: Town in Noord-Holland, the largest flower centre in Europe.

name: Aambeeldstraat
en: An aambeeld (anvil) is a blacksmith's tool: an iron block for forging on. Before 1948 the street was part of the Schaafstraat.

name: Aandammerbrug
en: The Aandammerbrug is named after the Aandammergouw, in which it lies, seen from the municipality of Broek in Waterland. The Aandammerbrug is one of the smallest bridges in Amsterdam; it was originally a wooden bridge built on six trestles. It was replaced by a so-called hoge zijl (high sluice).

name: Aandewind
en: A term for a position in sailing.

name: Aardbeistraat
en: The fruit.

name: Aaron Coplandstraat
en: American composer (1900-1990). He composed symphonies, ballets, film music and an opera ('The tender land'). He promoted American music through publicity and lectures.

name: Aart van der Leeuwstraat
en: Writer (1876-1931), author of sketches, stories and rural idylls.

name: Abbenesstraat
en: Village in the Haarlemmermeer.

name: Abberdaan
en: The Scottish port of Aberdeen, in a spelling found on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Abcouderpad
en: Name of the underlying path.

name: Abcouderstraatweg
en: The road leads to the village of Abcoude (Utrecht). Before the motorway was built, it was the route between Amsterdam and Utrecht.

name: Abdellah Zakibrug
en: Abdellah Zaki (ntb 1936 – Lelystad, 2017) was a Dutch-Moroccan artist with a love of history and culture. His work focused mostly on flowers and Amsterdam cityscapes. The naming also symbolises labour migration and the connection between two cultures.

name: Abe Lenstralaan
en: Frisian footballer (1920-1985). At fifteen he made his debut in Heerenveen's first team. At nineteen he played for the Dutch national team for the first time, and he went on to play for it 47 times in all. He scored 33 goals for Oranje in total, as many as Johan Cruijff later did. In 1951 Lenstra was chosen as the first Sportsman of the Year.

name: Abebe Bikilalaan
en: Ethiopian athlete who won gold in the marathon at the 1960 Olympic Games in Rome. He became a legend because he ran it barefoot. In 1964 he won gold again, this time not barefoot.

name: Abidjanweg
en: African port city in Ivory Coast. The street lies near the Afrikahaven in the western port area.

name: Abraham de Haanstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1910-1945) who was part of a resistance group within the Kromhout Motorenfabriek, where he worked. After the February Strike of 1941 he was arrested and released, and in 1942 he was arrested again on suspicion of illegal activities. He died in Bergen-Belsen on 10 May 1945.

name: Abraham Kuyperplein
en: Minister (clergyman), politician and statesman (1837-1920). He promoted anti-revolutionary principles in church and society. He succeeded Groen van Prinsterer as leader of the Anti-Revolutionaire Partij (Anti-Revolutionary Party) and founded the Vrije Universiteit in 1880. In 1888, together with the Roman Catholic statesman Dr Schaepman, he forged the alliance between Rome and Dordt, which led to the first coalition cabinet (1888-1891). He was Prime Minister from 1901 to 1905.

name: Abraham Kuyperstraat
en: Minister (clergyman), politician and statesman (1837-1920). He promoted anti-revolutionary principles in church and society. He succeeded Groen van Prinsterer as leader of the Anti-Revolutionaire Partij (Anti-Revolutionary Party) and founded the Vrije Universiteit in 1880. In 1888, together with the Roman Catholic statesman Dr Schaepman, he forged the alliance between Rome and Dordt, which led to the first coalition cabinet (1888-1891). He was Prime Minister from 1901 to 1905.

name: Abram Dudok van Heelstraat
en: Abraham Everardus Dudok van Heel (1802-1893), who in 1827, together with Paul van Vlissingen, founded the company that later grew into Werkspoor.

name: Abrikozenstraat
en: The fruit.

name: Abtswoudepad
en: Named after the village of the same name near Delft (Zuid-Holland). It was named in 1959 with the suffix 'straat' (street); because the urban layout was changed, this was altered to 'pad' (path) in 1967.

name: Accason
en: A corrupted spelling of the French port of Archachon, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Accraweg
en: African port city, capital of Ghana. The street lies near the Afrikahaven in the western port area.

name: Accumulatorweg
en: A device for storing electrical energy (in Dutch usually shortened to accu).

name: Achillesstraat
en: The Greek hero who fell in the Trojan War (1195 to 1184 BC) when he was struck in his most vulnerable spot, his heel (the Achilles tendon).

name: Achter Oosteinde
en: Named after its location: behind (achter) the Oosteinde.

name: Achter Twiske
en: Twiske is the (West) Frisian word for 'between'. It is not known whether the name refers to the location near the small river Twiske or perhaps to the peat-lake area of the same name.

name: Achterdek
en: Achterdek (afterdeck): one of the decks of a ship.

name: Achtergouwtje
en: Named after its location relative to the village centre. Gouw is the Waterland word for a village road.

name: Achtergracht
en: This canal was dug around 1660 behind (achter) the four main canals, hence the name. It connected the Reguliersgracht with the Amstel. In 1870 most of it was filled in.

name: Achterlaan
en: Named after its location in relation to the village centre.

name: Achtersteven
en: Part of a ship's hull: the achtersteven is the stern.

name: Ad Grimmonbrug
en: Ad (Adriaan Alphonsus Maria) Grimmon (1883-1953). As a furniture maker, (interior) architect and colour specialist, he moved from the craft tradition of the Amsterdamse School towards industrial modernism. His career spanned the first half of the 20th century.

name: Ad Windighof
en: Important photojournalist (1912-1996). During the Second World War he belonged to the group of photographers later known as 'De Ondergedoken Camera' (The Hidden Camera), which clandestinely documented the resistance and the Hunger Winter. After the war he was a co-founder of the photographers' association GKf.

name: Adam Smithplein
en: Scottish economist (1723-1790), founder of classical liberalism. Smith believed that the pursuit of individual self-interest would produce the greatest benefit for society. A free market would yield the most for society as a whole. In his most important work, 'An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations' of 1776, he laid the foundations of modern capitalism.

name: Adam van Germezhof
en: Actor from the time of Vondel (1610-1667). He played roles in the plays of Brederode.

name: Adama van Scheltemaplein
en: Carel Steven Adama van Scheltema (1877-1924), socialist poet, popular for his simplicity and clarity.

name: Adamello
en: Mountain peak in Italy, 3554 metres high.

name: Adelaarsweg
en: The bird of prey (an adelaar is an eagle). Originally this road began at the IJ, where the 'Adelaarswegpont' ferry landed and where, until 1956, the station building of the tram to Purmerend and Edam stood. That section is now part of the Meeuwenlaan.

name: Adèle Opzoomerstraat
en: Writer (1857-1925) who wrote historical novels under the pseudonym A.S.L. Wallis.

name: Adenhaven
en: Port city in Yemen, on the Red Sea.

name: Adingerdorphof
en: A village near Medemblik that was drowned in the fifteenth century.

name: Admiraal De Ruijterweg
en: Michiel Adriaansz. de Ruyter (1607-1676), the renowned admiral of Holland and West Friesland. He was born in Vlissingen. In Amsterdam he lived on what is now the Prins Hendrikkade.

name: Admiraal Helfrichstraat
en: Conrad E.L. Helfrich (1886-1962), fleet commander and commander-in-chief of the Allied naval forces in the South-West Pacific (1942).

name: Admiralengracht
en: A collective name for the admirals from Holland and Zeeland after whom the streets in the surrounding neighbourhood are named.

name: Admiraliteitstraat
en: In the Republic of the Seven United Netherlands there were five boards of supreme commanders for naval affairs (admiralties), one of which was in Amsterdam.

name: Adolf van Nassaustraat
en: The younger brother (1540-1568) of Prince William of Orange. He was killed in the Battle of Heiligerlee against the Spaniards.

name: Adolphine Eduardine Kokplantsoen
en: Lawyer (1879-1928). In 1900 she began studying law, and three years later she became the first Dutch woman to be sworn in as a lawyer. She campaigned above all for improving women's right to a say in decisions and their legal capacity.

name: Adriaan Ditvoorsthof
en: Film director (1940-1987). With his dark, bizarre and lyrical films and his new ideas about film grammar and camerawork, he became the figurehead of Dutch experimental avant-garde cinema.

name: Adriaan Dorsmanstraat
en: Master builder (1638-1682). His works include the Ronde Lutherse kerk (1668) and the Oosterkerk (1669).

name: Adriaan Kluitstraat
en: Historian (1735-1807) and professor at Leiden. A specialist in the Middle Ages.

name: Adriaan Loosjesstraat
en: Teacher of the Mennonite congregation at Westzaandam (1689-1767), known for his 'Beschrijving van de Zaanlandse dorpen' (Description of the Zaan villages).

name: Adriaan van Bergenstraat
en: The Brabant peat skipper who in 1590 smuggled Sea Beggars into Breda in his peat boat.

name: Adriaan van der Horststraat
en: Actor, director and theatre manager (1868-1942). He staged the plays of Herman Heijermans. His wife, Wilhelmina van der Horst-van der Lugt Melsert, was a great tragedienne.

name: Adriaan van Oordthof
en: Writer (1865-1910) who belonged to the school of the Tachtigers (the Movement of the Eighties) (1865-1910). He wrote historical novels.

name: Adrianus van Waertweg
en: Resistance fighter (1915-1942) who took part in underground work in Amsterdam Noord, including distributing 'De Waarheid' and pamphlets aimed at the German occupier. He was arrested in 1941 and died a year later, on 9 June, in a prison.

name: Adrichemstraat
en: Former settlement in the Noordzeekanaal area, east of Beverwijk.

name: Adriënne Solserhof
en: Variety artiste (1873-1943) from the Jordaan who enjoyed great success in theatre and cinema in the 1920s.

name: Aert van Nesstraat
en: Naval captain (1625-1693), vice-admiral under Michiel de Ruyter from 1666. He took part in the expedition to Chatham and fought in the naval battles of Solebay and Kijkduin.

name: Afrikahaven
en: Continent. Africa has deserts, steppes, savannas and jungles. About two-fifths of Africa is desert.

name: Afrikanerplein
en: The usual term for white people born in South Africa. The square lies in the district where the names recall the struggle of the Dutch Boers, first against the indigenous population and later against the English.

name: Afroditekade
en: Figure from Greek mythology, goddess of love, fertility and beauty. Her equivalent in Roman mythology is Venus.

name: Agamemnonstraat
en: The legendary figure who led the Greeks against Troy in the Trojan War (1195 to 1184 BC).

name: Agatha Christiesingel
en: Agatha Mary Clarisse Miller (1891-1976), British writer of detective novels and stories. (Christie is the surname of her first husband.)

name: Agatha Dekenstraat
en: Aagje Deken (1741-1804), writer. Together with Betje Wolff she wrote novels, including 'Sara Burgerhart' and 'Willem Leevend'.

name: Akbarstraat
en: Title of a novel by Petrus van Limburg Brouwer (1829-1873), published in 1872.

name: Akerpolderstraat
en: Named after the Akerpolder in the former municipality of Sloten. Aker and Akerwatering are historical names that already appear on a 1687 map of Rijnland by Jan Dou.

name: Akersingel
en: Named after the Akerpolder in the former municipality of Sloten. Aker and Akerwatering are historical names that already appear on a 1687 map of Rijnland by Jan Dou.

name: Akersluis
en: Named after the Akerpolder in the former municipality of Sloten. Aker and Akerwatering are historical names that already appear on a 1687 map of Rijnland by Jan Dou.

name: Akerwateringstraat
en: Named after the Akerpolder in the former municipality of Sloten. Aker and Akerwatering are historical names that already appear on a 1687 map of Rijnland by Jan Dou.

name: Akkerdistelstraat
en: An akkerdistel (creeping thistle) is a species of thistle.

name: Akkerstraat
en: An akker is a field of arable land, often bounded by ditches.

name: Akkerwindeweg
en: Akkerwinde (field bindweed) is a climbing plant with white flowers.

name: Akoleienstraat
en: The akolei (columbine) is a flower of the buttercup family.

name: Alan Turingplein
en: Alan Mathison Turing (1912-1954), British computer pioneer, mathematician and logician. He played a key role in breaking coded German messages, which probably shortened the Second World War considerably. He was convicted of homosexual activity in 1952 and died two years later of cyanide poisoning. In the 21st century Britain apologised and rehabilitated him.

name: Alaskahaven
en: Alaska is the largest state of the United States, located in the far north-west of the North American mainland.

name: Albardagracht
en: Johan Willem Albarda (1879-1957), social-democratic politician and statesman. He was Minister of Waterstaat (public works and water management) from 1939 to 1945 (in London from 1940 to 1945).

name: Albardakade
en: Johan Willem Albarda (1879-1957), social-democratic politician and statesman. He was Minister of Waterstaat (public works and water management) from 1939 to 1945 (in London from 1940 to 1945).

name: Albatrospad
en: A bird. There are 24 species of albatross worldwide, most of them living in the southern hemisphere. The largest albatross has a wingspan of more than three metres, making it the largest seabird in the world.

name: Alberdingk Thijmstraat
en: Josephus Albertus Alberdingk Thijm (1820-1889), writer of poems and historical novellas, and professor of aesthetics and art history at the Academie voor Beeldende Kunst in Amsterdam.

name: Albert Camuslaan
en: French writer and philosopher (1913-1960), born in Algiers. He was one of the leading representatives of existentialism. In 1957 he received the Nobel Prize in Literature.

name: Albert Cuypstraat
en: Landscape and portrait painter (1620-1691). The street was laid out after the Zaagmolensloot was filled in. Until the second half of the nineteenth century, a number of timber sawmills stood here. In 2005 the Albert Cuypmarkt, which is held in this street, marked its hundredth anniversary.

name: Albert Hahnplantsoen
en: Political cartoonist (1877-1918), mainly of caricatures. The park was previously called Willem Witsenplantsoen.

name: Albert Helmanbrug
en: Albert Helman is the pseudonym of Lodewijk Alphonsus Maria Lichtveld (1903-1996). He was a Dutch-Surinamese writer, politician and resistance fighter. His best-known novels are Zuid-Zuidwest (South-Southwest) from 1926 and De stille Plantage (The Silent Plantation) from 1931. He received an honorary doctorate from the Universiteit van Amsterdam and died in Buitenveldert.

name: Albert Luthulistraat
en: The South African Albert John Luthuli (1898-1967), former president of the African National Congress (ANC), and until the 1950s the principal spokesman of the non-violent resistance to apartheid. In 1960 he received the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Albert Molhof
en: Albert Mol (Amsterdam, 3 January 1917 – Laren (Gelderland), 9 March 2004) was a Dutch actor, dancer, cabaret performer and writer.

name: Albert Neuhuysstraat
en: Painter (1844-1914), known among other things for his small domestic interiors from Laren.

name: Albert Schultenshof
en: Linguist (1666-1750), professor at Franeker and Leiden. He discovered the importance of Arabic for the study of Hebrew.

name: Albert Verweystraat
en: Poet and critic (1865-1937), professor at Leiden from 1924 to 1935. Co-founder of 'De Nieuwe Gids' (The New Guide), and later founder and editor of the literary magazine 'De Beweging' (The Movement). His collected criticism and essays have been published in ten volumes. He had an important influence on the young poets of his time.

name: Albert Wittenbergplein
en: During the Second World War, the Wittenberg family lived at President Brandstraat 32 II. At that time the family consisted of the parents, Albert and Janna, and their two children, Albert and Tine. Albert Wittenberg was a Surinamese man from Paramaribo who was also in the resistance. From the end of February 1943 until September 1945, they lovingly took into their family a Jewish girl who was then 6 weeks old. Albert Wittenberg was arrested in 1944 by a Dutch policeman. After the remand prison on the Weteringschans came the camps of Vught and (probably) Dora-Mittelbau. As the Americans approached, thousands of prisoners were put on transport to the Neuengamme camp. Between Hannover and Berlin, near Gardelegen, the train could go no further because of constant attacks. The remaining SS men sought local help, including the Hitlerjugend (Hitler Youth), to guard the prisoners. On 13 April 1945, a few hours before the Americans arrived, more than a thousand prisoners were burned alive in a grain barn into which they had been herded. Anyone who tried to escape was shot. Wittenberg, too, met this horrific fate. On 7 November 2011, Albert and Janna were posthumously awarded the Yad Vashem honour, which was presented to surviving relatives of the family.

name: Albertus Magnushof
en: German theologian and philosopher (1193-1280). One of the founders of scholasticism: the philosophy that tries to make the teaching of the church comprehensible to reason. Magnus was the teacher of Thomas Aquinas.

name: Alblasstraat
en: Small river in the Alblasserwaard.

name: Albrecht Dürerstraat
en: German painter (1471-1528), also a renowned engraver and woodcut artist.

name: Albrecht Rodenbachhof
en: Flemish poet (1856-1880), the soul of the Flemish student movement.

name: Alcantarastraat
en: A lake in Spain, the Embalse Alcantara, located in the province of Extremadura near the border with Portugal.

name: Aldebaranplein
en: A star in the constellation Taurus (the Bull).

name: Aldebaranstraat
en: A star in the constellation Taurus (the Bull).

name: Aldendriel
en: A restored seventeenth-century castle near Mill (Noord-Brabant), originally dating from around 1500.

name: Aldengoor
en: Aldengoor or Aldenghoir, a castle near Haelen, close to Roermond (Limburg).

name: Aldo van Eyckbrug
en: Aldo van Eyck (1918-1999) is best known as the architect of the Burgerweeshuis on the nearby IJsbaanpad. His colleagues named him 'Dutch architect of the century'.

name: Aletta Jacobslaan
en: Physician (1854-1929) who in 1879 became the first woman doctor to set up practice in the Netherlands. A campaigner for women's emancipation.

name: Alexander Boersstraat
en: Alexander Boers (1842-1890), burgomaster of Nieuwer-Amstel from 1885 to 1890. The street belonged to that municipality until 1 May 1896.

name: Alexander Dumaslaan
en: Named after two French novelists, namely the father, the pen name of Davy de la Pailleterie (1802-1870), author of works including 'De drie musketiers' (The Three Musketeers), and the son (1824-1875), author of works including 'La dame aux camélias'.

name: Alexanderkade
en: Prince Willem Alexander Karel Hendrik Frederik (1851-1884), youngest son of King Willem III. His early death made Princess Wilhelmina heir to the throne.

name: Alexanderplein
en: Prince Willem Alexander Karel Hendrik Frederik (1851-1884), youngest son of King Willem III. His early death made Princess Wilhelmina heir to the throne.

name: Alexandrine Tinnehof
en: Alexandrine Pieternella Francoise Tinne (1835-1869), traveller and pioneer of photography. Together with her mother and aunt she travelled through North Africa, visiting places that were not yet on the map. In 1860-'61 she took photographs of her birthplace, Den Haag.

name: Alfred Döblinstraat
en: German writer and physician (1878-1957) who went into exile abroad in 1933, where he continued to publish. One of his best-known novels is 'Berlin Alexanderplatz'.

name: Algolstraat
en: A double star in the constellation Perseus.

name: Alhambralaan
en: The palace and fortress of the Moorish rulers in Granada. The name literally means 'the red castle', because the palace is built of red brick. It is a magnificent monument of Islamic secular architecture, built mainly between 1238 and 1358.

name: Alida van den Bosstraat
en: Alida Johanna van den Bos (1902-2003), an Amsterdam gymnast. With the gymnastics team she won gold at the 1928 Olympic Games in Amsterdam, which made her one of the first Dutch women to become Olympic champions.

name: Alkmaarstraat
en: The town in Noord-Holland.

name: Allard Piersonstraat
en: Walloon Church minister (in Liège and Rotterdam), philosopher and aesthetician (1831-1896). From 1877 he was professor of art history, first in Heidelberg and later in Amsterdam. His major work was 'Onze geestelijke voorouders' (Our spiritual ancestors). He campaigned for state schools.

name: Allen Ginsbergstraat
en: Irwin Allen Ginsberg (1926-1997) was a Jewish American poet.

name: Allenstraat
en: The lake Loch Allen, in County Leitrim, Northern Ireland.

name: Alma Tademastraat
en: Sir Laurens Alma Tadema (1836-1912), Dutch-English painter of historical subjects. He did much of his work in England. He is buried in St Paul's Cathedral in London.

name: Almstraat
en: The Alm, a small river in the Land van Altena (Noord-Brabant).

name: Alpert van Metzhof
en: Also known simply as Alpertus. He lived around the year 1000 and is regarded as the first historian of the northern Netherlands.

name: Aluminiumbrug
en: This drawbridge is called Aluminiumbrug because in 1956 its leaf (the bridge deck) was made of aluminium, the first in the Netherlands. Another name for it was Dwingerbrug, after the neighbouring bastion 'Swijght Utrecht'.

name: Amaliastraat
en: Amalia van Solms (1602-1675), wife of stadholder Frederik Hendrik.

name: Amandelstraat
en: The fruit of the almond tree.

name: Amazonenstraat
en: The female warriors of Greek mythology.

name: Ambonplein
en: An island in Indonesia, part of the Moluccas.

name: Ambonstraat
en: An island in Indonesia, part of the Moluccas.

name: Amelandstraat
en: A Wadden island (Noord-Holland).

name: Amerbos
en: The small nature reserve near Amen, close to Rolde (Drente).

name: Amerikahaven
en: The continent.

name: Amerikahavenweg
en: The continent.

name: Amoebastraat
en: A microscopic water creature.

name: Ampèrestraat
en: André Marie Ampère (1775-1836), French mathematician and physicist. His name is now used internationally for the unit of electric current.

name: Amstel
en: The river to which Amsterdam owes its name and its origin.

name: Amstelbestpad
en: A historic farm or country house along the Amstel, roughly where the Weesperzijde is today.

name: Amstelbeststraat
en: A historic farm or country house along the Amstel, roughly where the Weesperzijde is today.

name: Amstelboulevard
en: A boulevard at right angles to the Amstel.

name: Amsteldijk
en: A canal dug around 1920 as part of Berlage's Plan Zuid. It connects the river of the same name with a five-way junction of canals, including the Boerenwetering, the Noorder Amstelkanaal and the Zuider Amstelkanaal.

name: Amstelkade
en: A canal dug around 1920 as part of Berlage's Plan Zuid. It connects the river of the same name with a five-way junction of canals, including the Boerenwetering, the Noorder Amstelkanaal and the Zuider Amstelkanaal.

name: Amstelkanaal
en: A canal dug around 1920 as part of Berlage's Plan Zuid. It connects the river of the same name with a five-way junction of canals, including the Boerenwetering, the Noorder Amstelkanaal and the Zuider Amstelkanaal.

name: Amstelpark
en: City park near the Amstel.

name: Amstelplein
en: A canal dug around 1920 as part of Berlage's Plan Zuid. It connects the river of the same name with a five-way junction of canals, including the Boerenwetering, the Noorder Amstelkanaal and the Zuider Amstelkanaal.

name: Amstelstraat
en: The river.

name: Amstelstroombrug
en: The bridge is named after the avenue. The Amstelstroomlaan is named after a former country house (estate) on the Amsteldijk, demolished in 1916. A house already stood here in 1583, and it was known by the name Amstelstroom.

name: Amstelstroomlaan
en: Former country house (estate) on the Amsteldijk, demolished in 1916. A house already stood here in 1583; in 1806 Agatha Clara Crol sold it under the name Amstelstroom. It had previously been called Borssenburg.

name: Amstelveenseweg
en: Village. Before 1 January 1964 the municipality was called Nieuwer-Amstel. Before it was widened in 1898, the stretch of the road along the Vondelpark as far as the Overtoom was called Dubbele Buurt.

name: Amstelveld
en: The river.

name: Amstelvlietstraat
en: Historic country house (estate) on the Amsteldijk. It was built after 1721 by Gerrit Nieuwenhuizen, who originally called it Meerhuizen. It has been known as Amstelvliet since 1784. It was demolished in or after 1916.

name: Amsterdam Rijnkanaalkade
en: Busy canal, 72 kilometres long, that links the IJ via Utrecht to the Waal near Tiel. It is part of an important route to the Ruhr area.

name: Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal
en: Busy canal, 72 kilometres long, that links the IJ via Utrecht to the Waal near Tiel. It is part of an important route to the Ruhr area.

name: Amundsenweg
en: Roald Amundsen (1872-1928), Norwegian polar explorer. In 1903 he discovered the Northwest Passage. He lost his life during an attempt to rescue the crew of the airship Italia.

name: Analoogstraat
en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

name: Anatole Francesingel
en: Pen name of Jacques Anatole Francois Thibault (1844-1924), French novelist and essayist. He received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1921.

name: Anderiesenstraat
en: Willem Gerardus Anderiesen (1903-1944), Amsterdam footballer. Between 1925 and 1940 he played 309 league matches for Ajax and scored 20 goals. He played 46 internationals, an Ajax record that was not broken until 1979, by Ruud Krol.

name: Anderlechtlaan
en: Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

name: Andersensingel
en: Hans Christian Andersen (1805-1875), Danish writer of novels, poems and travel writing. He became best known for his fairy tales.

name: Andijkstraat
en: Village in Noord-Holland, east of Medemblik.

name: Andoornstraat
en: A plant belonging to the mint family.

name: Andreas Bonnstraat
en: Amsterdam professor of surgery. He lived from 1738 to 1817.

name: Andreas Schelfhoutstraat
en: Painter (1787-1870) of landscapes and winter scenes. The street came within the boundaries of Amsterdam under the name Bosboomstraat (council decision of Sloten, 21 November 1905), but this name was changed to avoid confusion with the Bosboom-Toussaintstraat, named after Bosboom's wife.

name: Andreasplein
en: Former hospital that stood on this site from the 1970s. It opened in 1891 on the Keizersgracht as the Nederlandse Hervormde Diaconessen Inrichting. In 1996 it merged with the Sint Lucasziekenhuis and later moved to that location.

name: Andrej Sacharovstraat
en: Russian physicist (1921-1989) and human rights activist. He opposed nuclear armament and was an outspoken critic of the Soviet regime. In 1975 he received the Nobel Peace Prize. In 1980 he was arrested and exiled to Gorky.

name: Andries Copierstraat
en: Andries Dirk Copier (1901-1991), glass artist, designer and ceramicist. He designed various dinner services and glassware, such as the popular Gilde wine glass.

name: Andries Snoekstraat
en: Actor (1766-1829). Together with Majofski and Wattier, he was a dominant figure in the heyday of Dutch theatre up to 1820.

name: Andries Vierlinghstraat
en: Hydraulic engineer (1507-1579), known in particular for building dikes, including near Steenbergen.

name: Andromedastraat
en: A constellation, and a nebula lying far beyond our Milky Way galaxy.

name: Anemoonstraat
en: A plant belonging to the buttercup family.

name: Anfieldroad
en: A stadium in Liverpool. On 14 December 1966, Ajax played a round-of-16 match of the European Cup (Europa Cup voor Landskampioenen) in this stadium: Liverpool FC vs Ajax (2-2).

name: Angenietje Swarthofbrug
en: Around 1800, Amsterdam had thousands of foundlings. They were placed in the care of the Aalmoezeniersweeshuis on the Prinsengracht (near the bridge), which boarded them out with wet nurses in the city. These were women who wanted to add a wet nurse's wage to their household income. Angenietje Swart was one of them. In all, she cared for 126 children.

name: Anielewiczsingel
en: Mordechai Anielewicz was one of the Polish Jews who organised the uprising in the Warsaw Ghetto in 1943. He was killed on 7 May of that year.

name: Anjeliersstraat
en: An anjelier (carnation) is a flower belonging to the pink family.

name: Ank van der Moerstraat
en: Anna Maria van der Moer (1912-1983) was an actress who performed with various companies, including the Nederlandse Comedie from 1950 to 1972. She also worked as a director and actress on radio and television programmes.

name: Ankerweg
en: An anker (anchor) is the ship's part.

name: Anna Bijnsstraat
en: Anna Bijns (1494-1575) was a poet from the Southern Netherlands. She fiercely opposed the teachings of Luther.

name: Anna Blamansingel
en: Anna Blaman was the pen name of Johanna Petronella Vrugt (1905-1960), a writer. She wrote about the problems of modern life. Her view of the world is related to that of French existentialism. In 1957 she received the P.C. Hooftprijs.

name: Anna Paulownabrug
en: Anna Paulowna (1795-1865) married the Hereditary Prince of Orange, later King William II, on 21 February 1816. Through this marriage she received the title of Hereditary Princess. After William I abdicated on 7 October 1840, William II was inaugurated on 28 November in the Nieuwe Kerk in Amsterdam. Under Anna's influence, court life took on a more royal grandeur. Although her upbringing gave her a distant and sometimes haughty manner as queen, she was deeply involved in Dutch society. She had learned Dutch from the court teacher Arie van der Spuij and spoke it better than her husband, with whom she usually spoke French. Even as Hereditary Princess she worked with conviction for 'the people'. She set up 'commissiën van weldadigheid' (charity committees) in Soest and Baarn, and in 1832, with her support, the Koninklijke Winternaaischool Scheveningen was founded to teach needy women and girls sewing and needlework skills. Near bridge 136, all the streets are named after members of the House of Orange.

name: Anna Pavlovastraat
en: Anna Pavlova was a Russian ballet dancer, choreographer, producer and teacher. She became famous for her performance of The Dying Swan.

name: Anna Spenglerstraat
en: Elisabeth Catharina (also called Anna) Spengler (1842-c.1905) was a nurse who worked with Johanna Reynvaan for several years on reorganising nursing at the Wilhelmina Gasthuis. The street was originally named Anna Sprenglerstraat in error (council decision of 3 April 1985).

name: Anna van Burenstraat
en: The first wife of Prince William of Orange (1533-1558).

name: Anna van den Vondelstraat
en: Daughter of Joost van den Vondel (1620-1675), who cared for her father for many years. The street was originally named Anna Vondelstraat, but was later renamed (council decision of 29 November 1986) because it was confused with the Vondelstraat.

name: Anna van Saksenbrug
en: Named after Anna van Saksen (1544-1577), the second wife of Willem van Oranje and mother of Prince Maurits and Princess Anna.

name: Anna Vockstraat
en: Anna Vock (1884-1962) founded the Swiss gay and lesbian association Schweizerisches Freundschafts Verband in 1933 and was its chair for the first few years. The club grew out of the women's club Amicitia and the club for homosexual men Excentric.

name: Annabellaweg
en: A juicy, sweet cherry from a white-flowering cherry tree.

name: Anne Frankstraat
en: Anne Frank, born to Jewish parents in 1929, was in hiding from 1942 to 1944 with her parents and other members of her family in the building at Prinsengracht 263, where she kept a diary. In 1944 the German occupiers discovered the family and deported them. Anne Frank died of illness and exhaustion in 1945 in the Bergen Belsen extermination camp.

name: Anne Kooistrahof
en: Anne Hendrik Kooistra (1919-1942) was a resistance fighter. He was born in Amsterdam and died in the Gross Rosen concentration camp. He was one of the pioneers among the underground workers in the Netherlands. He helped to organise the underground press and was also active in providing financial support to the victims of the Februaristaking (February Strike). He was also involved with the underground paper 'Vrij Nederland'.

name: Annemie Wolffbrug
en: The photographer Anna Maria Koller was known as Annemie Wolff and also used the pseudonym Marianne (Germany, 27 December 1906 - Amsterdam, 2 February 1994). In Munich she married the architect and photographer Helmuth Egon Wilhelm Wolff (1895-1940). In May 1933 they fled to Amsterdam, because as a Jew Helmuth could no longer work in Germany and a warrant had been issued for his arrest on false grounds. On the night of 14 to 15 May 1940, Annemie and Helmuth tried to take their own lives. They were found and taken to the Nederlands Israëlitisch Ziekenhuis, where Helmuth died. As a young widow of 35, Annemie had to get her life back on track. Major clients such as the City of Amsterdam dropped away, but she continued to work for Libelle, where she published under the name A.M. Koller. Letters from Berlin told her of the destruction of Helmuth's family, and in Amsterdam, too, loved ones disappeared. She took people in hiding into her home and helped the resistance with her photography wherever she could. She set up a photo studio in her living room, where between 1943 and 1945 she made portraits of hundreds of men, women and children. Many of the photos were commissioned as keepsakes by people who were about to be deported. Wolff also made portrait photos for false identity papers and as evidence for the 'Calmeyerdossiers' (Calmeyer files), named after the German official who dealt with requests to review a person's registration as a Jew. Wolff manipulated the photos by printing the hair and skin somewhat lighter. In this way, people tried to prove that they were not 'real' Jews. On 2 May 1945, Wolff photographed the food drops at Schiphol. After the liberation she resumed her work for the City of Amsterdam. Above all, she became the chronicler of the revival of the port of Amsterdam and of Schiphol. In a consistent, high-quality style she recorded the shipping and the flourishing of the Oostelijk Havengebied. In 1950 Annemie Wolff became a Dutch citizen.

name: Annie Boshof
en: Actress (1886-1975). In the 1910s she played many roles, often the lead, in films made by Hollandia, the film company of the director Maurits Binger. She belonged to the permanent core group of actors around Maurits Binger and was a true film diva in her day.

name: Annie M.G. Schmidtstraat
en: Anna Maria Geertruida Schmidt (1911-1995) wrote verse, songs, children's books, plays, musicals, cabaret texts, and radio and television programmes. For a long time she worked as a journalist for 'Het Parool'. Her children's books, including 'Pluk van de Petteflet' and the 'Jip en Janneke' series, are hugely popular.

name: Annie Romeinplein
en: Annie Romein-Verschoor (1895-1978) was a writer and historian. She was married to the historian Jan Romein, with whom she wrote several history books. In the 1950s she challenged the prevailing views on the position of women. Her autobiography 'Omzien in verwondering' (Looking back in wonder) appeared in 1970-1971 and shows her to be a sharp-witted and critical woman.

name: Anselmushof
en: Anselmus, Archbishop of Canterbury (1033-1109), is called the father of scholastic philosophy.

name: Anske Lammingastraat
en: Hydraulic engineer (1855-1920). He was the founder of irrigation engineering in what was then the Dutch East Indies.

name: Antarusstraat
en: Name of a star.

name: Anthonie van Akenstraat
en: Tennis player (1876-1966). She was Dutch champion three times at the beginning of the twentieth century. For a time she played under the pseudonym A.N. Thonie, because otherwise she would have damaged the family's good name. She was the first woman in the Netherlands to dare to serve overarm, although her racket regularly caught on the hat she had to wear on court.

name: Anthonie van Dijckstraat
en: Flemish painter (1599-1641), pupil of Rubens and court painter to Charles I of England. In his day he was the greatest portrait painter.

name: Anthony Fokkerweg
en: Aircraft manufacturer (1890-1939). He started out in a workshop in Berlin and later moved his company to Amsterdam. The Dutch Fokker factory supplied aircraft all over the world. In 1996 the N.V. Koninklijke Nederlandse Vliegtuigenfabriek was declared bankrupt.

name: Anthony Spatzierhof
en: Actor (1718-1777) and also theatre director. He performed abroad several times.

name: Antillenstraat
en: Group of islands in the Caribbean Sea, in particular the six islands that together form the Netherlands Antilles.

name: Anton Constandsestraat
en: Anton Levien Constandse (1899-1985), political writer. After the war he was foreign editor of the 'Algemeen Handelsblad' for twenty years. He is best known as the author of numerous books, pamphlets and political commentaries in which he promoted his anarchist-inspired views.

name: Anton de Komplein
en: Surinamese human rights campaigner (1898-1945). He fought for the democratic rights of the population and argued for the country's independence. He was arrested and in 1933 deported to the Netherlands, where he fought against unemployment and rising fascism. In 1944 he was arrested again by the Germans, and he died in the Neuengamme concentration camp.

name: Anton Hölzelsingel
en: Resistance fighter (1909-1945), involved in many clandestine activities.

name: Anton Jolingbrug
en: Antonius Jacobus Joling (1857-1934), architect. He learned his trade under Pierre Cuypers (1827-1921) and set up on his own around 1887. He mainly designed public buildings such as offices, hospitals and schools. The Peek & Cloppenburg building on the Dam is by Joling.

name: Anton Petershof
en: Actor (1812-1872), very popular with Amsterdam audiences in the mid-nineteenth century.

name: Anton Schleperspad
en: Lived from 1945 to 1993. He worked especially hard to preserve the area through which the path named after him runs: the Oeverlanden. He was a co-founder of the association 'De Oeverlanden blijven' (The Oeverlanden stay).

name: Anton Struikstraat
en: Thomas Antonie Struik (1897-1945), resistance fighter, born in Rotterdam, died in Lübeck (Germany).

name: Anton Verheijstraat
en: Musician (1871-1924), pianist, organist and conductor. He composed mainly music for male choirs.

name: Anton Waldorpstraat
en: Painter (1803-1866), a representative of the realist school. He painted landscapes, interiors and portraits.

name: Antonie Heinsiusstraat
en: Pensionary of Delft, later Grand Pensionary (1641-1720). He was a great supporter of Prince William III during his stadtholdership.

name: Antonio Vivaldistraat
en: Italian composer (1678-1741). From 1703 to 1740 he was attached to the Conservatorio dell'Ospedale della Pietà, one of the four famous music schools in Venice. Vivaldi's great importance as a composer lies in the development of the violin concerto. His most famous work is 'Le quattro stagioni' (The Four Seasons), published in Amsterdam in 1725.

name: Antony Moddermanstraat
en: Jurist (1838-1885), professor in Amsterdam and Leiden, and Minister of Justice.

name: Antoon Keldermansstraat
en: Flemish master builder (1450-1512). Among other works, he built the town halls of Middelburg and Veere.

name: Antwerpenbaan
en: Belgian city in the province of Antwerp.

name: Apollolaan
en: Apollo was one of the principal gods of Greek mythology: god of the sun, music and poetry, and leader of the Muses. The widened section of this avenue, near the Minervalaan, bore the name August Allebéplein until 1958.

name: Appelweg
en: The fruit of the apple tree.

name: Aragohof
en: Dominique F.J. Arago (1786-1853), French physicist and astronomer, discoverer of electromagnetism.

name: Arcadia
en: Region on the Greek peninsula of the Peloponnese. The area inspired the Greco-Roman ideal of an unspoilt society devoted to beauty and nature.

name: Arcellastraat
en: A microscopically small aquatic creature enclosed in a shell.

name: Archangelkade
en: The Russian port city on the Barents Sea (Arctic Ocean), a port that exports timber. Amsterdam merchants were already visiting the city regularly around 1600.

name: Archangelweg
en: The Russian port city on the Barents Sea (Arctic Ocean), a port that exports timber. Amsterdam merchants were already visiting the city regularly around 1600.

name: Archimedeslaan
en: Famous Greek mathematician and physicist (287-212 BC), known for Archimedes' principle, which states that "the upward force experienced by a body in a liquid is equal to the weight of the liquid displaced". When the municipality of Watergraafsmeer was abolished, the Archimedesweg was taken over under the name Langeweg (Watergraafsmeer council decision of 26 April 1901).

name: Archimedesplantsoen
en: Famous Greek mathematician and physicist (287-212 BC), known for Archimedes' principle, which states that "the upward force experienced by a body in a liquid is equal to the weight of the liquid displaced". When the municipality of Watergraafsmeer was abolished, the Archimedesweg was taken over under the name Langeweg (Watergraafsmeer council decision of 26 April 1901).

name: Archimedesweg
en: Famous Greek mathematician and physicist (287-212 BC), known for Archimedes' principle, which states that "the upward force experienced by a body in a liquid is equal to the weight of the liquid displaced". When the municipality of Watergraafsmeer was abolished, the Archimedesweg was taken over under the name Langeweg (Watergraafsmeer council decision of 26 April 1901).

name: Ardennenlaan
en: Hilly region in Belgium.

name: Arenborg
en: A seventeenth-century manor near Venlo (Limburg).

name: Arend Bontekoeplantsoen
en: Resistance fighter (1895-1945), born in Naarden, who died in the Sachsenhausen concentration camp (Germany).

name: Arendonksingel
en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

name: Arènpalmstraat
en: A palm species. The arèn palm, or sugar palm, is common in the Indonesian archipelago. This palm yields palm wine, sugar and flour.

name: Arent Janszoon Ernststraat
en: Arent Janszoon Ernst van Bassen, bailiff of Amstelland from 1569 to 1573.

name: Argonautenstraat
en: Greek sea heroes who sailed out on the ship Argo to fetch the Golden Fleece.

name: Argostraat
en: A former constellation, now divided into three smaller constellations.

name: Ariana Nozemanstraat
en: Ariana Nozeman, née van den Bergh (died 1661), actress. In 1655 she became the first woman to perform in the Amsterdamse Schouwburg.

name: Arie Biemondstraat
en: Neurologist (1902-1973), attached to the Wilhelminagasthuis. From 1947 to 1970 he was a professor at the Universiteit van Amsterdam.

name: Arij Prinsstraat
en: Industrialist and writer (1860-1922) who initially published under the pseudonym Cooplandt. He wrote naturalistic sketches and later medieval fantasies.

name: Aristotelesstraat
en: The greatest Greek philosopher of antiquity (384-322 BC). He had a great influence on the development of thought.

name: Arlandabrug
en: Name of Stockholm's airport.

name: Arlandaweg
en: Name of Stockholm's airport.

name: Armand Sunierbrug
en: Armand Louis Jean Sunier (Rotterdam, 17 December 1886 – Baarn, 13 May 1974) was a Dutch biologist and the third director of the Natura Artis Magistra zoo. Sunier prevented the deportation of staff and animals to Germany and turned a blind eye to people hiding in the zoo. He was also one of the key figures in the breeding programme set up to save the wisent (European bison) from extinction. In addition, he was a member of the International Union of Directors of Zoological Gardens for many years and briefly served as its president.

name: Armbrug
en: The seventh bridge over the Oudezijls Voorburgwal. The middle section of this wooden bridge at the O.Z. Armsteeg could be raised. It was rebuilt in 1882 and renewed in 1906.

name: Armeensebrug
en: Named after the nearby former Armenian church.

name: Arnold Geulincxpad
en: Philosopher from the Southern Netherlands (1626-1669).

name: Arnold Ingwersenpad
en: Architect (1882-1959). Among other works, in 1918-1919 he designed the area around the Zwanenplein and the Koekoeksplein in Amsterdam-Noord together with T. Kuipers.

name: Arnold Schönberglaan
en: American composer of Austrian origin (1874-1951). With his atonal compositions he broke with traditional harmony and its application. Together with his pupils Alban Berg and Anton Webern he formed the so-called Second Viennese School, which marks a turning point in the history of music.

name: Aron Wolff Berlijnbrug
en: Composer and conductor (1817-1870). He wrote more than two hundred works, including at least twenty large romantic ballets for the Stadschouwburg, where he was orchestra master from 1846.

name: Arondeusstraat
en: Willem Arondeus (1894-1943), painter and graphic artist. He was active in the resistance during the German occupation and was executed by firing squad in Haarlem. Among other things, he played a major part in organising the 1943 attack on the Bevolkingsregister (population register).

name: Artemisstraat
en: Goddess from Greek mythology, daughter of the supreme god Zeus and twin sister of Apollo. The Latin name of Artemis is Diana.

name: Arthur van Schendelstraat
en: Novelist (1874-1946). Originally a neo-romantic, he later dealt with simple Dutch themes.

name: Arubastraat
en: Part of the Netherlands Antilles until 1 January 1986. Since then an autonomous country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands (status aparte, 'separate status').

name: Ashaven
en: Cargo that was, and still is, shipped through the port of Amsterdam.

name: Asingaborg
en: Seventeenth-century castle near Middelstum (Groningen), restored in 1926.

name: Assendelftstraat
en: Village in Noord-Holland. The street was originally named Tweede Spaarndammerdwarsstraat (council decision of 30 March 1881). From 2 September 1913 to 6 June 1917 an Assendelftstraat existed in name at another location in this neighbourhood, but it was never built. In 1978 a change in the street pattern gave the street a completely different route.

name: Assumburg
en: Castle near Heemskerk (Noord-Holland), built in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries and restored in the seventeenth century and in 1911.

name: Asta Elstakstraat
en: The Surinamese Asta Elstak (1917-1994) made a great contribution both to Suriname and to the Surinamese community in the Netherlands. Among other things, she was a board member of the Landelijke Organisatie Surinaamse Ouderen (National Organisation of Surinamese Elderly).

name: Astasiastraat
en: A microscopically small aquatic organism.

name: Asterdwarsweg
en: A microscopically small aquatic organism.

name: Asterweg
en: Ornamental plant belonging to the daisy family.

name: Atatürk
en: Named after the first Turkish residential centre on this site. Mustafa Kemal (1881-1938), Turkish soldier and statesman, founder and first president of the Republic of Turkey. He radically reformed the old Turkey along Western European lines. He received the name Atatürk (= father of the Turks) in 1934, when surnames were introduced.

name: Atje Keulen-Deelstrastraat
en: Speed skater (1938-2013). One of the greatest Dutch skaters ever. Her record includes four world titles, three European titles and three medals at the 1972 Olympic Games in Sapporo. She also won 61 skating marathons.

name: Atlantisplein
en: A mythical island, already mentioned by Plato, with paradisiacal living conditions and an advanced civilisation, which was destroyed by a catastrophe. Suggested locations include the Atlantic Ocean and the Greek island of Santorini.

name: Atlas Maiorbrug
en: Named after the Atlas Maior, which Joan Blaeu produced in 1662 on the Bloemgracht. In 1672 this workshop burned out completely.

name: Atochabrug
en: A station in Madrid.

name: August Allebéplein
en: Painter and draughtsman (1846-1927), director of the Academie voor Beeldende Kunst. Against the lyrical character of the Haagse School (Hague School) he set a moderate realism.

name: August Vermeylenstraat
en: Flemish man of letters (1872-1945), professor at Ghent and founder of the monthly magazine 'Van nu en straks' (Of now and later). He wrote 'Overzicht van de nieuwe Vlaamse letteren' (Survey of the new Flemish literature).

name: Aurikelstraat
en: An ornamental plant, a species of primula.

name: Australiëhaven
en: The continent.

name: Australiëhavenweg
en: The continent.

name: Avalon
en: A mythical island in British waters, to which King Arthur is said to have sailed to recover from wounds received in battle.

name: Avenhornstraat
en: The village of Avenhorn, north of the Beemster.

name: Avercampstraat
en: Hendrik Avercamp (1585-1634), painter, mainly of winter scenes. Avercamp, who lived in Kampen from 1613, was born deaf and mute and was therefore nicknamed 'de stomme van Kampen' (the mute of Kampen).

name: Avogadrostraat
en: Italian physicist (1776-1856). He is known for Avogadro's law of 1814: 'equal volumes of different gases and vapours contain the same number of molecules at the same pressure and temperature'.

name: Azaleastraat
en: A small shrub, grown as a garden and house plant.

name: Azartplein
en: Since 1992 this has been the unofficial name of the spot on the island where the first new residents of the area got to know the boat dwellers and artists who were already living there. 'Azart' is Russian for inspiration.

name: Aziëhaven
en: The largest of the continents.

name: Aziëhavenweg
en: The largest of the continents.

name: B. Merkelbachsingel
en: Benjamin Merkelbach (1901-1961), Amsterdam architect. A follower of the Nieuwe Bouwen (New Building) movement, he was responsible for, among other things, housing blocks in West and commercial buildings near Nieuwendam. He became city architect (stadsbouwmeester) in 1956.

name: Baanakkerspad
en: A small nature reserve in the lake district of Jisp and Wormer (Noord-Holland).

name: Baanbrug
en: This bridge is named after the Lijnbaansgracht, which used to be called the Baangracht.

name: Baarsjesweg
en: The former inn 'De Drie Baarsjes' (The Three Little Perches), which at the time stood on the Kostverlorenvaart.

name: Baarsstraat
en: A freshwater fish: baars means perch.

name: Baas Gansendonckstraat
en: The main character of the novella of the same name by the Flemish writer Hendrik Conscience (1812-1883).

name: Bachplein
en: Johann Sebastian Bach (1685-1750), German composer. He was the most important member of the German Bach family, which produced many composers. His works include oratorios (the St Matthew Passion) and more than four hundred cantatas. He was the last and most universal representative of the Baroque.

name: Bachstraat
en: Johann Sebastian Bach (1685-1750), German composer. He was the most important member of the German Bach family, which produced many composers. His works include oratorios (the St Matthew Passion) and more than four hundred cantatas. He was the last and most universal representative of the Baroque.

name: Back-upstraat
en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

name: Backershagen
en: An eighteenth-century country house in Wassenaar (Zuid-Holland). The name is derived from the Backer and Hagen families.

name: Baden Powellweg
en: Lord Robert Baden Powell (1857-1941), English general in the Boer War. In 1908 he founded the Scout movement, of which he remained the international leader until his death.

name: Badhuiskade
en: The former Obelt bathhouse, built in 1914 and demolished around 1927. The road is no longer a public road and lies entirely on the grounds of the Shell laboratory.

name: Badrianhof
en: Gerhard Joseph Badrian (1906-1944), born in Upper Silesia (Germany), executed by firing squad in Amsterdam.

name: Baetostraat
en: A tragedy by P.C. Hooft (1581-1647).

name: Baffinstraat
en: William Baffin (1584-1622) was an English navigator. In 1616, while searching for the Northwest Passage, he discovered Baffin Bay and Baffin Island, both named after him.

name: Baionen
en: A corrupted spelling of the French port of Bayonne, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Bakhuizen van den Brinkhof
en: Reinier C. Bakhuizen van den Brink (1810-1865) was a man of letters and historian. He was on the editorial board of 'De Gids' and became National Archivist in 1854.

name: Bakhuys Roozeboomstraat
en: Hendrik Willem Bakhuys Roozeboom (1854-1907) was a chemist. He was a professor in Amsterdam from 1896.

name: Bakkersbrug
en: This drawbridge takes its name from the bakery that was housed on the adjoining Plantage Middenlaan until the early 1960s.

name: Bakkersstraat
en: This street, first recorded under this name in 1604, owes its name to the 'Backhuis' (bakehouse) that stood here from around 1595 to 1603. Ship's biscuits for the VOC were baked here.

name: Bakkerswaal
en: A nature reserve on the Lek near Lekkerkerk.

name: Bakkumstraat
en: A village in Noord-Holland.

name: Balatonmeerlaan
en: A lake in western Hungary.

name: Balboaplein
en: Vasco Nuñez de Balboa (1475-1517) was a Spanish explorer. In 1513 he discovered the Pacific Ocean, then called the South Sea.

name: Balboastraat
en: Vasco Nuñez de Balboa (1475-1517) was a Spanish explorer. In 1513 he discovered the Pacific Ocean, then called the South Sea.

name: Baldermoer
en: The town of Baltimore, a port on the south coast of Ireland, spelled as it appears on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Baldwinstraat
en: James Baldwin (1924-1987), American writer. Racism and homosexuality are the main themes of his work. He campaigned for civil rights alongside Martin Luther King, among others.

name: Balearenlaan
en: Spanish group of islands in the Mediterranean Sea. The best-known islands in the group are Majorca, Menorca, Ibiza and Formentera.

name: Balgzandstraat
en: The sandbank in the Wadden Sea, near Den Helder.

name: Balistraat
en: The island east of Java, in Indonesia. It is known for its Hindu works of art.

name: Balthasar Floriszstraat
en: Balthasar Florisz van Berkenrode (1591-1644), cartographer and land surveyor. In 1625 and 1644 he made large, highly accurate maps of Amsterdam.

name: Bamberghof
en: The Bamberg family of performers. Its best-known members were David Bamberg (1787-1858), a popular conjuror, and Eduard Bamberg (1816-1900), an actor and director of the 'Salon des Variëtés' in the Amstelstraat.

name: Bananenstraat
en: The fruit.

name: Bandijkstraat
en: A bandijk is a heavy river dike that holds back the water when river levels are high. The word 'ban' means jurisdiction or legal authority, and here it refers to the governing body responsible for such a dike.

name: Bankastraat
en: The island east of Sumatra in Indonesia, known for its tin mining.

name: Bankwerkerij
en: This and other streets were laid out on the site of the former Amsterdamse Droogdok Maatschappij (ADM). The names of the various workshops were used for the street names as a reminder of the site's former use.

name: Banne Buikslootlaan
en: Buiksloot was an independent municipality until 1921, when it was absorbed into Amsterdam. 'Ban' means both jurisdiction and legal authority. The Banne Buiksloot was traditionally one of the six bannen (jurisdictions) into which the bailiwick of Waterland was divided. After the Batavian Revolution of 1795 the word remained in use, but by then it referred only to the polder. The Waterland bannen were not abolished until 1936.

name: Banneplein
en: This square lies at the centre of the Buiksloot district, historically the Banne Buiksloot. In past centuries a ban or banne was an administrative area. Together, the bannen made up the bailiwick.

name: Banstraat
en: Joan Albert Ban (1597-1644), priest and composer. Among other works, he set texts by Vondel and Tesselschade to music.

name: Bantammerbrug
en: The name of this fixed bridge recalls the sixteenth century, when the Dutch brought goods from Bantam (Dutch East Indies) to Amsterdam.

name: Banterij
en: A corrupted spelling of the Irish port of Bantry, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Barajasweg
en: The name of Madrid's airport.

name: Barbara Strozzilaan
en: Italian composer (1619-1677), adopted daughter of the poet Giulio Strozzi. She studied music with Francesco Cavalli, the leading opera composer of his day. She wrote more than a hundred vocal works, including madrigals, cantatas, arias and duets.

name: Barbara van Meertenstraat
en: Anna Barbara van Meerten-Schilperoort (1778-1853), educationalist and writer. She wrote about, and campaigned for, the education of girls, poor relief and prisoners.

name: Barbusselaan
en: Henri Barbusse (1873-1933), French novelist.

name: Barcelonaplein
en: A port city on the east coast of Spain, to which the former KNSM (see KNSM-laan) ran a regular shipping service.

name: Barentszplein
en: Willem Barentszoon, the famous skipper who, together with Jacob van Heemskerck, tried in 1596 to reach the Indies by way of the Arctic Ocean. He spent the winter on Nova Zembla, but died on the return journey in 1597.

name: Barentszstraat
en: Willem Barentszoon, the famous skipper who, together with Jacob van Heemskerck, tried in 1596 to reach the Indies by way of the Arctic Ocean. He spent the winter on Nova Zembla, but died on the return journey in 1597.

name: Barkasstraat
en: A barkas (launch) was originally the largest boat carried aboard a warship. Today a barkas is a popular, rugged motor boat with an open cockpit.

name: Barkentijnkade
en: A barkentijn (barquentine) is a ship that is a cross between a schooner, a barque and a brig. It is also called a barkschoener or schoenerbark.

name: Barkpad
en: A bark (barque) is a three-masted sailing ship that is square-rigged.

name: Barndesteeg
en: The name is derived from barnen, an archaic form of branden (to burn). The alley was probably wholly or partly destroyed by fire in earlier times. Older spellings of the alley's name include Brandesteeg, Bernendesteeg and Verbemdesteeg.

name: Barnegat
en: Former arm of the sea off the IJ. The name derives from 'barnen', an older form of the verb branden (to burn). This probably refers to the frequent reed fires in the area.

name: Barnevelderstraat
en: The chicken breed developed in and around Barneveld. The street was laid out on the site once occupied by the Sluis company, which produced chicken feed and birdseed.

name: Baron de Coubertinlaan
en: Pierre F. Baron de Coubertin (1863-1937), a Frenchman. He initiated the modern Olympic Games and was their first organiser.

name: Baron G.A. Tindalplein
en: George August Tindal (1839-1921), director and board member of several Amsterdam steamship companies, including the N.V. Stoomvaart Maatschappij 'Nederland'. From 1872 to 1874 he was an alderman of Amsterdam, and he later became chamberlain to William III.

name: Baron G.A. Tindalstraat
en: George August Tindal (1839-1921), director and board member of several Amsterdam steamship companies, including the N.V. Stoomvaart Maatschappij 'Nederland'. From 1872 to 1874 he was an alderman of Amsterdam, and he later became chamberlain to William III.

name: Baron Schimmelpenninck van der Oyeweg
en: Alphert baron Schimmelpenninck van der Oye (1880-1943), for many years chairman of the Nederlands Olympisch Comite. In 1943 he was executed by firing squad by the Germans.

name: Baroniepad
en: The Baronie van Breda, a region between Bergen op Zoom and 's-Hertogenbosch (Noord-Brabant).

name: Baroniestraat
en: The Baronie van Breda, a region between Bergen op Zoom and 's-Hertogenbosch (Noord-Brabant).

name: Baronstraat
en: One of the leaders of the revolt of enslaved people in Suriname. The enslaved people who had escaped, also known as marrons (maroons), waged a guerrilla war against their oppressors. They plundered the plantations and in this way dealt heavy blows to the economy.

name: Bart de Ligtstraat
en: Theologian (1883-1938), a Christian socialist, later an anarchist, and an anti-militarist. From 1910 to 1915 he was a minister of the Nederlandse Hervormde Kerk.

name: Bart Poesiatstraat
en: Amsterdam brewery worker (1831-1898), co-founder of 'Patrimonium' and of the Christelijk Werkliedenverbond.

name: Bart van der Leckplantsoen
en: Painter and designer (1876-1958), known for his figurative style. He worked with geometric shapes and primary colours, and was briefly a member of De Stijl.

name: Bart van Hovestraat
en: Sculptor (1854-1914) who made groups of sculptures for the Sint Nicolaaskerk, the Sint Bernardusgesticht and the Barlaeus Gymnasium.

name: Bartholomeus Diazstraat
en: Portuguese explorer (1450-1500). In 1486 he became the first European to sail around the Cape of Good Hope.

name: Bartholomeus Drijfhoutstraat
en: Seventeenth-century master builder (born 1605) of the school of Jacob van Campen. In 1640 he built the Lakenhal in Leiden, and in 1647 the Oosterkerk in Middelburg.

name: Bartholomeus Ruloffsstraat
en: Conductor (1740-1801), organist of the Westerkerk and director of the orchestras of the Stadsschouwburg and Felix Meritis. He wrote the music for Van Alphen's children's songs.

name: Bartholt Enthesstraat
en: Member of the Verbond der Edelen (Compromise of Nobles) (1540-1580) and vice-admiral of the Sea Beggars under Lumey at the capture of Den Briel. In the same year, on Lumey's orders, he tried to take Amsterdam from the Spanish troops.

name: Basisweg
en: When the harbour in the western port area was laid out, the original plan included a basiskanaal (base canal) into which the large branch docks would open. The road planned along this canal was therefore named Basisweg. The base canal was never dug, but the road was built. Because of the construction of the Hemspoorweg, the Basisweg was shortened in 1978 and its western part was renamed Noordzeeweg.

name: Bastenakenstraat
en: Belgian town in the province of Luxembourg. Bastenaken is the Flemish name for Bastogne.

name: Bastiaan Plooijstraat
en: Bastiaan Plooijst (1890-1967) is best known for his designs for Gereformeerde and Hervormde (Reformed) churches. He built about thirty of them in his lifetime, including the Maranathakerk.

name: Bastingstraat
en: ...the Mosplein. For this neighbourhood, the category chosen was names of Dutch architects who were involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Bataviastraat
en: City on Java, capital of the former Dutch East Indies. The city is now called Jakarta.

name: Batavus Droogstoppelbrug
en: Batavus Droogstoppel is a fictional character in Multatuli's Max Havelaar. He is a coffee broker at Lauriergracht 37. Multatuli portrays him as a 'wretched product of filthy greed and blasphemous sanctimony'.

name: Batjanstraat
en: An island in Indonesia, part of the Moluccas.

name: Batteryparkstraat
en: Waterfront development at the southern tip of Manhattan (New York City). It is a park named after the battery of cannons that Dutch colonists placed there in the 17th century, and it was partly built with the labour of enslaved people. In the 19th century the area was transformed into a public city park, and in the late 20th century it became an example of urban redevelopment.

name: Bauduinlaan
en: Mr D. Bauduin of The Hague became the first dijkgraaf (dike reeve) of the Houtrakpolder in 1876.

name: Bavinkhof
en: A character in the novels of the writer Nescio. Nescio (Latin for 'I do not know') is the pen name of Jan Hendrik Frederik Grönloh (1882-1961). His best-known works include 'De uitvreter' (The Freeloader) and 'Titaantjes' (Little Titans).

name: Baweanstraat
en: An Indonesian island in the Java Sea, north of Surabaya.

name: Becquerelstraat
en: Antonie Henri Becquerel (1852-1908), French physicist. He discovered that uranium salts emit a kind of X-ray. In 1903 he received the Nobel Prize in Physics.

name: Beeckenstein
en: An old eighteenth-century country house near Velsen (Noord-Holland).

name: Beek en Hoff
en: A former farmstead on the Haarlemmerweg, opposite the village of Sloterdijk.

name: Beemdgrasstraat
en: Beemdgras (meadow-grass) is a native plant genus of about five hundred species in the grass family.

name: Beemsterstraat
en: Named after the Beemster polder, a lake northwest of Purmerend that was drained between 1608 and 1612.

name: Beemsterstraatbrug
en: Named after the street beneath it.

name: Beethovenplein
en: Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827), German composer and grand master of instrumental music. His works include 9 symphonies, 32 piano sonatas, 11 overtures and 17 string quartets.

name: Beethovenstraat
en: Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827), German composer and grand master of instrumental music. His works include 9 symphonies, 32 piano sonatas, 11 overtures and 17 string quartets.

name: Begijnensteeg
en: The hof (courtyard), founded in the fourteenth century, was built to house beguines (lay sisters). The Begijnhof, together with the Sint Luciënklooster, was originally surrounded entirely by water. Behind the houses of the Kalverstraat ran a ditch, the Begijnensloot, which led from the Spui, not yet filled in at the time, to the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal. This ditch was neglected, and so what remained of it was filled in in 1865. It was given the name Gedempte Begijnensloot, a name made official by a council decision in 1914.

name: Begoniastraat
en: The plant.

name: Beijerlandstraat
en: The western part of the island of the Hoeksche Waard (Zuid-Holland).

name: Beiraweg
en: An African port city in Mozambique. The street is near the Afrikahaven in the western port area.

name: Beitelkade
en: A carpenter's tool: a beitel is a chisel.

name: Belgiëplein
en: The country (Belgium).

name: Bella Vistastraat
en: Former country house on the Amstel.

name: Bellamydwarsstraat
en: Jacobus Bellamy (1757-1786), poet, originally a baker's assistant. Until 1896, part of the street and the side street belonged to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel, under the names Nieuwe Weteringstraat (Nieuwer-Amstel council decision of 27 April 1888) and Nieuwe Weteringdwarsstraat (Nieuwer-Amstel council decision of 11 June 1891).

name: Bellamyplein
en: Jacobus Bellamy (1757-1786), poet, originally a baker's assistant. Until 1896, part of the street and the side street belonged to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel, under the names Nieuwe Weteringstraat (Nieuwer-Amstel council decision of 27 April 1888) and Nieuwe Weteringdwarsstraat (Nieuwer-Amstel council decision of 11 June 1891).

name: Bellamystraat
en: Jacobus Bellamy (1757-1786), poet, originally a baker's assistant. Until 1896, part of the street and the side street belonged to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel, under the names Nieuwe Weteringstraat (Nieuwer-Amstel council decision of 27 April 1888) and Nieuwe Weteringdwarsstraat (Nieuwer-Amstel council decision of 11 June 1891).

name: Bellefleurhof
en: A nineteenth-century apple variety from Brabant with large, fresh-tasting green-and-red apples.

name: Belmermeer
en: Drained lake south-east of Broek in Waterland, half of which lies in that municipality. Belmermeer means 'connecting lake'. Before 1921 the Amsterdam part belonged to the municipalities of Nieuwendam and Ransdorp, which were abolished that year.

name: Beloegastraat
en: The beluga, also called the white dolphin, can grow to ten to twelve metres long, weigh up to 1400 kilos and live for at least a hundred years. It lives in the Caspian Sea and the Black Sea.

name: Beltbrug
en: Recalls the municipal rubbish dump (vuilnisbelt) that was in use there until 1888.

name: Belvedereweg
en: Former country estate that stood on the west side of the old Schagerlaan. The estate was also known as 'Mijn lust is rust' (My delight is rest).

name: Ben Brilstraat
en: Barend (Ben) Bril (1912-2003), amateur boxer, who at the age of fifteen represented the Netherlands at the 1928 Summer Olympics in the flyweight class (up to 50.8 kg). He won the Dutch title in his weight class eight times.

name: Ben Hope
en: Mountain peak in Scotland, 927 metres high.

name: Ben van Meerendonkstraat
en: Ben van Meerendonk (1913-2008) was a Dutch photojournalist.

name: Ben Viljoenstraat
en: South African Boer commander who repelled an English raid in 1896. He took part in the Second Boer War in 1899. Born in 1868, he died in America (year of death unknown).

name: Ben Websterstraat
en: Benjamin Francis Webster (1909-1973), American jazz tenor saxophonist who emigrated to Europe in 1964. He was known for playing fast, fierce tempos with a raw tone and for creating sensitive ballads.

name: Benit
en: A corrupted spelling of the French port of Binic, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Benjamin Brittenstraat
en: Lord Edward Benjamin Britten (1913-1976), English composer and pianist. He was one of the most important classical composers of the twentieth century. His works include the opera 'Peter Grimes' and the 'War Requiem'.

name: Benkoelenstraat
en: A city on the west coast of the island of Sumatra (Indonesia).

name: Bennebroekstraat
en: A village in Noord-Holland.

name: Benno Stokvisstraat
en: Benno Jules Stokvis (1901-1977), lawyer and politician. He became known for defending Henk Sneevliet in 1933 at his trial following the mutiny on the naval ship De Zeven Provinciën. He was also a writer, a literary critic and an advocate of full rights for homosexuals. An anti-fascist, he became a fierce critic of Stalinism after the war.

name: Bentinckstraat
en: Barend Hendrik baron Bentinck tot Buckhorst (1753-1830), governor of Overijssel. He was forced to leave the country because of his sympathy for stadholder Willem V. He played an important role in the founding of the Kingdom in 1813.

name: Benzolweg
en: Benzol is a mixture of hydrocarbons, a petroleum derivative.

name: Bep Bakhuysstraat
en: Elisa Hendrik Bakhuys (1909-1982), footballer. In the 1930s he played a leading role in the successes of the Dutch national team.

name: Berberisstraat
en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

name: Berceusestraat
en: Berceuse is French for 'lullaby' or 'cradle song'. It is also the title of a poem by the Flemish modernist Paul van Ostaijen (1896-1928).

name: Berchvliet
en: A corrupted spelling of the French port of Barfleur, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Bercylaan
en: A district along the Seine in south-east Paris, where many wine warehouses once stood along the river. Large-scale renovation took place there at the end of the twentieth century.

name: Berend Boeijingastraat
en: Urban planner and architect (1886-1969) who worked for, among others, the Gemeentelijke Woningdienst (Municipal Housing Department). He designed the former laboratory of the Vrije Universiteit and built Disteldorp, Tuindorp Oostzaan and Tuindorp Nieuwendam.

name: Berensluis
en: This fixed bridge is named after the Berenstraat, on which it lies. In the seventeenth century, the tanneries and the hide trade were located in the adjacent part of what is now the Jordaan.

name: Berenstraat
en: In the seventeenth century, the tanneries and the hide trade were located in the adjacent part of what is now the Jordaan. This trade included bearskins.

name: Bergmolen
en: A berg- or beltmolen (mound mill) is named after the mound that is raised around the mill once it has been built, as an alternative to a stage (stelling). A bergmolen is usually a corn mill.

name: Bergstraat
en: The street already existed under this name before it came to lie within the city rampart during the expansion of 1593. It is known that from 1633 a house stood here with a gable stone depicting Mount Sinai. Whether such a building also existed before then, and whether it gave the street its name, is not known.

name: Beringenstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Beringhaven
en: The Beringstraat (Bering Strait), a strait between Asia and America. It was discovered in 1741 and named after the Dane Vitus Bering.

name: Berkelstraat
en: The small river that flows into the IJssel near Zutphen.

name: Berkhouthof
en: A village in Noord-Holland (near Hoorn).

name: Berlaarstraat
en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

name: Berlagebrug
en: Hendrik Petrus Berlage (1856-1934), architect. His buildings include the Koopmansbeurs on the Damrak. He designed the southern expansion plan (uitbreidingsplan-Zuid) and the Mercatorplein and its surroundings. His last creation was the Berlagebrug (1932). In 1966 Hildo Krop made a statue of him, which was placed on the Victorieplein.

name: Berlagehof
en: Hendrik Petrus Berlage (1856-1934), architect. His buildings include the Koopmansbeurs on the Damrak. He designed the southern expansion plan (uitbreidingsplan-Zuid) and the Mercatorplein and its surroundings. His last creation was the Berlagebrug (1932). In 1966 Hildo Krop made a statue of him, which was placed on the Victorieplein.

name: Bernard Kochstraat
en: Musician (1791-1858) and conductor of the Italian Opera in Amsterdam. His compositions include the opera 'Moeder de Gans' (Mother Goose).

name: Bernard Loderstraat
en: Jurist (1849-1935), a leading expert on international law and president of the Permanent Court of International Justice.

name: Bernard Shawsingel
en: George Bernard Shaw (1856-1950), British (Irish) playwright and novelist whose works include 'Pygmalion'.

name: Bernard Zweerskade
