en: Composer and choral conductor (1854-1924). He was a senior teacher at the Amsterdams Conservatorium. For his songs and choral works he used only Dutch texts, by poets such as Boutens and Verweij.

name: Bernissestraat
en: In the Middle Ages a broad stretch of water, and today still a small storage basin (boezemwater) between Voorne and Putten (Zuid-Holland).

name: Bert Haanstrakade
en: Film director (1916-1997) who became famous for films such as 'Fanfare', 'Zoo', 'Alleman' and 'Bij de beesten af', in which he took a witty look at Dutch society. He received 78 awards for his films and documentaries, including an Oscar in 1958 for his documentary 'Glas' (Glass).

name: Berta de Vriesbrug
en: Luberta de Hondt de Vries, known as Berta de Vries (Amsterdam, 23 January 1885 – Amsterdam, 19 April 1959), was active in the revolutionary socialist women's movement, the Communistische Partij in Nederland and the Amsterdams Speeltuinverbond.

name: Bertelmanplein
en: Jan Georg Bertelman (1782-1854), composer of cantatas and a requiem.

name: Bertelmanstraat
en: Jan Georg Bertelman (1782-1854), composer of cantatas and a requiem.

name: Bertha von Suttnerstraat
en: Austrian writer (1848-1914). In 1891 she founded the Österreichische Gesellschaft der Friedensfreunde (known since 1964 as the Suttner-Gesellschaft). Her book 'Die Waffen nieder' (Lay Down Your Arms) became world-famous for its pacifist message and moving style. She inspired Alfred Nobel to establish the Nobel Prizes. In 1905 she received the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Berthelotstraat
en: Pierre Eugène Marcellin Berthelot (Paris, 29 October 1827 – Paris, 18 March 1907) was a French chemist and politician. In his chemical work he discovered routes for synthesising many hydrocarbons, fats and sugars, and in doing so proved that organic chemical compounds can be prepared using the same chemical techniques as inorganic compounds.

name: Berthold Brechtstraat
en: Eugen Berthold Friedrich Brecht (1898-1956), also known as Bertolt Brecht; there is disagreement about the correct spelling. German playwright and prose writer. He was one of the so-called exile writers. In 1933 he left National Socialist Germany and, by way of France, reached the United States of America. In 1947 he returned to his native country.

name: Bertrand Russellstraat
en: Bertrand Arthur William Russell (1872-1970), British philosopher and writer on public affairs. His work as a writer, lecturer, speaker and activist covered four distinct areas: the philosophy of mathematics and logic, the theory of knowledge, ethics and education, and finally pacifism. In 1950 he received the Nobel Prize in Literature.

name: Bertus van Grouwstraat
en: Gijsbertus Ludovicus van Grouw (1907-1945), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, who died in Neuengamme concentration camp.

name: Berzeliusstraat
en: Johannes Jacob Berzelius (1779-1848), Swedish chemist. Founder of modern analysis.

name: Bessemerstraat
en: Henry Bessemer (1813-1898), English engineer. He invented a method for rolling glass and one for producing liquid steel. The street was taken over from the former municipality of Watergraafsmeer, where it was called Ringlaan.

name: Bessenpad
en: The fruit: bessen are currants or berries.

name: Bestevâerstraat
en: An honorary name given by sailors to Maarten Harpertsz. Tromp, and later to Michiel Adriaansz. de Ruyter. It literally means 'best father'. The street was originally named Wilhelminastraat by the municipality of Sloten (Sloten council decision of 28 June 1911).

name: Bet van Beerenbrug
en: Elizabeth Maria van Beeren (1902-1967) ran the nearby café 't Mandje at Zeedijk 63. She was called the Queen of the Zeedijk. She was openly lesbian, and in the 1950s her café became a refuge for homosexuals, making her a pioneer in their emancipation.

name: Betelgeuzestraat
en: A star in the constellation Orion.

name: Bethaniëndwarsstraat
en: Named after the convent of St. Maria Magdalena in Bethaniën (St Mary Magdalene in Bethany), which stood here from around 1450 to 1589. The street was laid out in 1506 along the convent's southern wall.

name: Bethaniënstraat
en: Named after the convent of St. Maria Magdalena in Bethaniën (St Mary Magdalene in Bethany), which stood here from around 1450 to 1589. The street was laid out in 1506 along the convent's southern wall.

name: Betuwestraat
en: The region in Gelderland between the Rijn (Rhine) and the Waal.

name: Beudekerbrug
en: Frans Beudeker (1815-1897) was director of the Stads-bestedelingenhuis, a municipal home for people who could not look after themselves. In the nineteenth century, 'Hij gaat naar Beudeker' (he's going to Beudeker) was an expression for someone who had become dependent on care. The Stads-bestedelingenhuis was later converted into the Paleis van Justitie, which stands right next to this bridge.

name: Beukenplein
en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

name: Beukenweg
en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

name: Beulingsloot
en: Named after one of the residents, Gerrit Jansz Beulinck, who lived here around 1660. He may have made this known with a hanging sign. In the sixteenth century the names Leertouwersstraat and Leertouwerssloot, and also Huidevettersstraat and Huidevetterssloot, occur here (leertouwers and huidevetters were tanners).

name: Beulingstraat
en: Named after one of the residents, Gerrit Jansz Beulinck, who lived here around 1660. He may have made this known with a hanging sign. name: Beursplein
en: Named after Berlage's Koopmansbeurs (commodity exchange), built in 1903. The street and square came into being after part of the Damrak was filled in. The name Beurspassage arose after the former Baafjessteeg was built over by new construction in 1903.

name: Beursstraat
en: Named after Berlage's Koopmansbeurs (commodity exchange), built in 1903. The street and square came into being after part of the Damrak was filled in. The name Beurspassage arose after the former Baafjessteeg was built over by new construction in 1903.

name: Beverenstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of West-Vlaanderen (West Flanders).

name: Beverwijkstraat
en: A town in Noord-Holland, at the foot of the dune region.

name: Beysterveld
en: The castle of Oud Beysterveld near Oirschot (Noord-Brabant). It was built in 1775 on the foundations of a seventeenth-century castle and was later used as a monastery.

name: Bezaanjachtplein
en: A type of sailing ship, usually with three masts. The rearmost mast is called the bezaanmast (mizzen mast), and it carries a gaff sail.

name: Bickersgracht
en: These streets are on the Bickerseiland. This island was originally owned by Dr Johan Bicker (1591-1653), a shipbuilder and merchant, and a schepen (magistrate) and burgomaster of Amsterdam, who bought it in 1631. name: Bickerswerf
en: These streets are on the Bickerseiland. This island was originally owned by Dr Johan Bicker (1591-1653), a shipbuilder and merchant, and a schepen (magistrate) and burgomaster of Amsterdam, who bought it in 1631. The streets later laid out on the island automatically took the name of its founder.

name: Bierens de Haanstraat
en: Johannes D. Bierens de Haan (1866-1943), philosopher. Among other works, he wrote a study of Spinoza.

name: Biesboschstraat
en: The area of islands, peat flats and creeks between the Bergsche Maas and the Merwede, now partly diked. Before the Delta-werken (Delta Works) were built, it was subject to the tides.

name: Bieslookpad
en: Bieslook is chives, a plant of the genus Allium that is used as a herb.

name: Bijdorpstraat
en: The name is based on former country estates along the Amstel and in the Watergraafsmeer.

name: Bijleveldschesluis
en: This name appears in old archives; its exact meaning is unknown.

name: Bijlmerdreef
en: Named after the polder created when the Bijlmermeer was drained in 1626. The polder became an independent municipality in 1817 and was merged with Weesperkarspel in 1846. When the municipality of Weesperkarspel was abolished in 1966, part of it was added to Amsterdam.

name: Bijlmerplein
en: Named after the polder created when the Bijlmermeer was drained in 1626. The polder became an independent municipality in 1817 and was merged with Weesperkarspel in 1846. When the municipality of Weesperkarspel was abolished in 1966, part of it was added to Amsterdam.

name: Bijlmerpleinpad
en: Named after the square it runs across.

name: Bijlmerringsloot
en: Named after the polder created when the Bijlmermeer was drained in 1626. The polder became an independent municipality in 1817 and was merged with Weesperkarspel in 1846. When the municipality of Weesperkarspel was abolished in 1966, part of it was added to Amsterdam.

name: Bijltjespad
en: De Bijltjes (the Little Axes) was the name given to the people of Kattenburg (shipwrights) in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. They are known for the fight over the Kattenburgerbrug between the Patriots and the Bijltjes, who supported the House of Orange.

name: Bilderdijkgracht
en: Willem Bilderdijk (1756-1831), poet and historian. Bilderdijk went against the complacent spirit of his time, which made him a highly controversial figure. The name Bilderdijkstraat originally applied as far as the Vondelstraat. That section, from the Jacob van Lennepkade onwards, is now called Eerste Constantijn Huygensstraat (council decision of 21 March 1894). The Bilderdijkpark (park and street) was laid out on the site of the cemetery of the former Roman Catholic church 'De Liefde'.

name: Billie Holidaystraat
en: Eleanora Gough McKay (1915-1959), stage name Billie Holiday, American singer. She made her debut in 1929 and her first recording in 1933. She was known for her timbre and relaxed phrasing.

name: Billitonstraat
en: Island in Indonesia between Sumatra and Kalimantan (Borneo). Important for its tin mining.

name: Binairstraat
en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

name: Binnen Bantammerstraat
en: The name recalls the sixteenth century, when the Dutch brought goods from Bantam (Dutch East Indies) to Amsterdam. In 1597 Houtman's ships were unloaded in the Waal. The Binnen Bantammerstraat was originally called Bantammerstraat. As early as around 1600 the bridge over the Geldersekade was called the Bantamsbrug. The houses on the street were then described as lying outside the Bantamspoort. In 1644 the Nieuwe Waalseiland was created. The Bantammerstraat was then given the prefix Binnen (inner), and its extension across the Oude Waal became the Buiten Bantammerstraat.

name: Binnen Brouwersstraat
en: Named after the many breweries found in this neighbourhood in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. The prefixes Binnen (inner) and Buiten (outer) refer to the location in relation to the Haarlemmerdijk.

name: Binnen Dommersstraat
en: The owner of the land on which the street was laid out was IJsbrand Jansz. Dommer. He was a ropemaker and a member of the council, and in 1579 he was appointed schepen (magistrate) of the city. Binnen (inner) and Buiten (outer) refer to the location, inside and outside the Haarlemmerdijk.

name: Binnen Oranjestraat
en: The origin of the name is uncertain. It may refer to the house 'de Prins van Oranje', which once stood nearby on the Haarlemmerdijk. The division into Binnen (inner) and Buiten (outer) Oranjestraat refers to the location: inside and outside the dike (the Haarlemmerdijk).

name: Binnen Vissersstraat
en: The name recalls the many fishermen who lived here, originally outside the city gate. The first of the two streets lay inside the dike; the second lay on the IJ side, and so outside the dike.

name: Binnen Wieringerstraat
en: The street is named after Albert Pietersz van Wieringen. According to old documents from 1610 and 1624, he owned a house and several plots of land here. At that time the street was already referred to as Wieringerstraat. The division into two parts, inside and outside the Haarlemmerdijk, came into use in the eighteenth century.

name: Binnendraaierij
en: This and other streets were laid out on the grounds of the former Amsterdamse Droogdok Maatschappij (ADM, Amsterdam Dry Dock Company). As a reminder of the site's former use, the streets were named after its various workshops (a draaierij is a turnery, or lathe workshop). Because a small square splits the street into two parts, there is a Binnendraaierij (inner) and a Buitendraaierij (outer).

name: Binnenhofstraat
en: The name describes the location: the inner courtyard (binnenhof) within a block of streets. The 'Binnenhof', around which the Binnenhofstraat runs, is no longer a public road. This name was abolished after the housing complex was rebuilt, by council decision of 19 October 1949.

name: Binnenkadijk
en: When a great deal of land had built up through silting outside the old sea dike (St. Antoniesdijk), a summer dike, or quay dike (kadijk), was built. It was originally called the new sea dike, but that name later fell out of use. When this new dike was raised further, people spoke of the Laagte (low part) and the Hoogte (high part) of the Kadijk. Until 1943 the Tussen Kadijken was called Korte Kerkstraat. This is because it lies in line with the Plantage Kerklaan, although it has never been connected to it.

name: Binnenkant
en: The Waalseiland, which was created in 1644 by filling in land (see under Waal), was given the name Binnenkant (inner side) on the city side and Buitenkant (outer side) on the IJ side. The latter name was changed to Prins Hendrikkade in 1879.

name: Binnenpolderringdijk Noord
en: Refers to the ring dike of the Osdorper Binnenpolder.

name: Binnenvaart
en: Shipping on inland waters (binnenvaart).

name: Binnenzagerij
en: This street and others were laid out on the grounds of the former Amsterdamse Droogdok Maatschappij (ADM). As a reminder of the site's former use, the streets were named after the various workshops. Because a small square splits the street into two parts, there is a Binnenzagerij (inner sawmill) and a Buitenzagerij (outer sawmill).

name: Biothof
en: Jean-Baptiste Biot (1774-1862), French physicist and astronomer. In 1804 he made the first scientific balloon flight. Among other things, he worked on electromagnetism.

name: Bitterzoetstraat
en: Bitterzoet (bittersweet), a plant belonging to the nightshade family.

name: Blancefloorstraat
en: A character from the medieval chivalric romance 'Floris ende Blancefloor'.

name: Blankenbergestraat
en: A Belgian coastal town in the province of West Flanders (West-Vlaanderen).

name: Blankenstraat
en: Jan Blanken (1755-1838), hydraulic engineer and builder of fortifications. The Noordhollandsch Kanaal was dug to his design between 1818 and 1824.

name: Blasiusstraat
en: Gerardus Blasius (1625-1693), professor of medicine in Amsterdam. The street was originally named Vierde Boerhaavestraat (council decision of 15 November 1882).

name: Blauwbrug
en: The name of this fixed bridge recalls an earlier version of it, which after the Alteration of Amsterdam in 1578 was painted in the blue of Nassau. The present bridge dates from 1884. Its architects, B. de Greef and W. Springer, took their inspiration from a bridge over the Seine. Another name for this bridge was Sophiabrug, but through all the changes the name Blauwbrug was kept. That other name for the Blauwbrug never caught on, just as Sophiaplein never did for the Muntplein. Sophia of Württemberg (1817-1877) was the first wife of King Willem III, who opened this renewed bridge in 1839.

name: Blauwburgwal
en: Probably named after the Blauwe Brug (blue bridge). The canal was dug at the end of the sixteenth century. The present name occurs from 1614. Before that it was called the canal of the Blauwe brugge outside the Jan Roonpoort, or the cross canal (dwarse burgwal) by the Blauwe brugge. Most bridges at that time were painted red.

name: Blauwdasstraat
en: The songbird. A colourful bird the size of a tit, often kept in aviaries. It occurs in Suriname, Guyana, Venezuela and northern Brazil.

name: Blauwezandbrug
en: Tuindorp Buiksloot used to be called the Blauwe Zand (blue sand) because of the bluish colour of the pumped-up sand on which the village was built.

name: Blauwhoedenveem
en: A veem is a company that stores goods in its warehouses and delivers them from there. Each veem had its own emblem, after which it was named. These could be hats of different colours and shapes (among them Blauwhoeden, blue hats, and Klapmutsen). They also took their names from where their workmen came from (among them the Vriesseveem and the Zeeuwse Veem).

name: Blauwpijpstraat
en: Named after the ships of the Nederlandse Stoomvaartmaatschappij Oceaan NV, formerly based on the Borneokade, which were called blauwpijpen (blue funnels) because of the blue band on their funnels.

name: Blauwvoetstraat
en: A poem by the Flemish poet Albrecht Rodenbach. (The Blauwvoeterij was a Flemish student movement of around 1875, a protest against the Frenchification of the colleges.)

name: Blazerpad
en: A small fishing vessel, similar to a botter.

name: Bleijenbeek
en: A seventeenth-century castle near the village of Afferden (Limburg), completely burnt out in 1944 and now a ruin.

name: Bloedstraat
en: Before the street was laid out, the blood chamber (bloedkamer) of the Franciscan friary stood here. This was the operating room, but it may also have served as a torture chamber. According to the historian Melchior Fokkens (1661), Alva held his 'Council of Blood' here.

name: Bloemendalergouw
en: Bloemendaal was one of the quarters of the former Banne Ransdorp. The gouw (the Waterland name for a village road) ran in the eighteenth century from Ransdorp to the Zeedijk. Its last stretch was washed away by the water of the Kinselmeer in the following centuries. The second part of the present road (towards Holysloot) was originally called Kanaalweg.

name: Bloemgracht
en: Many streets and canals in the Jordaan are named after flowers. In this expansion of 1612, the Bloemgracht is probably the oldest canal. The canal ran to the Bolwerk de Bloem (later called Rijkeroord), after which it is named. From 1614 to 1878 the windmill 'De Blom' stood on the bastion; it was then moved to the Haarlemmerweg near the Nieuwpoortkade.

name: Bloemstraat
en: Many streets and canals in the Jordaan are named after flowers. In this expansion of 1612, the Bloemgracht is probably the oldest canal. The canal ran to the Bolwerk de Bloem (later called Rijkeroord), after which it is named. From 1614 to 1878 the windmill 'De Blom' stood on the bastion; it was then moved to the Haarlemmerweg near the Nieuwpoortkade.

name: Blokkerstraat
en: The North Holland villages of Wester- and Oosterblokker, near Hoorn.

name: Blokmakerstraat
en: An occupational name from shipbuilding: a blokmaker (block maker). The name recalls the many shipyards that stood along the Grote Bickersstraat in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

name: Blomwijckerpad
en: A road in old Sloten that disappeared as the city expanded.

name: Bloys van Treslongstraat
en: Willem Bloys van Treslong (1529-1594), admiral of Holland and a leader of the Sea Beggars at the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

name: Blusséstraat
en: Jan Jacob Blussé (1870-1931), a well-known single sculler. He did a great deal for rowing in the Netherlands. He was chairman of the rowing club 'De Hoop' from 1898 to 1931.

name: Boas en Judelshof
en: Israël Boas (1811-1886) and Nathan Judels (1815-1903), both cabaret performers. They were the directors of the 'Salon des Variëtés' in the Amstelstraat.

name: Bob Haarmslaan
en: Bob Haarms was a former AFC Ajax player and later worked for many years as a (rehabilitation) trainer. He was much loved by the club and its supporters.

name: Bocholtstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Bodenseehof
en: The lake known as the Bodensee (Lake Constance), on the border between Germany and Switzerland.

name: Boeckenburg
en: The later name of Boechorst castle, which stood in the Boekhorstpolder near Voorhout (South Holland).

name: Boeierspad
en: A boeier is a flat-bottomed sailing yacht.

name: Boeierstraat
en: A boeier is a boat, a small flat-bottomed vessel, used mainly by the well-to-do middle classes for comfortable business journeys.

name: Boeninlaan
en: Ivan Alexejewitsj Boenin (Ivan Bunin, 1870-1953), a Russian writer of the early twentieth century. He lived in France from the time of the Russian Revolution. He received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1933.

name: Boerenwetering
en: The name of the watercourse that originally ran from the Kalfjeslaan to what is now the Koningsplein. It was formerly also called the Oude Wetering, as opposed to the Nieuwe Wetering (Kostverlorenvaart). The Weteringbuurt and the Weteringschans take their names from this wetering (drainage canal).

name: Boerenweteringbrug
en: The name of the watercourse that originally ran from the Kalfjeslaan to what is now the Koningsplein. It was formerly also called the Oude Wetering, as opposed to the Nieuwe Wetering (Kostverlorenvaart). The Weteringbuurt and the Weteringschans take their names from this wetering (drainage canal).

name: Boerenweteringpad
en: The name of the watercourse that originally ran from the Kalfjeslaan to what is now the Koningsplein. It was formerly also called the Oude Wetering, as opposed to the Nieuwe Wetering (Kostverlorenvaart). The Weteringbuurt and the Weteringschans take their names from this wetering (drainage canal).

name: Boerhaaveplein
en: Hermannus Boerhaave (1668-1738), professor of medicine at Leiden. He enjoyed international fame. The street name Boerhaavestraat (First to Fourth) has been changed several times. It was set as Boerhaavestraat on 15 November 1876 and changed to Eerste Boerhaavestraat on 15 November 1882. This change was reversed on 10 December 1884. On 13 October 1897 the street was extended under the same name, and finally, on 19 February 1908, it was split into the present Eerste and Tweede Boerhaavestraat. The Tweede, Derde and Vierde Boerhaavestraat, named in 1882, were replaced by the names Deymanstraat, Ruyschstraat and Blasiusstraat.

name: Boeroestraat
en: An island in Indonesia, one of the Ambon Islands (Moluccas).

name: Boetonstraat
en: An island in Indonesia, south of Sulawesi (Celebes).

name: Bogortuin
en: The Indonesian city of Bogor, formerly Buitenzorg, lies sixty kilometres south of Jakarta and is famous above all for its botanical garden. The garden, laid out in 1817, contains well over a thousand species of tropical plants from all over the world.

name: Bok de Korverweg
en: Johannes Marius de Korver (1883-1957), footballer. He was many times centre-half and captain of the Dutch national team, including in the match at Houtrust (1913) in which the Netherlands beat England for the first time.

name: Bokkinghangen
en: A bokkinghang is a shed where herring is hung up to be smoked. Smoked herring is called bokking (bloater). A bylaw of 1652 designated this area near the Barentszplein for these smokehouses.

name: Bolensteinpad
en: The name Nigtevechtpad is being changed to Bolensteinpad because Weesp already has a street called Nigtevechtsepad, which could cause confusion. The name Bolenstein fits the theme of 'castles and country houses along the Vecht'. The name was submitted by a resident. Bolenstein is a knightly manor in Maarssen, built in the 14th century.

name: Bolestein
en: A castle-like house on the Vecht near Maarssen (Utrecht), originally fourteenth-century and substantially rebuilt in the seventeenth and nineteenth centuries.

name: Bolkstraat
en: Louis Bolk (1866-1930), professor of anatomy in Amsterdam. He was known for his work on the theory of evolution.

name: Bolstoen
en: The English port of Boston, in a spelling found on Dutch sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Bombraak
en: Named after a small wiel behind the Oostzanerdijk, level with Buitendijk. A wiel is a lake that formed after a dike breach or was left behind after a flood. Braak is a North Holland word for wiel.

name: Bonaireplein
en: An island belonging to the Netherlands Antilles.

name: Bonairestraat
en: An island belonging to the Netherlands Antilles.

name: Bongart
en: A sixteenth-century castle near Bocholtz (Limburg). Today, two side wings and a round corner tower still remain.

name: Bongerdbrug
en: Bongerd is another word for 'boomgaard' (orchard). Bongerd is also the name of the neighbourhood where the bridge is located.

name: Bongerdkade
en: Bongerd is another word for 'boomgaard' (orchard). De Bongerd is also the name of the neighbourhood in which the quay is located.

name: Bonhoeffersingel
en: Dietrich Bonhoeffer (1906-1945), German theologian and writer. As a minister, he openly expressed his aversion to the National Socialist regime, and from 1940 he took an active part in the resistance. In 1943 he was taken prisoner. From prison he wrote his letters, which later became world-famous. He was put to death shortly before the end of the war.

name: Boniplein
en: An area on the south-western peninsula of Sulawesi (Indonesia).

name: Bonistraat
en: An area on the south-western peninsula of Sulawesi (Indonesia).

name: Bonnefantenstraat
en: The Bonnefantenmuseum in Maastricht, the provincial museum of Limburg for fine art and archaeology. The collection consists of old archaeological finds, medieval sculpture, early Italian painting, painting from the Southern Netherlands, and a department of contemporary art. In 1995 the new museum building, designed by the Italian architect Aldo Rossi, was opened.

name: Bontekoestraat
en: Willem IJsbrantsz Bontekoe (1587-1618), seafarer, known for his accounts of his voyages.

name: Boomgaardlaan
en: A street on the former allotment garden complex De Bongerd. The word bongerd means orchard. The streets in the neighbourhood are named after types of fruit.

name: Boomklokstraat
en: Until 1863 the city was separated from the IJ by a long row of piles. This palisade had a number of openings, known as 'bomen' (booms), to let ships through. The boomklok (boom bell) was rung whenever the 'bomen' were opened and closed. One of these openings was near the spot where the Boomklokstraat now lies.

name: Boomsteeg
en: The alley owes its name to the former corner house on the Zeedijk, which was then called 'In de lyndeboom' (In the lime tree).

name: Boomstraat
en: In this part of the Jordaan, streets are named after flowers, shrubs and trees. In the seventeenth century, the street was also called Lindeboomstraat.

name: Boorderstraat
en: A metalworker: someone who works with a metal drill. The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

name: Boorstraat
en: The tool (a drill).

name: Bootstraat
en: Recalls the former seventeenth-century shipyard 'De Boot'.

name: Borgerstraat
en: Elias Anne Borger (1784-1820), professor at Leiden of theology and of classical history and literature. Poet and pulpit orator.

name: Borggraaf
en: A miniature castle near Lottum/Grubbenvorst (Limburg), built in the sixteenth century.

name: Borgloonstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Boris Pasternakstraat
en: Boris Leonidovich Pasternak (1890-1960), Russian poet and prose writer. His best-known work is 'Doctor Zhivago'.

name: Borneokade
en: The largest island of Indonesia. Borneo belongs to the Republic of Indonesia, except for its north-western part, which belongs to Malaysia. It is now called Kalimantan.

name: Borneolaan
en: The largest island of Indonesia. Borneo belongs to the Republic of Indonesia, except for its north-western part, which belongs to Malaysia. It is now called Kalimantan.

name: Borneostraat
en: The largest island of Indonesia. Borneo belongs to the Republic of Indonesia, except for its north-western part, which belongs to Malaysia. It is now called Kalimantan.

name: Bornhout
en: The English port of Burnham (near Bristol), in a spelling found on Dutch sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Borrendammehof
en: Land near Zierikzee (Zeeland) drowned in the sixteenth century.

name: Borssenburgplein
en: A former country house on the Amsteldijk, demolished in 1886. Around 1583 it was the country retreat of Jacob Frans Oetgens, who was married to Lysbeth Bors, after whom he named the house.

name: Borssenburgstraat
en: A former country house on the Amsteldijk, demolished in 1886. Around 1583 it was the country retreat of Jacob Frans Oetgens, who was married to Lysbeth Bors, after whom he named the house.

name: Bos en Lommerplantsoen
en: Named after a farmstead on the former Sloterdijkermeerweg (no. 60), originally eighteenth-century, rebuilt in 1886 and demolished in 1940. The oldest part of the road was originally called Joos Banckersstraat (council decisions of 26 July 1922 and 27 April 1933). Before the GAK building was built, the Adindastraat and the Saidjastraat lay where the Bos en Lommerplantsoen is now (council decision of 20 April 1939).

name: Bos en Lommerplein
en: Named after a farmstead on the former Sloterdijkermeerweg (no. 60), originally eighteenth-century, rebuilt in 1886 and demolished in 1940. The oldest part of the road was originally called Joos Banckersstraat (council decisions of 26 July 1922 and 27 April 1933). Before the GAK building was built, the Adindastraat and the Saidjastraat lay where the Bos en Lommerplantsoen is now (council decision of 20 April 1939).

name: Bos en Lommerweg
en: Named after a farmstead on the former Sloterdijkermeerweg (no. 60), originally eighteenth-century, rebuilt in 1886 and demolished in 1940. The oldest part of the road was originally called Joos Banckersstraat (council decisions of 26 July 1922 and 27 April 1933). Before the GAK building was built, the Adindastraat and the Saidjastraat lay where the Bos en Lommerplantsoen is now (council decision of 20 April 1939).

name: Bosboom Toussaintstraat
en: Anna Louisa Geertruide Toussaint (1812-1886), who in 1851 married the painter Jan Bosboom. She wrote a great many novels, most of them historical. The street was named in tribute to her during her lifetime, an exception, then and now, to the rule that living people are not honoured with street names.

name: Bosbraakhof
en: A historical name from Rijnland, to which the Sloter polders belong (map of Rijnland from 1614). Braak refers to a dike breach and means the same as breek or wiel (a pool formed after a dike breach).

name: Bosch van Drakesteinpad
en: Jonkheer Gérard Dagobert Henri Bosch van Drakestein (1887-1972), racing cyclist. He won seventeen national titles and two Olympic medals (in 1924 and 1928).

name: Bosplaat
en: The eastern part of Terschelling. A nature reserve of dunes, beaches and tidal creeks.

name: Bosporushaven
en: A strait in Turkey, part of the connection between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean, which separates Europe from Asia.

name: Bosrankstraat
en: A perennial climber of the buttercup family (traveller's joy). It grows on chalky soil in woods and scrub.

name: Boterbloemstraat
en: A plant genus of the buttercup family with about four hundred species, mostly with yellow or white flowers.

name: Boterdiepstraat
en: A canal in the province of Groningen.

name: Boterkersstraat
en: A yellow to pale pink cherry with a distinctive taste, a nineteenth-century variety from England.

name: Bottelarijstraat
en: Refers to the wine merchant Roders, which was on the Cruquius site from 1965 to 2010. Wine arrived by ship and was stored in five silos. Once the import duties were paid, the wine was bottled and sold. This came to an end when the rules were tightened and wine had to be bottled in its country of origin.

name: Botterstraat
en: A fishing vessel with a bun, a well in which the catch is kept alive.

name: Botteskerksingel
en: A village south of the Merwede drowned in the St Elizabeth's flood of 1421.

name: Botticellistraat
en: Sandro Botticelli (1447-1510), Italian painter of allegorical figure pieces and portraits.

name: Boulevardpad
en: With the name Boulevard, the neighbourhood that proposed it was thinking of the Eilandenboulevard, a local name for the Kattenburgergracht, Wittenburgergracht and Oostenburgergracht, which were widened and rebuilt into a broad main road around 1960.

name: Boutenburg
en: A former farmstead on the Haarlemmerweg, level with the Vredenhofweg.

name: Boutensstraat
en: Pieter Cornelis Boutens (1870-1943), poet. A teacher of classical languages, he also translated ancient Greek authors.

name: Bouvigne
en: A castle near Ginneken (Noord-Brabant), owned by the House of Orange from 1614 to 1775. During the siege of Breda (1637) it was the headquarters of Frederik Hendrik.

name: Bouwen Ewoutszstraat
en: A Sea Beggar (geuzen) captain in the Eighty Years' War. In 1574 he forced the Spanish to surrender the city of Middelburg.

name: Bovenover
en: In this building two little streets run one above the other: one on the ground floor, along the bottom of the façade, and the other on the third floor, which is why it was named Bovenover (over the top).

name: Boy Edgarbrug
en: George Willem Fred (Boy) Edgar (1915-1980), composer and arranger of light entertainment music, and a doctor by training. His compositions added a great deal to the repertoire of light music.

name: Boy Edgarstraat
en: George Willem Fred (Boy) Edgar (1915-1980), composer and arranger of light entertainment music, and a doctor by training. His compositions added a great deal to the repertoire of light music.

name: Boylestraat
en: Robert Boyle (1627-1691), English physicist. Boyle's law: at constant temperature, the volume of a gas is inversely proportional to the pressure on it.

name: Boymansweg
en: The Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen in Rotterdam. Frans Jacob Otto Boijmans (1767-1847), a judge in Utrecht, left his art collection to the city of Rotterdam. The Museum Boijmans was founded in 1849. The addition Van Beuningen dates from 1958, when the collection was enlarged with that of the Rotterdam collector and patron D.G. van Beuningen (1877-1955).

name: Braak en Bosch
en: A former farmstead on the Haarlemmerweg, demolished to build the garden suburb of Geuzenveld.

name: Brachthuijzerstraat
en: Daniël Brachthuijzer (1779-1832), organist of the Nieuwe Kerk and carillonneur of the Munttoren. An interpreter of Bach and Handel.

name: Braeburnstraat
en: An apple variety from New Zealand with firm fruit, probably a cross between Granny Smith and Lady Hamilton.

name: Brahmsstraat
en: Johannes Brahms (1833-1897), German composer and a grand master of chamber music. Among his works are four symphonies, a violin concerto, two piano concertos and some three hundred songs.

name: Bramzeil
en: One of the sails of a ship (the topgallant sail).

name: Bramzeilhof
en: One of the sails of a ship (the topgallant sail).

name: Brand Dirk Ochsepark
en: Brand Dirk Ochse (1892-1958), director of the Haarlem film company Polygoon, which became famous for its cinema newsreel.

name: Brandewijnsteeg
en: The alley ran behind the brewery 'Den Witten Haen', which used to stand on the Geldersekade. That is probably where the name (brandy alley) comes from.

name: Brandslangstraat
en: Refers to a company, formerly based here, that made firefighting equipment (a brandslang is a fire hose).

name: Brandts Buysstraat
en: Jan Willem Frans Brandts Buys (1868-1939), musician, who settled in Austria in 1893. He composed operas, piano concertos and orchestral music.

name: Brandweerbrug
en: Named after the fire station next to it.

name: Brantasgracht
en: A river in Indonesia, in East Java, 257 km long.

name: Brede Kerkepad
en: The Kerkepad is named after its position and purpose: the path from the dike village of Nieuwendam to the village church.

name: Brede Vogelstraat
en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

name: Brederodestraat
en: Gerbrand A. Bredero (1585-1618), poet and playwright. His works include 'De Spaanse Brabander'.

name: Bredeweg
en: Named after its width compared with the streets around it.

name: Brediusstraat
en: Willem Elias Bredius (1860-1930), a pioneer of swimming as a sport in the Netherlands. Chairman of the Dutch Swimming Federation from 1900 to 1929.

name: Breedveld
en: These names were given for the meaning of the word (broad field), as a counterpart to Het Hoogt and Het Laagt.

name: Breezandpad
en: A village in Noord-Holland, in the municipality of Anna Paulowna.

name: Breitnerstraat
en: George Hendrik Breitner (1857-1923), impressionist painter, above all of Amsterdam cityscapes. The street was first named Dijsselhofstraat (council decision of 22 April 1925).

name: Bremstraat
en: A shrub of the pea family (broom).

name: Brenner
en: A mountain pass between Austria and Italy, 1374 metres high.

name: Brentanostraat
en: Clemens Brentano (1778-1842), German novelist, and Bernard von Brentano (1901-1964), German novelist and one of the so-called exile writers.

name: Brettenpad
en: De Bretten is the name of a former country house and farm that stood on the old Spaarnwouderdijk.

name: Breughelstraat
en: A Southern Netherlandish family of painters of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. Best known are Pieter the Elder, 'Peasant Bruegel' (1525-1569), Pieter the Younger, 'Hell Bruegel' (1564-1638), and Jan the Elder, nicknamed 'Velvet Bruegel' (1568-1625).

name: Brienzerstraat
en: The lake, the Brienzersee, in central Switzerland.

name: Brigantijnkade
en: A two-masted sailing ship, also called a schooner brig.

name: Brink
en: Brink means edge. The brink (a green or open space) usually lies somewhat to the side of the settlement. It is found in villages on sandy soil, on higher boulder-clay formations, and in villages on a mixture of the two.

name: Brinkiepad
en: Named after the children's farm of the same name next to it.

name: Brinkstraat
en: A brink is an open space in a settlement. Many brinks have since become village squares.

name: Brisselkerkstraat
en: A church village on the island of Schouwen, swallowed by the sea in 1554.

name: Bristou
en: A corrupted spelling of the French port of Brest, as found on sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Brittenburg
en: A sunken Roman fort at the old mouth of the Rhine off Katwijk (Zuid-Holland). In 1520, and later too, its foundations became visible on the beach in heavy storms.

name: Broekergouw
en: The gouw leads to the village of Broek in Waterland. Gouw is the Waterland word for a village road.

name: Broekermeerringsloot
en: A ring ditch around the clay polder Broekermeer, which was made around 1628.

name: Broekzijdschepad
en: A seventeenth-century polder south of Gaasperdam, near Abcoude.

name: Bromostraat
en: A volcano on the Indonesian island of Java. The Bromo is part of the Tengger massif in East Java.

name: Bronckhorststraat
en: Johannes G. Bronckhorst (1603-1662), painter and glass painter of historical scenes (windows in the Nieuwe Kerk and the Palace on the Dam).

name: Brouwersgracht
en: Named after the many breweries found in this neighbourhood in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. The prefixes Binnen (inner) and Buiten (outer) refer to the location in relation to the Haarlemmerdijk.

name: Bruins Slotstraat
en: Jan Albertus Hendrik Johan Bruins Slot (1906-1972), politician. Burgomaster of Adorp from 1933 to 1942 and a co-founder of the clandestine resistance paper 'Trouw'. After the Second World War he became a member of the House of Representatives for the Anti-Revolutionary Party, and ten years later he led its parliamentary group. He combined this with the editorship of 'Trouw'.

name: Bruinvisstraat
en: A fish-eating cetacean (the harbour porpoise) that never grows longer than two metres.

name: Brusselsingel
en: The capital of Belgium, in the province of Brabant.

name: Bufferstraat
en: A disc on a steel spring between two railway carriages that absorbs the shock when they bump together.

name: Buiksloterbreek
en: Buiksloot was an independent municipality until 1921, when it was absorbed into Amsterdam. 'Ban' means both jurisdiction and legal authority. The Banne Buiksloot was traditionally one of the six bannen (jurisdictions) into which the bailiwick of Waterland was divided. After the Batavian Revolution of 1795 the word remained in use, but by then it referred only to the polder. The Waterland bannen were not abolished until 1936.

name: Buiksloterdijk
en: The Waterland sea dike, as far as it lies in the former municipality of Buiksloot. The stretch continuing the Meeuwenlaan was later renamed Leeuwarderweg (council decision of 10 June 1936), and by council decision of 23 October 1974 the last stretch of the dike was added to the Landsmeerderdijk.

name: Buiksloterdraaibrug
en: The Buikslotermeerpolder, a lake drained in 1628.

name: Buiksloterkanaal
en: Buiksloot was an independent municipality until 1921, when it was absorbed into Amsterdam. 'Ban' means both a jurisdiction and the authority to judge. The Banne Buiksloot was of old one of the six bannen (jurisdictions) into which the bailiwick of Waterland was divided. After the Batavian Revolution of 1795 the word survived, but referred only to the polder. The Waterland bannen were not abolished until 1936.

name: Buiksloterkerkpad
en: Buiksloot was an independent municipality until 1921, when it was absorbed into Amsterdam. 'Ban' means both jurisdiction and legal authority. The Banne Buiksloot was traditionally one of the six bannen (jurisdictions) into which the bailiwick of Waterland was divided. After the Batavian Revolution of 1795 the word remained in use, but by then it referred only to the polder. The Waterland bannen were not abolished until 1936.

name: Buikslotermeerdijk
en: The Buikslotermeerpolder, a lake drained in 1628. Originally meadowland, it was largely built over with city districts between 1965 and 1974, and part of it is set aside for recreation. The dike came under Amsterdam in 1921 as the Meerdijk.

name: Buikslotermeerplein
en: The Buikslotermeerpolder, a lake drained in 1628. Originally meadowland, it was largely built over with city districts between 1965 and 1974, and part of it is set aside for recreation. The dike came under Amsterdam in 1921 as the Meerdijk.

name: Buiksloterweg
en: The road from the Tolhuis to the village of Buiksloot. It has been part of Amsterdam since 1877.

name: Buiten Bantammerstraat
en: The name recalls the sixteenth century, when the Dutch brought goods from Bantam (Dutch East Indies) to Amsterdam. In 1597 Houtman's ships were unloaded in the Waal. The Binnen Bantammerstraat was originally called Bantammerstraat. As early as around 1600 the bridge over the Geldersekade was called the Bantamsbrug. The houses on the street were then described as lying outside the Bantamspoort. In 1644 the Nieuwe Waalseiland was created. The Bantammerstraat was then given the prefix Binnen (inner), and its extension across the Oude Waal became the Buiten Bantammerstraat.

name: Buiten Brouwersstraat
en: Named after the many breweries found in this neighbourhood in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. The prefixes Binnen (inner) and Buiten (outer) refer to the location in relation to the Haarlemmerdijk.

name: Buiten Dommersstraat
en: The owner of the land on which the street was laid out was IJsbrand Jansz. Dommer. He was a ropemaker and a member of the council, and in 1579 he was appointed schepen (magistrate) of the city. Binnen (inner) and Buiten (outer) refer to the location, inside and outside the Haarlemmerdijk.

name: Buiten Kadijken
en: When a great deal of land had built up through silting outside the old sea dike (St. Antoniesdijk), a summer dike, or quay dike (kadijk), was built. It was originally called the new sea dike, but that name later fell out of use. When this new dike was raised further, people spoke of the Laagte (low part) and the Hoogte (high part) of the Kadijk. Until 1943 the Tussen Kadijken was called Korte Kerkstraat. This is because it lies in line with the Plantage Kerklaan, although it has never been connected to it.

name: Buiten Oranjestraat
en: The origin of the name is uncertain. It may refer to the house 'de Prins van Oranje', which once stood nearby on the Haarlemmerdijk. The division into Binnen (inner) and Buiten (outer) Oranjestraat refers to the location: inside and outside the dike (the Haarlemmerdijk).

name: Buiten Vissersstraat
en: The name recalls the many fishermen who lived here, originally outside the city gate. The first of the two streets lay inside the dike; the second lay on the IJ side, and so outside the dike.

name: Buiten Wieringerstraat
en: The street is named after Albert Pietersz van Wieringen. According to old documents from 1610 and 1624, he owned a house and several plots of land here. At that time the street was already referred to as Wieringerstraat. The division into two parts, inside and outside the Haarlemmerdijk, came into use in the eighteenth century.

name: Buiten-IJ
en: The water east of the Oranjesluizen, joining the IJmeer and the Markermeer.

name: Buitendijk
en: Named after the foreland of the Oostzanerdijk where the Melkweg sports park and the Coentunnel are now.

name: Buitendraaierij
en: This and other streets were laid out on the grounds of the former Amsterdamsche Droogdok Maatschappij (ADM). In memory of that earlier use, they are named after the shipyard's various workshops, in this case its turnery.

name: Buitengouw
en: The historical name of a route between the Zunderdorpergouw and the Buikslotermeer.

name: Buitenkerkerweg
en: Named after Buitenkerk, one of the four quarters into which Diemen used to be divided. Across the canal, in Diemen, lies the Buitenkerkerlaan.

name: Buitenrustpad
en: A former country house on the Kruislaan, opposite the present cemetery, built before 1725.

name: Buitenveldertselaan
en: Named after the Binnendijksche Buitenveldersche polder, originally a landscape of meadows and market gardens.

name: Buitenzagerij
en: This and other streets were laid out on the grounds of the former Amsterdamsche Droogdok Maatschappij (ADM). In memory of that earlier use, they are named after the shipyard's various workshops, in this case its sawmill.

name: Bulgerstein
en: A former castle on the Maas in Schieland, built according to tradition in the eleventh century.

name: Bullebak
en: The bullebak was a mythical water bogeyman that haunted not only the old little lock near the Haarlemmerplein but also the stone vault that joined the Bloemgracht to the Buitensingel (bridge 160). According to legend, the monster lay in wait there to drag into the water any passer-by who ventured too close to the edge.

name: Bullepad
en: Named after a side path of the Haarlemmerweg, level with the Vredenhofweg, that disappeared when the city expanded. The bul, the neighbourhood's breeding bull, was probably kept here.

name: Bullewijkpad
en: A small river, formed where the Waver and the Holendrecht meet, that flows into the Amstel at Ouderkerk.

name: Bultrugpad
en: A cetacean (the humpback whale), black with a white underside and peculiar lumps on its body, especially on its head. It occurs all over the world.

name: Bundlaan
en: An important street in Shanghai along the Huangpu River, thoroughly revitalised since the 1980s.

name: Bunsenstraat
en: Robert Wilhelm Bunsen (1811-1899), German chemist and discoverer of spectral analysis. He also invented the Bunsen burner named after him, a gas burner in which the gas is mixed with air before it burns.

name: Burgemeester Bletzstraat
en: Jan Christiaan Bletz (1865-1956), burgomaster of Weesperkarspel from 1895 to 1931. The street was named shortly after he stepped down.

name: Burgemeester Cramergracht
en: Willem Daniël Cramer (1788-1856), burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1836 to 1841.

name: Burgemeester De Vlugtlaan
en: Willem de Vlugt (1872-1945) was burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1921 to 1941. A carpenter's son from Kattenburg, he began as a building worker and contractor, and in that role worked on, among other things, the building of De Bijenkorf. His time as burgomaster is somewhat forgotten, partly because of the popularity and influence of his aldermen Floor Wibaut and Salomon de Miranda. De Vlugt earned good money in building but had no connections with the city's business, academic or cultural elite. He was a convinced Anti-Revolutionary: a conservative Christian burgomaster of an Amsterdam that was mostly left-wing at the time. Less than half the population was Protestant, and barely five percent was, like De Vlugt, Gereformeerd. At his job interview he was asked how he would respond if he had to grant permits for secular events. His answer was telling. He understood that 'city life in a municipality like Amsterdam makes its own particular demands, and that he had to take account of a public that does not share his principles'. He proved a man of his word by letting the 1928 Olympic Games go ahead on Sundays too, and even attending events on that day. Despite the hard times of the 1930s depression, De Vlugt was a popular burgomaster, and he held the office for a long time. But his failed and harsh handling of the Jordaan riot of 1934 shows another side. The riot began as a socialist and communist counter-demonstration against a demonstration by the NSB. When the NSB demonstration did not go ahead, the organisers of the counter-demonstration decided to protest instead against the cuts in unemployment relief brought in because of the depression. The riot was put down with a heavy hand: 5 people died and more than 50 were badly injured. Afterwards most of the Jordaan was asphalted, so that paving stones could never again be pulled up and thrown at the police. Another stain is how he treated his colleague De Miranda, whom De Telegraaf accused of corruption. De Miranda turned out to be innocent, but the affair drove him into depression and he had to be admitted to a psychiatric hospital. De Vlugt dropped De Miranda completely during this period. De Vlugt was burgomaster in a time of crisis, and then in wartime. The city government did not know how to deal with the occupying power and was unsure what the new relations would be. During the February Strike he did not speak out against the raids that the strike was protesting, and in a public notice he called on striking municipal employees to return to work. By then De Vlugt had been burgomaster for twenty years and was of advanced age. After the February Strike, in 1941, the German occupier dismissed him and replaced him with the pro-German burgomaster Edward Voûte. Earlier, as resident commissioner of the newspaper De Standaard and not as burgomaster, De Vlugt had agreed to the appointment of the NSB member Max Blokzijl as its editor. He retired to Aerdenhout, where he died on 10 February 1945.

name: Burgemeester Eliasstraat
en: Jonkheer David Willem Elias (1758-1828), member of the city government 1781-1795 and burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1813 to 1828. In 1814 he co-founded the Netherlands Bible Society.

name: Burgemeester Fockstraat
en: Cornelis Fock (1828-1910), burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1866 to 1868, and afterwards the King's Commissioner for Zuid-Holland.

name: Burgemeester Hogguerstraat
en: Jonkheer Paul Iwan Hogguer (1760-1816), member of the city government from 1791 to 1795, burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1813 to 1816 and president of De Nederlandsche Bank.

name: Burgemeester Kasteleinstraat
en: Dirk Daniel Willem Kastelein, born 1916, burgomaster of the former municipality of Weesperkarspel from 1956 until it was abolished in 1966. The street name was adopted at that municipality's last council meeting. Before that the street was called Gaaspstraat (council decision of Weesperkarspel, 29 November 1957).

name: Burgemeester Mulstraat
en: Aart Willem Mul (born 1887), burgomaster of the municipality of Weesperkarspel, and afterwards acting burgomaster for some years.

name: Burgemeester Rendorpstraat
en: Joachim Rendorp (1728-1792), several times burgomaster of Amsterdam between 1781 and 1792.

name: Burgemeester Röellstraat
en: Jonkheer Antonie baron Röell (1864-1940), burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1910 to 1915, and afterwards the Queen's Commissioner for Noord-Holland.

name: Burgemeester Stramanweg
en: Josephus Anthonius A. Straman (1890-1938), burgomaster of Ouder-Amstel from 1920.

name: Burgemeester Tellegenstraat
en: Jan Willem Cornelis Tellegen (1859-1921), structural engineer. Burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1915 to 1921; before that, director of the Building and Housing Inspectorate.

name: Burgemeester Van de Pollstraat
en: Jonkheer Frederik van de Poll (1780-1853), burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1828 to 1835, who resigned over the tax riot.

name: Burgemeester Van Leeuwenlaan
en: Wilhelmus Frederik van Leeuwen (1860-1930), successively alderman (1895-1901) and burgomaster of Amsterdam (1901-1910), Queen's Commissioner for Noord-Holland (1910-1915) and vice-president of the Council of State. While he was burgomaster, the municipal water, gas and transport companies were set up.

name: Burgemeester Van Tienhovengracht
en: Gijsbert van Tienhoven (1841-1914), alderman from 1874 to 1880 and burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1880 to 1891, and afterwards a minister.

name: Burgemeester Vening Meineszlaan
en: Sjoerd Anne Vening Meinesz (1833-1909), alderman of Amsterdam (1869-1872), burgomaster of Rotterdam (1881-1891) and burgomaster of Amsterdam (1891-1901).

name: Burgersdijkstraat
en: Leendert A.J. Burgersdijk (1828-1900), physicist and man of letters. He translated the complete works of Shakespeare into Dutch.

name: Burgersweerhof
en: Burgersweer was once a settlement on the south side of the Lutkemeer (map by Gerrit Drogeham, about 1650).

name: Burgerweeshuispad
en: Named after the Burgerweeshuis (citizens' orphanage), which from 1580 to 1960 occupied the buildings of today's Amsterdam Historical Museum on the Kalverstraat, and then moved to the IJsbaanpad. The orphanage took its name from the fact that it admitted only children whose parents could be shown to have been official citizens (burgers) of the city.

name: Burmandwarsstraat
en: Johannes Burman (1706-1779), professor of botany in Amsterdam. When it was laid out, this street was first named Oetgensstraat (council decision of 30 November 1881).

name: Burmanstraat
en: Johannes Burman (1706-1779), professor of botany in Amsterdam. When it was laid out, this street was first named Oetgensstraat (council decision of 30 November 1881).

name: Busken Huetstraat
en: Coenraad Busken Huet (1826-1886), a Walloon Church minister who from 1862 devoted himself to journalism and literature. A member of the editorial board of 'De Nieuwe Gids'.

name: Buskenblaserstraat
en: One of the fourteenth-century sotternieën (farces).

name: Bussumstraat
en: A town in the Gooi (Noord-Holland).

name: Butaanweg
en: A colourless, odourless, flammable gas.

name: Butskopweg
en: A dolphin-like toothed whale (the bottlenose whale) with a distinct beak and a very blunt, high forehead. It can reach seven to ten metres in length. It occurs in the Atlantic and in the southern Indian Ocean.

name: Buys Ballotstraat
en: Christoforus Henricius Buys Ballot (1817-1890), meteorologist and founder of the meteorological institute (Buys Ballot's law).

name: Buyskade
en: Johan Theodoor Buys (1828-1893), Leiden professor of political science. His works include 'De Grondwet' (the Constitution), a three-volume standard work published 1883-1888.

name: Buyspad
en: Johan Theodoor Buys (1828-1893), Leiden professor of political science. His works include 'De grondwet' (the Constitution), a three-volume standard work published between 1883 and 1888.

name: Buziaustraat
en: Johannes Fr. Buziau (1877-1958), revue artist, for many years with the Ter Hall revue.

name: C. Kruyswijkstraat
en: Cornelis Kruyswijk (1884-1935), architect. He designed fourteen Amsterdam primary schools and several churches, such as today's Apostolic Church on the Clematisstraat.

name: C. van Eesterenlaan
en: Cornelis van Eesteren (1897-1988), architect and town planner. From 1929 to 1959 he headed the Urban Development department of Amsterdam's Public Works service. He designed the General Extension Plan of Amsterdam and played a leading part in planning the post-war districts of Slotermeer, Slotervaart, Osdorp and the Bijlmermeer.

name: C.J.K. van Aalststraat
en: Cornelis Johannes Karel van Aalst (1866-1939), banker. President of the Nederlandsche Handel-Maatschappij and later director of the Nederlandsche Overzee Trust Maatschappij. One of the initiators of the Koninklijke Hollandsche Lloyd and the Nederlandsche Scheepvaart Unie.

name: C.K. Eloutstraat
en: Cornelis K. Elout (1870-1947), journalist, for many years parliamentary reporter and correspondent for the Algemeen Handelsblad.

name: C.P.M. Rommeplantsoen
en: Carl Paul Maria Romme (1896-1980), statesman. Member of the House of Representatives for the Roman Catholic State Party (1933-1937), Minister of Social Affairs under Colijn (1937-1939) and a member of Amsterdam's city council. From 1946 to 1961 he led the KVP's parliamentary group, and from 1945 to 1953 he was editor-in-chief of 'de Volkskrant'. In 1971 he was made a Minister of State.

name: Cabotstraat
en: The father Giovanni Cabot (1425-1498) and his son Sebastiano Cabot (1472-1557), Italian explorers. Giovanni discovered Labrador, among other places; Sebastiano explored the east coast of South America and discovered Newfoundland.

name: Cabralstraat
en: Pedro Alvarez Cabral (1460-1520), Portuguese navigator who discovered Brazil in 1500 on his voyage to India.

name: Cacaohaven
en: The tropical product, the raw material for chocolate, that is transhipped in the port of Amsterdam.

name: Cacaoweg
en: The tropical product, the raw material for chocolate, that is transhipped in the port of Amsterdam.

name: Callantsoogstraat
en: A village in the dunes of Noord-Holland.

name: Camera Obscurabrug
en: This bridge is named after the book Camera Obscura, published in 1839 by Hildebrand, the pseudonym of Nicolaas Beets (1814-1903).

name: Camille Balystraat
en: Camille E. Baly (Sint Maarten, 1936 - Sint Maarten, 2012) was a poet, writer and performer of spoken word. His work drew heavily on the oral history of the Windward Islands of the former Netherlands Antilles. He wrote mainly in English but also performed in Dutch. For many years he headed the island of Sint Maarten's office of Culture and Education.

name: Campanulapad
en: Named after the plant (the bellflower).

name: Campanulastraat
en: Named after the plant (the bellflower).

name: Camperstraat
en: Petrus Camper (1722-1789), professor of medicine and surgery in Amsterdam and Groningen.

name: Cannenburg
en: A fourteenth-century castle near Vaassen (Gelderland), rebuilt several times since.

name: Capriweg
en: An Italian island in the Mediterranean.

name: Carel Reynierszhaven
en: Lived from 1604 to 1653. He founded the first settlement of the Dutch East India Company on the Coromandel Coast (India). From 1650 to 1653 he was Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies.

name: Carillonstraat
en: A carillon (klokkenspel) consisting of a number of cast bells.

name: Carnapstraat
en: Rudolf Carnap (1891-1970), German-American philosopher, professor in Prague from 1931 to 1935. For Carnap, the task of philosophy lay mainly in the logical and epistemological analysis of the language of the sciences.

name: Carolina MacGillavrylaan
en: Carolina Henriëtte MacGillavry (1904-1993), professor of chemistry at the University of Amsterdam. In 1950 she became the first woman to join the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (KNAW).

name: Caroline Herschelbrug
en: Caroline Herschel (Hanover, 1750 - Hanover, 1848) was involved in building and grinding the lenses of the very largest telescopes of the seventeenth century, and she discovered and described nebulae not observed before. Caroline Herschel also made many observations of her own. She was the first woman with a paid scientific post.

name: Carrascoplein
en: The name of the airport of Montevideo, Uruguay.

name: Carry Pothuis-Smitstraat
en: Wilhelmina Carolina Benjamina Smit (1872-1951), a feminist from the very beginning and a leading figure in the social-democratic women's organisations. Member of Amsterdam's city council from 1919 to 1924. In 1920 she became the first woman member of the Senate (Eerste Kamer).

name: Carry van Bruggenstraat
en: Carry de Haan (1881-1932), writer, wife of the writer Kees van Bruggen.

name: Cas Oorthuyskade
en: Photographer (1908-1975). In the early 1930s he joined the Association of Worker Photographers. During the Second World War he belonged to the group of photographers later known as De Ondergedoken Camera (the hidden camera). He photographed the Hunger Winter of 1944. Long after the liberation, social engagement remained central to Oorthuys's photography.

name: Casablancaweg
en: A port city in Morocco. The street lies near the Afrikahaven in the western port area.

name: Castorplein
en: A star in the constellation Gemini (the Twins).

name: Castorstraat
en: A star in the constellation Gemini (the Twins).

name: Catharina Boudewijnshof
en: Catharina Boudewijns (c. 1520 - after 1603), Southern Netherlandish poet, a representative of distinctly Catholic literature in the second half of the sixteenth century.

name: Catharina van Rennesstraat
en: Composer, singer and teacher (1858-1940). Her great contribution was to children's songs. She set many texts by Guido Gezelle to music and wrote, among others, the music for 'Drie kleine kleutertjes' and 'Kinderen van een Vader'. She founded singing schools in several towns.

name: Catharina van Tussenbroekstraat
en: Doctor (1852-1925). She took her doctorate in 1887, which makes her one of the three women doctors to do so before 1898. At the National Exhibition of Women's Work in 1898 she made a plea for good vocational training for women. A member of the Association of Women with an Academic Degree. In 1919 she ended her career as an obstetrician.

name: Cecilia van Alphen-Jagtmanbrug
en: Cecilia Maria Cornelia Jagtman (1910-1972) and her husband Pieter van Alphen (1909-1953) were active members of the CPN (Communist Party). During the Second World War, at the risk of their lives, they produced and distributed the clandestine newspaper De Waarheid, among others. He was arrested by the Nazis in April 1941. She carried on the work, and also hid people in her house at Fresiastraat 12 in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Ceintuurbaan
en: At the end of the nineteenth century a ring road (ceintuurweg, or belt) was laid around a large part of the city. The stretch between the Boerenwetering and the Amstel was later named Ceintuurbaan. The other stretches later got other names, because a section in between was not yet part of Amsterdam at the time.

name: Ceintuurbrug
en: At the end of the nineteenth century a ring road (ceintuurweg, or belt) was laid around a large part of the city. The stretch between the Boerenwetering and the Amstel was later named Ceintuurbaan. The other stretches later got other names, because a section in between was not yet part of Amsterdam at the time.

name: Celebesstraat
en: An island in Indonesia, now called Sulawesi.

name: Celsiusstraat
en: Anders Celsius (1701-1744), Swedish physicist and astronomer. In 1742 he introduced a temperature scale from zero to a hundred degrees, known as the Celsius scale. The municipality of Watergraafsmeer originally named the street Steinstraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 31 October 1891).

name: Centaurusstraat
en: A constellation of the southern sky.

name: Centavoshof
en: The centavo is worth 1/100 of Portugal's standard coin (the escudo).

name: Centimehof
en: The centime is worth 1/100 of France's standard coin (the French franc).

name: Centrale Groothandelsmarkt
en: Refers to the Centrale Markthallen (central market halls).

name: Céramiquelaan
en: A district on the Maas in Maastricht, named after the demolished Société Céramique pottery works. In 1987 its present buildings were developed by architects such as Aldo Rossi and Jo Coenen.

name: Ceramplein
en: An island in Indonesia.

name: Chaloen
en: The castle, also called Schaloen, near Valkenburg (Limburg), built in the seventeenth century and restored and altered in 1894.

name: Changiweg
en: The name of Singapore's airport.

name: Charles Boissevainstraat
en: Journalist (1842-1929), for many years editor-in-chief of the Algemeen Handelsblad. Known for his commentaries in the column 'Van dag tot dag' (from day to day).

name: Charles Leickertstraat
en: Painter (1818-1907), mainly of townscapes.

name: Charley Tooropbrug
en: Charley Toorop (1891-1955) developed her own style, Expressive Objective Realism (Expressief Zakelijk Realisme). She is widely regarded as the most powerful woman in twentieth-century Dutch painting.

name: Charlie Parkerstraat
en: American jazz alto saxophonist (1920-1955), nicknamed Bird. An improviser and composer, and one of the most important figures in the history of jazz.

name: Charlotte Brontéstraat
en: English novelist (1816-1855), sister of the writers Anne and Emily Brontë. The correct spelling, incidentally, is Brontë. Her best-known book is 'Jane Eyre'.

name: Charlotte de Bourbonstraat
en: The third wife of Prince William of Orange (1546-1582).

name: Chasséstraat
en: David Henderikus Chassé (1765-1849), officer. A general at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815, he defended the Citadel of Antwerp in 1832. When it was laid out, the street was named Van Rijnstraat (council decision of Sloten, 20 July 1910).

name: Chestertonlaan
en: Gilbert Keith Chesterton (1874-1936), English novelist, poet and essayist. His lasting fame comes from the stories about the priest-detective Father Brown.

name: Chet Bakerstraat
en: Chesney Henry Baker (1929-1988), American singer and trumpeter, known for his restrained trumpet solos and his fragile singing. In the 1980s he worked mainly in Europe. He died in Amsterdam after a fall from the window of a hotel on the Prins Hendrikkade.

name: Chico Mendesstraat
en: Brazilian rubber tapper (1944-1988) from the Amazon, a prominent campaigner for saving the rainforests and against land theft by big landowners.

name: Chopinstraat
en: Frédéric Chopin (1810-1849), Polish composer and pianist, who settled in Paris in 1831.

name: Chris Lebeaustraat
en: Visual artist (1878-1945), an important representative of Dutch Art Nouveau and Art Deco. He was active in the resistance during the Second World War. He was arrested in 1943 and died two years later in the Dachau concentration camp.

name: Christiaan Brüningsstraat
en: Hydraulic engineer (1736-1805). He worked for the centralisation of water management.

name: Christiaan de Wetstraat
en: One of the Boer generals of the Orange Free State (1854-1922). He inflicted a number of defeats on the British, and remained anti-British after the peace of 1902. He was honoured with this street in his lifetime. It was first named De Wetstraat in 1904. The street's shape was changed several more times, by council decisions of 21 January 1920, 26 July 1923 and 7 May 1929.

name: Christiaan Huygensplein
en: Mathematician and physicist (1629-1695), inventor of the pendulum clock and author of the wave theory of light.

name: Christian Neefestraat
en: Christian Gottlob Neefe (1748-1798), German opera composer and conductor. Court organist in Bonn and, from 1779, teacher of Ludwig van Beethoven.

name: Christine Poolmanhof
en: Actress (1850-1930), for many years with the Royal Society Het Nederlands Toneel under Willem Royaards.

name: Christine Stoetzhof
en: Actress (1829-1897) who excelled in comic roles and succeeded Mrs Kleine as teacher at the Drama School. She was a granddaughter of Majofski, the mother of Marie van Westerhoven and the grandmother of Louis Chrispijn.

name: Christoffel Plantijngracht
en: Southern Netherlandish printer and lexicographer (1514-1589). His printing and publishing house in Antwerp grew into one of the most famous in Europe (now a museum).

name: Christoffel Plantijnpad
en: Southern Netherlandish printer and lexicographer (1514-1589). His printing and publishing house in Antwerp grew into one of the most famous in Europe (now a museum).

name: Christoffelkruidstraat
en: An ornamental plant of the buttercup family found in South Limburg (baneberry), with white flowers and poisonous black berries.

name: Chrysantenstraat
en: A plant (the chrysanthemum).

name: Churchill-laan
en: Sir Winston L.S. Churchill (1874-1965), English statesman, head of the British war cabinet in 1940-45. One of the Big Three, with Roosevelt and Stalin, to whom we partly owe our liberation. He received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1953. Churchill is one of the few people honoured with a street name in their lifetime. Before 1946 the street was called Noorder Amstellaan (council decision of 22 March 1922).

name: Cilliersstraat
en: Sarel Cilliers, South African, a leader of the Great Trek of the Boers in 1836 from the Cape Colony to what later became the Transvaal.

name: Circusplein
en: A show in a tent with attractions such as animal acts, acrobatics and clowns. The name is linked to the world of travelling people and refers to the caravan site here.

name: Cissy van Marxveldtstraat
en: Pseudonym of Sietske Beek-de Haan (1889-1948), children's author, best known for her four-part Joop ter Heul series.

name: Citroenenstraat
en: A citrus fruit (the lemon).

name: Clara Bartonstraat
en: Nurse (1821-1912), called the 'Florence Nightingale' of the American Civil War. One of the pioneers of the Red Cross.

name: Clara Meyer-Wichmannstraat
en: Clara Gertrud Meyer-Wichmann (1885-1922), lawyer and writer. She helped found a local branch of the Dutch Association for Women's Suffrage, and from 1911 to 1916 wrote extensively on women's suffrage. The Clara Wichmann Foundation, the national centre for government equality policy in law, is named after her.

name: Clara Schumannstraat
en: Clara Schumann (1819-1896), German composer and pianist.

name: Clara Zetkinstraat
en: German champion of women's emancipation (1857-1933), active from 1878 for the then illegal German Social Democratic party. Early in the twentieth century she led the German women's movement. From 1920 to 1933 she was a member of the Reichstag, which she chaired in 1933.

name: Claude Debussylaan
en: Claude Achille Debussy (1862-1918), French composer and an innovator in classical music. He was inspired by his travels to Beirut and by Javanese music. With his own distinctive combinations of sounds and harmonies, he wrote many works for piano and orchestra, chamber music and vocal music.

name: Claus van Amsbergstraat
en: Claus George Willem Otto Frederik Geert van Amsberg (1926-2002), Prince of the Netherlands, Jonkheer van Amsberg, husband of Queen Beatrix of the Netherlands. Prince Claus worked for peace and human rights. Among other posts, he was appointed to the National Advisory Council for Development Cooperation, chairman of the National Committee for Development Strategy and chairman of the Netherlands Volunteers Foundation.

name: Clauskindereweg
en: A village on Schouwen-Duiveland (Zeeland) drowned by a storm flood in 1511.

name: Clematisstraat
en: A climbing plant (clematis).

name: Cliffordstraat
en: Jonkheer George Gerard Clifford (1779-1847). Treasurer of Amsterdam, Minister of the Colonies, Minister of State.

name: Cliostraat
en: The muse of history (Greek mythology).

name: Coenhaven
en: Jan Pieterszoon Coen (1587-1629). Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies (1619-1623 and 1627-1629). He founded Batavia, which regained its old name after the transfer of sovereignty.

name: Coenhavenweg
en: Jan Pieterszoon Coen (1587-1629). Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies (1619-1623 and 1627-1629). He founded Batavia, which regained its old name after the transfer of sovereignty.

name: Coentunnelcircuit
en: Jan Pieterszoon Coen (1587-1629). Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies (1619-1623 and 1627-1629). He founded Batavia, which regained its old name after the transfer of sovereignty.

name: Coentunnelweg
en: Jan Pieterszoon Coen (1587-1629). Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies (1619-1623 and 1627-1629). He founded Batavia, which regained its old name after the transfer of sovereignty.

name: Coffijboomstraat
en: Named after the historical ship the Coffijboom, which carried enslaved people in the eighteenth century.

name: Cola Debrotstraat
en: Cola Debrot (Bonaire, 1902 - Amsterdam, 1981) left for the Netherlands at fourteen to study. He studied law in Utrecht for a time, but left for Paris in 1928. From 1931 he studied medicine in the Netherlands, and in 1942 he set up as a doctor in Amsterdam. While a student he made his debut with a long novella, Mijn zuster de negerin (1935), and in 1940 he co-founded the magazine Criterium. In 1948 Debrot returned to the Antilles and settled in Willemstad, where he was active in cultural life, especially for the Cultureel Centrum Curaçao. In 1952 he became Minister Plenipotentiary of the Netherlands Antilles, and in 1962 governor. In 1970 he settled in the Netherlands again and devoted himself to writing. After his death the Cola Debrot Prize was established. Its first winner was Boelie van Leeuwen, for his whole body of work.

name: Colenbranderhof
en: Herman Theodoor Colenbrander (1871-1945), historian. Editorial secretary of 'De Gids' and author of several historical works, among them 'De Patriottentijd', 'De Belgische Omwenteling' and 'Koloniale Geschiedenis'.

name: Colensostraat
en: A place in Natal (South Africa) where the Boer general Botha defeated the British in 1899.

name: Colimastraat
en: A volcano in Mexico with two peaks.

name: Colnot en Poonshof
en: The cabaret artists Gustaaf Jacobus Marinus Colnot (1863-1951) and Salomon Poons (1853-1925), who ran the Plantage-Schouwburg theatre on what is now the Henri Polaklaan.

name: Columbusplein
en: Christopher Columbus (1446-1506), seafarer from Genoa. Trying to reach China by sailing west, he discovered the Antilles in 1492, and Central and South America on three later voyages.

name: Columbusstraat
en: Christopher Columbus (1446-1506), seafarer from Genoa. Trying to reach China by sailing west, he discovered the Antilles in 1492, and Central and South America on three later voyages.

name: Comeniusstraat
en: Jan Amos Komenský (1592-1670), who called himself Comenius. A founder of pedagogy, from Moravia (Czech Republic). He settled in Amsterdam in 1657 and lived for a long time with burgomaster De Geer at Keizersgracht 123 (the 'Huis met de Hoofden', house with the heads). He is buried in Naarden, where his mausoleum is now part of the Comenius Museum.

name: Commelinstraat
en: Caspar Commelin (1636-1693), historian of Amsterdam. He edited the updated new edition of 'De beschrijvinghe van Amsterdam' (the description of Amsterdam) in 1691.

name: Compagniestraat
en: Named after the Dutch East India Company (VOC), which from 1661 had its arsenal, shipyard and ropewalk built here on Oostenburg. The building at Oostenburgergracht 79 still recalls this. The street was laid out over the former Oostenburgermiddenstraat, which disappeared as a result.

name: Computerweg
en: As a counterpart to the street names recalling Amsterdam-Noord's former shipbuilding industry, this name refers to modern information technology.

name: Conakryweg
en: An African port city, capital of Guinea. The street lies near the Afrikahaven in the western port area.

name: Concertgebouwplein
en: The concert hall, built between 1882 and 1888 by A.L. van Gendt. Shortly after it opened, the Concertgebouw Orchestra was founded. The square got this name to mark the Concertgebouw's centenary. Before that it was the Jan Willem Brouwersplein (council decision of 3 April 1912).

name: Condensatorweg
en: A capacitor: a part of electrical appliances, or a component in its own right, that can hold an electric charge.

name: Confuciusplein
en: The correct spelling is Confucius. Chinese philosopher (551-478 BC), founder of the old Chinese state religion, in which personal morality is subordinate to that of the state.

name: Conny Stuartstraat
en: Conny Stuart (Wijhe, 5 September 1913 - Amsterdam, 22 August 2010), pseudonym of Cornelia van Meijgaard, was a Dutch singer, actress, cabaret artist and musical star.

name: Conradstraat
en: Frederik Willem Conrad (1800-1876), hydraulic engineer. He designed several hydraulic works in the Netherlands and the plans for cutting through the Isthmus of Suez, as well as the first railway station at the Haarlemmerpoort (1839).

name: Contactweg
en: An electrical connection (contact).

name: Coöperatiehof
en: The form of cooperation (coöperatie) through which the housing in this district was built after the First World War.

name: Coornhertstraat
en: Dirk Volkertszoon Coornhert (1522-1590), writer, humanist and philosopher. He fought against abuses in the Roman Catholic Church.

name: Copernicusstraat
en: Nicolaus Copernicus (1473-1543), Polish physician and astronomer. He taught that the sun is the centre of our planetary system, against the teaching of Ptolemy, who held the earth to be the centre.

name: Coppelstockstraat
en: Jan Pieterszoon Coppelstock, the ferryman who helped the Sea Beggars (watergeuzen) take Den Briel on 1 April 1572.

name: Cor Hermusstraat
en: Actor and director (1889-1953). As a gifted teacher he influenced the younger generation.

name: Cor Ruyshof
en: Actor (1890-1952) who excelled in comedy. For many years he performed with his own company.

name: Cor van der Hartbrug
en: Cornelis van der Hart (1928-2006) was a Dutch centre-half who began his football career at Ajax in 1947, where he was also assistant coach from 1984 to 1987. Between 1955 and 1961 he played 44 times for the Netherlands national team.

name: Corantijnstraat
en: A river in Suriname, on the border with Guyana.

name: Corellistraat
en: Arcangelo Corelli (1653-1713), Italian composer and violinist.

name: Cornelis Aarnoutsstraat
en: Cornelis Aarnouts or Aernouts (1914-1943), resistance fighter. He organised the distribution network of the clandestine paper 'De Waarheid'. Executed by firing squad in Scheveningen on 10 August 1943.

name: Cornelis Anthoniszstraat
en: Painter, engraver and cartographer (1500 - after 1559), known for his maps of Amsterdam. In 1536 he made a painted map; his detailed woodcut dates from 1544.

name: Cornelis Dijksterhuisstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1921-1944), involved in organising the clandestine paper 'Trouw'.

name: Cornelis Dirkszstraat
en: Burgomaster of Monnickendam, later admiral of Noord-Holland (1542-1583). One of the leaders of the Sea Beggars (watergeuzen), he defeated the Spanish on the Zuiderzee in 1573.

name: Cornelis Dopperkade
en: Composer (1870-1939), opera conductor, later second conductor of the Concertgebouw Orchestra. He composed eight symphonies and several operas.

name: Cornelis Douweskanaal (Oost)
en: Navigator, mathematician and astronomer (1712-1773). Director of the Amsterdam Nautical School (Zeevaartschool).

name: Cornelis Douweskanaal (West)
en: Navigator, mathematician and astronomer (1712-1773). Director of the Amsterdam Nautical School (Zeevaartschool).

name: Cornelis Douwesweg
en: Navigator, mathematician and astronomer (1712-1773). Director of the Amsterdam Nautical School (Zeevaartschool).

name: Cornelis Drebbelstraat
en: Engineer, physicist and versatile inventor (1572-1631), Dutch by birth, who worked at the imperial court in Prague (1610-1613) and later in England. He designed the first submarine and improved the microscope. The street came over from the municipality of Watergraafsmeer in 1921 under the name Kerklaan.

name: Cornelis Krusemanstraat
en: Painter (1797-1857) of historical and biblical scenes.
