name: Cornelis Lelylaan
en: Hydraulic engineer and statesman (1854-1929), several times Minister of Water Management. He designed the plan to close off the Zuiderzee and partly drain it. His statue, by Man Andriessen, stands at the start of the Afsluitdijk. The town of Lelystad, capital of the province of Flevoland, is named after him.

name: Cornelis Lelyplein
en: Hydraulic engineer and statesman (1854-1929), several times Minister of Water Management. He designed the plan to close off the Zuiderzee and partly drain it. His statue, by Man Andriessen, stands at the start of the Afsluitdijk. The town of Lelystad, capital of the province of Flevoland, is named after him.

name: Cornelis Outshoornstraat
en: Architect (1812-1875). His works include the Paleis voor Volksvlijt (1859-1864) and the Amstel Hotel (1864).

name: Cornelis Roobolstraat
en: A captain of the Beggars (geuzen). In 1572 he was captured by the Spanish near Haarlem and put to death.

name: Cornelis Roosstraat
en: Cornelis Janszoon Roos (1692-1757), burgomaster of Oostzaan and a whaling shipowner in 1724 and 1725. On the Twiske he owned about twelve warehouses containing train-oil boileries. (His gravestone is in the Dutch Reformed church in Oostzaan.)

name: Cornelis Schuurmanhof
en: Resistance fighter (1915-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Scheveningen. Schuurman worked on the clandestine paper 'De Waarheid'.

name: Cornelis Schuytstraat
en: Composer and organist (1557-1616), known above all as an organist.

name: Cornelis Sorgdragerstraat
en: Whaling commander (first voyage 1690). He did valuable work recording the experiences of whaling in his 'Bloeiende opkomst der aloude en hedendaagse Groenlandse visserij' (the flourishing rise of the old and present Greenland fishery).

name: Cornelis Springerstraat
en: Painter (1817-1891) of townscapes, among them Haarlem and Den Briel.

name: Cornelis Troostplein
en: Pastel and genre painter (1697-1750). He became known for his group portrait 'Inspectors of the Collegium Medicum'.

name: Cornelis Trooststraat
en: Pastel and genre painter (1697-1750). He became known for his group portrait 'Inspectors of the Collegium Medicum'.

name: Cornelis van Alkemadestraat
en: Historian (1654-1737) who wrote about old monasteries and noble houses.

name: Cornelis van der Lindenstraat
en: Conductor and composer (1839-1918) of operas, cantatas and overtures. Conductor of the Hollandse Opera from 1886 to 1903.

name: Cornelis van Rijplantsoen
en: Resistance fighter (1896-1958) who fought at the Grebbeberg in 1940. After his demobilisation he founded a resistance group and was also an editor of 'Vrij Nederland'. Arrested in 1941 for espionage and illegal possession of weapons, he was sentenced to death in 1942. The sentence was later commuted to fifteen years' penal servitude. He remained in prison until the liberation in 1945.

name: Cornelis van Vollenhovenstraat
en: Legal scholar (1874-1933), professor at Leiden from 1901 to 1933. An expert on the law of the Indies and on international law.

name: Cornelis Vermuydenstraat
en: Hydraulic engineer (1590-1677). In 1619 he took his knowledge of Zeeland dike building to England, where he was involved in draining the great peat district of The Fens in East Anglia. He was raised to the English nobility in 1629, but was later imprisoned for debts from failed projects. Some of his plans were carried out after his death.

name: Cornelis Vriendtstraat
en: Flemish architect and sculptor (1518-1575). His buildings include Antwerp's city hall.

name: Cornelis Zillesenlaan
en: Tax collector (1736-1828) and member of the Hollandsche Maatschappij der Wetenschappen (Holland Society of Sciences). He made two inventions meant to improve the means of measuring a ship's speed. The intended improvements were not achieved, however.

name: Coronelstraat
en: Pierre Antoine Coronel (1914-1945), resistance fighter. Born in Ouder-Amstel, executed by firing squad in Amsterdam.

name: Corry Tendeloobrug
en: Nancy Sophie Cornélie Tendeloo (1897-1956), politician, feminist and lawyer. City councillor for the Vrijzinnig Democratische Bond (VDB) from 1938 to 1941, and from 1945 to 1956 a member of the House of Representatives for the VDB and then the PvdA. Among other things, in 1955 she moved to end the dismissal of married women from government service, which happened a year later.

name: Corsgenbrug
en: This fixed bridge is named after the timber merchant Corsgen Jacobsz, who in the fifteenth century had an orchard on the Singel, just outside the city. The bridge over the Singel took its name from him, and then so did the alley on the other side of the Singel. This bridge was also called Korsjesbrug or Korsjespoort.

name: Corsicaweg
en: An island in the Mediterranean.

name: Cort van der Lindenkade
en: Pieter W.A. Cort van der Linden (1846-1935), liberal statesman. Professor at Groningen and Amsterdam, Minister of Justice (1897-1901) and Prime Minister (1913-1918). He brought in universal suffrage and equal funding for public and denominational schools.

name: Cortenbach
en: The originally fifteenth-century castle, now a manor house mainly dating from 1776, near Voerendaal (South Limburg).

name: Corversbosstraat
en: A nature reserve west of Hilversum. The Corversbos was originally part of the Gooilust estate and was for a time owned by the Amsterdam regent family Corver.

name: Cosmariumstraat
en: A microscopic water plant, a desmid (bandwier), made of two matching halves.

name: Couhornerhoek
en: Named after the almost right-angled bend in the Oostzanerdijk between the Plejadenplein and Molenwijk. It once lay completely exposed to the IJ.

name: Count Basiestraat
en: William (Count) Basie (1904-1984), American jazz pianist, composer and bandleader.

name: Courbetstraat
en: Gustave Courbet (1819-1877), French realist painter, mainly of hunting scenes and figure pieces.

name: Crabschuytstraat
en: A small fishing boat that turns up at the beginning of the seventeenth century in a description by the shipbuilder Cornelis van Yk.

name: Crack-State
en: An imposing state (a Frisian manor house) in Heerenveen (Friesland), probably built in 1608 by Hypolitus Crack.

name: Cromme Camp
en: A historical name in the former municipality of Sloten: a plot of land.

name: Cronenburg
en: A former castle near Loenen aan de Vecht. Built in 1122 and destroyed in 1296, rebuilt in 1354 and demolished in 1837. Only the outline of its foundations remains.

name: Cronjéstraat
en: Pieter Arnoldus Cronjé (1835-1911), South African Boer general, who had to surrender to the British at Paardeberg in 1900.

name: Cruquiuskade
en: Nicolaas Samuel Cruquius (or Kruik) (1678-1754), hydraulic engineer, who drew up a plan to drain the Haarlemmermeer.

name: Cruquiusstraat
en: Nicolaas Samuel Cruquius (or Kruik) (1678-1754), hydraulic engineer, who drew up a plan to drain the Haarlemmermeer.

name: Cruquiusweg
en: Nicolaas Samuel Cruquius (or Kruik) (1678-1754), hydraulic engineer, who drew up a plan to drain the Haarlemmermeer.

name: Cruuskerkstraat
en: A church village drowned in the St Elizabeth's flood of 1421, which lay where Dubbeldam (Zuid-Holland) is today.

name: Crynssenstraat
en: Abraham Crijnssen, Zeeland admiral. He conquered Suriname in 1667 and fought in the Battle of the Downs and against the Algerians. He died in 1669.

name: Cullinanplein
en: The Cullinan is the largest South African diamond.

name: Curaçaostraat
en: An island belonging to the Netherlands Antilles.

name: Curiestraat
en: The French couple Pierre Curie (1859-1906) and Marie Curie-Skłodowska (1867-1934), discoverers of radium. Together they received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903, and Madame Curie received another in 1911, for chemistry.

name: Cuyperspassage
en: Petrus J. Cuypers (1827-1921), architect and creator of Dutch Gothic Revival. His buildings include the Rijksmuseum (1885), Centraal Station (1889) and the Vondelkerk (1878).

name: Cycladenlaan
en: A Greek island group in the Aegean Sea. All the islands of the Cyclades lie in a circle (ancient Greek: kyklos) around Delos, an important Greek sanctuary in antiquity.

name: Cyclamenstraat
en: A house plant (cyclamen).

name: Czaar Peterstraat
en: Peter I, Emperor of Russia (1672-1725), who spent about half a year in the Netherlands in 1697, first in Amsterdam and then in Zaandam. He worked at the East India Company's shipyard to learn shipbuilding.

name: D.L. Hudigstraat
en: Dirk Louis Jacobszoon Hudig (1876-1973), director of the Koninklijke Nederlandse Stoomboot Maatschappij (Royal Dutch Steamship Company) from 1917 to 1947, which gave him a leading position in Dutch and international shipping. He held countless other posts, among them chairman of the supervisory board of N.V. Nederlandse Telegraaf Maatschappij.

name: Da Costagracht
en: Isaäc da Costa (1798-1860), Amsterdam lawyer, poet and prose writer of Portuguese-Jewish descent, who converted to Christianity.

name: Da Costakade
en: Isaäc da Costa (1798-1860), Amsterdam lawyer, poet and prose writer of Portuguese-Jewish descent, who converted to Christianity.

name: Da Costaplein
en: Isaäc da Costa (1798-1860), Amsterdam lawyer, poet and prose writer of Portuguese-Jewish descent, who converted to Christianity.

name: Da Costastraat
en: Isaäc da Costa (1798-1860), Amsterdam lawyer, poet and prose writer of Portuguese-Jewish descent, who converted to Christianity.

name: Daalwijk
en: The name of a farmstead in Markelo (Overijssel) and of a patrician house near Zuilen (Utrecht).

name: Daalwijkdreef
en: The name of a farmstead in Markelo (Overijssel) and of a patrician house near Zuilen (Utrecht).

name: Daam van Harenstraat
en: A captain of the Beggars' fleet at the capture of Den Briel.

name: Daan Roodenburghplein
en: Architect (1885-1972) who designed Ajax's 'De Meer' stadium on the Middenweg, demolished in 1996. He also designed a great deal in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Dachstein
en: A mountain peak in Austria, 1995 metres high.

name: Dadelpalmstraat
en: A kind of palm. The date palm has been planted on a large scale for thousands of years for its edible fruit, the dates.

name: Dadelstraat
en: The fruit of the date palm.

name: Daelenbroek
en: An eighteenth-century castle near Herkenbosch (Limburg). One wing remains, in use as a house.

name: Dageraadsbrug
en: This fixed bridge is named after the former shipyard 'De Dageraad' (the dawn) nearby.

name: Daguerrestraat
en: Louis-Jacques Mandé Daguerre (1787-1851), French photographer. In 1837 he invented the daguerreotype, named after him, a method (a photographic image on a silvered plate) by which photographs could be developed on a large scale, making him one of the founders of photography.

name: Dalsteindreef
en: A manor house near Rheden (Gelderland).

name: Daltonstraat
en: John Dalton (1766-1844), English chemist and physicist, founder of atomic theory.

name: Dam
en: The dam laid in the river Amstel here between 1204 and 1275, to which Amsterdam owes its name. Originally there were two squares. The dam proper was called the Middeldam. The western part (on the Palace side) was called the Plaetse until the sixteenth century. By the seventeenth century both squares were already seen as one and called the Dam. In 1795 the name was changed to Revolutieplein, and in Napoleon's time to Napoleonplein. After 1813 the name Dam returned. Part of the Dam on the Bijenkorf side was called the Vissersdam (after the fish market), and the part on the Rokin side was then the Vijgendam. The names Vissersdam and Vijgendam were abolished in 1957, when part of the Warmoesstraat was also added to the Dam.

name: Damloperspad
en: A cargo ship with leeboards, similar to a tjalk.

name: Damrak
en: Rak is the old name for a straight stretch of waterway. So here it is the rak, or channel, to the Dam, narrowed on its west side during the eighteenth century. When the road or quay was built (in 1526), the name of the water passed to it. The houses on the Warmoesstraat between the Nieuwebrugsteeg and the Beurs are still called the houses 'aan 't Water' (on the water).

name: Damrak
en: Rak is the old name for a straight stretch of waterway. So here it is the rak, or channel, to the Dam, narrowed on its west side during the eighteenth century. When the road or quay was built (in 1526), the name of the water passed to it. The houses on the Warmoesstraat between the Nieuwebrugsteeg and the Beurs are still called the houses 'aan 't Water' (on the water).

name: Damstraat
en: The street that runs to the Dam. The name was given to the Halsteeg once its widening was finished. The name Halsteeg recalls the Vleeshal (meat hall), which stood on the corner of the Nes in the sixteenth century.

name: Danie Theronstraat
en: Army commander (1869-1900) under General De Wet in the Boer War of 1899-1902. He was killed by a shell.

name: Daniël de Langestraat
en: Musician (1841-1918) who composed symphonies and cantatas. One of the founders, and director, of the Amsterdam Conservatory.

name: Daniël Defoelaan
en: British novelist and satirist (1660-1731). His best-known book is still 'Robinson Crusoe'.

name: Daniël Goedkoopstraat
en: First director of the Nederlandsche Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (Netherlands Shipbuilding Company) (1850-1929).

name: Daniël Stalpertstraat
en: Daniël Stalpaert (1615-1684), architect and draughtsman. He completed the city hall on the Dam designed by Jacob van Campen. As city architect he also designed, among others, the Admiralty building on Kattenburg (now the Maritime Museum), the Oosterkerk, the church on the Amstelveld, the synagogue on the corner of the Nieuwe Amstelstraat and the Huiszittenweduwenhof. As a surveyor he made a map of Amsterdam's fourth expansion.

name: Dantestraat
en: Dante Alighieri (1265-1321), Italian poet, whose works include 'La Divina Comedia', still regarded as a masterpiece.

name: Danzigerbocht
en: The city of Danzig (now Gdańsk), an important timber port on the Baltic. Originally a so-called Free City, later German, and a Polish city since 1945.

name: Danzigerkade
en: The city of Danzig (now Gdańsk), an important timber port on the Baltic. Originally a so-called Free City, later German, and a Polish city since 1945.

name: Dapperplein
en: Olfert Dapper (1636-1689), physician in Amsterdam. In 1663 he produced a historical description of the city of Amsterdam.

name: Dapperstraat
en: Olfert Dapper (1636-1689), physician in Amsterdam. In 1663 he produced a historical description of the city of Amsterdam.

name: Darlingstraat
en: A river in South Australia, named after a nineteenth-century governor of New South Wales, Sir Ralph Darling.

name: Darwinplantsoen
en: Charles Darwin (1809-1882), English naturalist, known for his theory of descent and evolution.

name: Daveren
en: The English port of Dover, in a spelling found on Dutch sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: David Blesstraat
en: Painter and etcher (1821-1899), mainly of little scenes from domestic life.

name: David Humehof
en: English philosopher (1711-1776), a forerunner of Kant. Also known as a historian.

name: David Kouwenaarstraat
en: Journalist (1876-1957), editor at the 'Nieuwe Rotterdamse Courant' and chairman of the 'Amsterdamse Pers'. Author of 'Amsterdam, kroondraagster van Europa' (Amsterdam, crown-bearer of Europe) and 'Tussen Dam en Muntplein'.

name: David Ricardostraat
en: British economist (1772-1823) of Dutch descent, known for his theories on how wages and value are determined.

name: David Vosstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1899-1944), born in Amsterdam, died in Auschwitz (Poland).

name: David Wijnkoopstraat
en: Politician (1876-1941) of Jewish descent. He played an important part in the railway strike of 1903. Originally a member of the SDAP, in 1909 he founded the Social Democratic Party (later the Communist Party). He was a city councillor from 1919 to 1940, and also a member of the House of Representatives from 1918 to 1925 and from 1929 to 1940. He died at the address where he was in hiding.

name: Davisstraat
en: John Davis (1550-1605), English navigator. In 1585 he discovered the east coast of Greenland and the Davis Strait, named after him.

name: De Alpen
en: The mountain range, lying in France, Germany, Switzerland, Austria and Italy.

name: De Arendbrug
en: One of the two locomotives that pulled the opening train on the first railway line in the Netherlands on 25 September 1839. The departure point was in today's Westerpark; the terminus was Haarlem. De Arend (the eagle) was taken out of service after 1857 and scrapped; in 1938 a replica was built, which now stands in the Railway Museum in Utrecht.

name: De Bazelhof
en: Karel P.C. de Bazel (1869-1923), architect and pupil of Pierre Cuypers. His buildings include the Nederlandsche Handel-Maatschappij building on the Vijzelstraat and the (former) Maritime Museum on the Cornelis Schuytstraat. A pioneer of public housing.

name: De Biezenhof
en: A historical name found on a seventeenth-century map of Sloten/Osdorp.

name: De Bleeckster
en: A whaler of the late seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries that sailed from Oostzanerwerf.

name: De Boelegracht
en: Gerrit de Boele, bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland (1354/55).

name: De Boelelaan
en: Gerrit de Boele, bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland (1354/55).

name: De Borcht
en: The sixteenth-century castle near Baarlo (Limburg), with fifteenth-century remains. In 1473 the castle was taken by Charles the Bold.

name: De Breekstraat
en: After the lake next to it, the Schellingwouder Breek, formed after a breach in the Waterland sea dike. Breek means the same as braak (a pool formed after a dike breach).

name: De Clercqstraat
en: Willem de Clercq (1795-1844), man of letters, one of the leading figures of the 'Réveil' (a Protestant revival movement), and also director of the Nederlandsche Handel-Maatschappij. The road was laid over the former Bleekerssloot.

name: De corridor
en: A corridor is literally a strip of land between two areas. The road connects the shopping area around the Arena with Bijlmer station.

name: De Cuserstraat
en: Willem de Cuser, bailiff of Amstelland, Waterland and Rijnland in 1326/1327. Murdered by the Hook (Hoekse) nobles in 1392.

name: De Duifbrug
en: Named after the church De Duif (the dove) at Prinsengracht 754, officially called the Sint Willibrordus binnen de Veste.

name: De Duikerstraat
en: In general a water-management term for a culvert (duiker) that lets water pass under a road or dam. On an old map of Rijnland the name 'den Duycker' appears in the area of old Sloten/Osdorp.

name: De Egmondenstraat
en: The Noord-Holland places Egmond-Binnen, Egmond aan Zee and Egmond aan den Hoef.

name: De entree
en: The street (the entrance) leads to the nearby Amsterdam ArenA.

name: De Genestetstraat
en: Petrus Augustus de Genestet (1829-1861), Remonstrant minister and poet, known above all for his 'Lekedichtjes' (lay poems).

name: De Groene Zoom
en: Named after its layout, a strip of park with paths (the green edge).

name: De Heusweg
en: Probably named after the De Heus family of millers, who later founded the animal-feed company.

name: De Kempenaerstraat
en: Jacob Mattheus de Kempenaer (1793-1870), liberal statesman. Minister of the Interior (1848-1849). He helped draft the constitution adopted in 1848.

name: De Klencke
en: A moated country house from around 1740 in Oosterhesselen (Drenthe). Another havezate (a manor with noble rights) stood here earlier, of which a wall-anchor date of 1670 and a tombstone from 1635 remain.

name: De Kluftstraat
en: The name of the café that stood on this spot from 1857 to 1965. 'Kluft' is a Noord-Holland word for a ramp up or down a dike.

name: De la Reijstraat
en: Jacobus Hercules de la Rey (1847-1914), called Oom Koos (Uncle Koos). A Boer general in the Boers' war of independence against the British. He opposed Louis Botha's policy in 1914 and was shot dead in Johannesburg during a police action.

name: De la Sallestraat
en: Jean-Baptiste de La Salle (1651-1719), a Frenchman, founder of the congregation of the 'Brothers of the Christian Schools'.

name: De Lairessestraat
en: Gerard de Lairesse (1641-1711), painter of allegories and of wall and ceiling paintings. He came to Amsterdam from Liège in 1667. His 'Groot schilderboek' (great book of painting) appeared in 1707.

name: De Leek
en: De Leek is a lake in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: De Leeuw van Vlaanderenstraat
en: After the novel of the same name (the Lion of Flanders) by the Flemish writer Hendrik Conscience (1838).

name: De Leggende Osstraat
en: A historical stolp farmhouse on the Kadoelenweg, rebuilt in 1983. 'Leggen' is colloquial here for liggen (to lie): the lying ox.

name: De Lierhof
en: Together with the villages of 's-Gravenzande, Heenweg, Honselersdijk, Kwintsheul, Maasdijk, Monster, Naaldwijk, Ter Heijde and Wateringen, De Lier is part of the municipality of Westland in Zuid-Holland, formed on 1 January 2004.

name: De loper
en: A loper (runner): a long narrow carpet laid out to welcome someone. The street leads to the nearby Amsterdam ArenA.

name: De Mirandalaan
en: Salomon (Monne) Rodrigues de Miranda (1875-1942), for 28 years a city councillor for the SDAP, sixteen of them as an alderman of Amsterdam, among other things for public housing. Murdered by the occupiers in a punishment camp.

name: De passage
en: The street (the entrance) leads to the nearby Amsterdam ArenA.

name: De Peerelstraat
en: A former farmstead in the Watergraafsmeer. It lay next to Zorgwijk on the Oosterringdijk.

name: De Rijpgracht
en: Jan Cornelisz de Rijp (1570-1630), navigator, who sailed at the same time as Heemskerk and Barentsz in search of a northern passage, but did not winter on Nova Zembla because he took a route around Spitsbergen. When the street was laid out, the council of the former municipality of Sloten named it Willem Barentsstraat (council decision of Sloten, 8 March 1910).

name: De Rijpstraat
en: Jan Cornelisz de Rijp (1570-1630), navigator, who sailed at the same time as Heemskerk and Barentsz in search of a northern passage, but did not winter on Nova Zembla because he took a route around Spitsbergen. When the street was laid out, the council of the former municipality of Sloten named it Willem Barentsstraat (council decision of Sloten, 8 March 1910).

name: De Roos van Dekamaweg
en: A historical novel by Jacob van Lennep from 1836, set in the fourteenth century.

name: De Ruijterkade
en: Michiel Adriaansz. de Ruyter (1607-1676), the renowned admiral of Holland and West Friesland. He was born in Vlissingen. In Amsterdam he lived on what is now the Prins Hendrikkade.

name: De Savornin Lohmanstraat
en: Alexander F. de Savornin Lohman (1837-1924), lawyer and statesman, at first Anti-Revolutionary and, after a conflict with Abraham Kuyper, Christian-Historical. Professor at the Vrije Universiteit and Minister of the Interior from 1890 to 1895.

name: De Schaapherderstraat
en: A historical novel from 1838 by J.F. Oltmans (the shepherd), about the Utrecht War of 1481-1483.

name: De Schorrenstraat
en: A nature reserve on the east side of Texel, where birds such as the spoonbill, eider and oystercatcher breed. Schorren are silted-up, vegetated stretches of land outside the dikes that no longer flood at ordinary high tide (salt marshes).

name: De Sitterstraat
en: Willem de Sitter (1872-1934), astronomer. Professor at Leiden and director of the Leiden Observatory. He wrote a study of the expanding universe.

name: De Tourton Bruynsstraat
en: Titus Willem de Tourton Bruyns (1898-1943), resistance fighter, born in Teteringen, died in the German extermination camp Buchenwald.

name: De Wieden
en: The Beulaker Wiede and the Belter Wiede, the lake district in north-west Overijssel between Giethoorn and Vollenhove.

name: De Wittenkade
en: The brothers Cornelis de Witt (1623-1672), burgomaster of Dordrecht, and Johan de Witt (1625-1672), Grand Pensionary of Holland, both murdered by the mob in The Hague on a false accusation. One side of the quay was first called Maljapenkade.

name: De Wittenstraat
en: The brothers Cornelis de Witt (1623-1672), burgomaster of Dordrecht, and Johan de Witt (1625-1672), Grand Pensionary of Holland, both murdered by the mob in The Hague on a false accusation. One side of the quay was first called Maljapenkade.

name: De-Grote-Geusplein
en: The nickname (the great Beggar) of Count Hendrik van Brederode (1531-1568), leader of the procession of the Nobles in 1566 and one of the first leaders in the Eighty Years' War against Spain.

name: Deccaweg
en: The Decca system is a navigation aid used in shipping and aviation. It is based on measuring the difference in arrival time of radio signals sent out simultaneously by two stations.

name: Dekschuitstraat
en: A flat-bottomed vessel with cargo space only on deck (a deck barge).

name: Del Court van Krimpenstraat
en: Golfer (1889-1944), the founder of golf in the Netherlands.

name: Delflandlaan
en: A water board (hoogheemraadschap) in Zuid-Holland, bordering Rijnland and Schieland.

name: Delflandplein
en: A water board (hoogheemraadschap) in Zuid-Holland, bordering Rijnland and Schieland.

name: Delistraat
en: A region on the east coast of Sumatra (Indonesia), long known for growing tobacco. Its capital is Medan.

name: Deltastraat
en: A delta is the land at the mouth of a river where it flows into the sea in two or more arms. The word comes from the Greek letter delta, which has the shape of a triangle.

name: Demerarastraat
en: A river in South America, along which the Dutch colony of the same name arose early in the seventeenth century. In 1814 the area passed to the United Kingdom, and in 1831 it became part of British Guiana.

name: Demerhof
en: A river in Belgium.

name: Den Brielstraat
en: In 1572 Den Briel was the first city the Beggars (geuzen) took from the Spanish.

name: Den Burgstraat
en: The main town of the Wadden island of Texel.

name: Den Helderstraat
en: The town on the northern tip of Noord-Holland.

name: Den Texstraat
en: Jonkheer Cornelis Jacob Arnold den Tex (1824-1882), burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1868 to 1879.

name: Denderhof
en: A river in Belgium.

name: Dennenhof
en: A conifer (the pine). The native Scots pine is by far the most common species in the Netherlands.

name: Dennenrodepad
en: A farm near Grubbenvorst (Limburg). Rode is an old word for clearing woodland; compare the verb rooien (to grub up), still in use.

name: Derde Egelantiersdwarsstraat
en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

name: Derde Goudsbloemdwarsstraat
en: The flower (the marigold), of the daisy family.

name: Derde Helmersstraat
en: Jan Frederik Helmers (1767-1813), Amsterdam broker who devoted himself to letters. His works include 'De Hollandsche Natie' (1813). The second part of the Eerste Helmersstraat lay in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel until 1896 and was then called Hofdijkstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 9 May 1890). The start of this street was originally a short side street of the Nassaukade called Sophiapark.

name: Derde Hugo de Grootstraat
en: Humanist (1584-1645), founder of international law. As a leader of the Remonstrants he was drawn into church disputes and imprisoned at Loevestein on the orders of Prince Maurice. He escaped from there in a book chest in 1621.

name: Derde Kostverlorenkade
en: After the Kostverlorenwetering, dug in 1413 to give a shorter waterway to the Haarlem and Leiden lakes. According to some, the name Kostverloren (cost lost) comes from the heavy legal costs of this channel, which was a bone of contention between Amsterdam and Haarlem until 1609. The name Kostverloren occurs in several places in the Netherlands.

name: Derde Leliedwarsstraat
en: All these streets are named after the oldest of them, the Oude Leliestraat, already mentioned in 1560. It takes its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' (in the white lily) on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Torensluis). After 1612 the name passed to the canal dug in line with it, and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets in the Jordaan.

name: Derde Looiersdwarsstraat
en: The tanneries and the hide trade, after which this street and nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal ring are named, were at first sited outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came inside the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after these long-flourishing trades, starting with the Runstraat (run is tanbark) and the Huidenstraat (hides street). After 1658 the tanneries spread to land east of the Vijzelgracht, where the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat are now. Before it was filled in, the Derde Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision of 1 June 1898).

name: Derde Marnixdwarsstraat
en: Philips of Marnix, Lord of Sint-Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and adviser of Prince William of Orange, drafter of the Compromise of Nobles (1568) and possibly the poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was laid out after 1850 where the city ramparts had stood, which were levelled between 1820 and 1840.

name: Derde Oosterparkstraat
en: Named after the nearby Oosterpark, and originally (council decision of 15 November 1882) named Eerste, Tweede and Derde Parkstraat. The Eerste Oosterparkstraat was earlier called Oetgenspad, after Frans Hendriks Oetgens, a sixteenth-century burgomaster over whose land several paths were laid. Until 1895 the street name applied as far as the Linnaeusstraat. In that year the stretch along the park was given the park's name.

name: Derde Schinkelstraat
en: A schinkel is a short connecting stretch between two weteringen (drainage channels), in this case the Nieuwe Meer and the Overtoom. It is thought the connection owes its name to its shape: 'schinkel' is a synonym of 'schenkel', the lower leg between foot and knee. The quay was earlier called Visserkade by Nieuwer-Amstel. The municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel had named the streets Visserstraat, Alexanderstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 20 October 1882) and Willemsparkstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 30 January 1883), but in 1896 they were changed because of confusion with names that already existed in Amsterdam.

name: Derde Vogelstraat
en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

name: Derde Weteringdwarsstraat
en: The streets lie in the Weteringbuurt. The names recall the Wetering, which originally flowed from outside into the Spui; the Boerenwetering is a remnant of it. The Schans was once the rampart on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century the walls and ramparts were demolished. Parts were turned into promenades (Eerste and Tweede Weteringplantsoen), and a road was built that was at first called the Schans along its whole length but later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat. The Nieuwe Weteringstraat was laid out on the site freed by the demolition of the flour and bread factory. In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries this was the paving yard.

name: Derde Wittenburgerdwarsstraat
en: One of the three eastern islands (with Kattenburg and Oostenburg), laid out in the second half of the seventeenth century and built up with shipyards and houses from the start. One of the first yards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. This is very probably where the name Wittenburg comes from.

name: Derkinderenstraat
en: Antonius Johannes Derkinderen (1859-1925), painter, known for his murals (the city hall in Den Bosch) and book decoration. Director of the Rijksakademie van Beeldende Kunsten (State Academy of Fine Arts).

name: Des Présstraat
en: Josquin des Prés or Després (1450-1521), French composer and choirmaster (masses and chansons).

name: Descartespad
en: René Descartes (1596-1650), also called Cartesius. French philosopher, natural scientist and mathematician, founder of modern philosophy. From 1629 to 1649 he lived on the Westermarkt (no. 6).

name: Descartesstraat
en: René Descartes (1596-1650), also called Cartesius. French philosopher, natural scientist and mathematician, founder of modern philosophy. From 1629 to 1649 he lived on the Westermarkt (no. 6).

name: Desselstraat
en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

name: Deurloostraat
en: One of the Zeeland sea inlets, at the mouth of the Westerschelde.

name: Develstein
en: The name of a manor house in Heerjansdam (Zuid-Holland).

name: Dever
en: A castle from about 1400 near Lisse (Zuid-Holland), of which the ruin of a massive semicircular tower remains. A manor house was built against it in the seventeenth century.

name: Deymanstraat
en: Jan Deyman (1620-1666), professor of anatomy in Amsterdam. The street was earlier called Tweede Boerhaavestraat (council decision of 15 November 1882).

name: Diaconessenbrug
en: From 1884, for more than 100 years, a hospital stood very near this bridge: the LDI, the Lutherse Diaconessen Inrichting (Lutheran Deaconess Institution). The deaconesses, who were responsible for nursing the sick, mostly also lived in the building at Koninginneweg 1.

name: Diamantstraat
en: The hardest and most precious gemstone. Why this and other gemstones were used for names in the neighbourhood cannot be traced. It may be assumed that it was because of Asscher's diamond-cutting works, based in the Tolstraat since 1907. The street came over from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel under the name Eerste De Ruyterdwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 30 September 1890).

name: Diatomastraat
en: A microscopic water creature: one of the diatoms, a siliceous alga.

name: Dichtershofje
en: A reference to the overall theme of the street names in the neighbourhood (poets' courtyard). Many eighteenth- and nineteenth-century poets and writers in particular are commemorated in the immediate surroundings of this courtyard.

name: Dick Greinerstraat
en: Architect (1891-1964). His work includes the centre of Betondorp in Amsterdam's Watergraafsmeer, built in the 1920s. After the war he helped rebuild Middelburg and Ierseke.

name: Dick Hilleniuspad
en: Biologist, essayist and poet (1927-1987). All three sides can always be recognised in his wide-ranging work. He wrote about travel and art, among other things.

name: Dick Schmüllbrug
en: Diederich Herman 'Dick' Schmüll (Sumatra, 1908 - Amsterdam, 1990) founded the Dutch Basketball Federation and the Dutch Volleyball Federation.

name: Dickenslaan
en: Charles John Huffam Dickens (1812-1870), English novelist. His work exposes social abuses, for example in 'Oliver Twist'. Author of the famous Christmas story 'A Christmas Carol'.

name: Diderotstraat
en: Denis Diderot (1713-1784), French philosopher who, with d'Alembert among others, compiled an encyclopaedia of 35 volumes from 1749.

name: Diemerbospad
en: The Diemerbospad is a cycle path between the Brasapark in Amsterdam Zuidoost and the Diemerbos in the municipality of Diemen.

name: Diemerparklaan
en: Named after the village of Diemen. The park is managed ecologically and links the nature areas on the south and north sides of the IJmeer.

name: Diemerzeedijk
en: This dike, only partly in Amsterdam, runs from Zeeburg past the village of Diemen to Muiderberg. It was built as early as the fourteenth century to hold back the water of the Zuiderzee. Before the Watergraafsmeer or Diemermeer was drained, the dike was Amsterdam's only link with Muiden and the area beyond.

name: Diepen
en: A corrupted spelling of the French port of Dieppe, as found on sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Diepenbeekplantsoen
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Diepenbrockstraat
en: Alphonsus Joannes Maria Diepenbrock (1862-1921), a composer of international standing who wrote mainly church music.

name: Dierenriem
en: The zodiac: the belt of the sun and planets in the sky. In ancient times the zodiac was fixed as twelve signs (constellations) at equal distances.

name: Diezestraat
en: A river in Noord-Brabant formed where the Dommel and the Aa flow together.

name: Digitaalstraat
en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

name: Dijkbraak
en: Named after the wiel (a pool formed by a dike breach or left behind after a flood) inside the Oostzanerdijk, west of the Zuideinde towards Oostzaan. Braak is a Noord-Holland word for wiel.

name: Dijkdwarsstraat
en: The street was laid out as a dike at the end of the sixteenth century, after which the surroundings (long a marsh) were filled in with earth (aangeplempt).

name: Dijkgraafplein
en: A dijkgraaf (dike reeve) is the chairman of a dike board or water board.

name: Dijkmanshuizenstraat
en: A polder on the Wadden island of Texel, north of Oudeschild, now a nature reserve.

name: Dijkmeerlaan
en: The name is based on former country estates along the Amstel and in the Watergraafsmeer.

name: Dijkmeerstraat
en: The name is based on former country estates along the Amstel and in the Watergraafsmeer.

name: Dijksgracht
en: The street was laid out as a dike at the end of the sixteenth century, after which the surroundings (long a marsh) were filled in with earth (aangeplempt).

name: Dijksgracht
en: Named after the water of the same name, which runs along the inside of the railway embankment here. The embankment originally closed off the Oosterdok from the IJ, which was then still open.

name: Dijkstraat
en: The street was laid out as a dike at the end of the sixteenth century, after which the surroundings (long a marsh) were filled in with earth (aangeplempt).

name: Dijkwater
en: A nature reserve between Duiveland and Dreischor (Zeeland): a dammed tidal creek with its banks.

name: Dijkwegpad
en: An old local name from this part of Rijnland.

name: Dijlehof
en: A river in Belgium.

name: Dijsselhofplantsoen
en: Gerrit Willem Dijsselhof (1866-1924), impressionist painter. For some years the park was first called Breitnerplantsoen (council decision of 22 April 1925).

name: Dikninge
en: Originally an old abbey (1325-1602), now a late Empire-style country house on the Reest near De Wijk (Drenthe). Gateposts from 1817.

name: Dilbeekpad
en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

name: Dillestraat
en: A plant of the carrot family (dill), widely used as a kitchen herb in the northern half of Europe.

name: Dilsenstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Dina Appeldoornstraat
en: Christina Adriana Arendina Koudijs, née Van Appeldoorn (1884-1938), composer of chamber music and symphonic poems. She also composed Dutch dances and a suite for orchestra.

name: Dinarpromenade
en: A currency of the Arab world and the Balkans.

name: Dintelstraat
en: A river in Noord-Brabant that flows into the Volkerak at Dinteloord.

name: Diopter
en: Pseudonym of Arie Keppler (1876-1941); literally a spy, or also a sight (on a gun). The first director of Amsterdam's Municipal Housing Department (1915-1936), a great champion and promoter of social housing. The garden villages in Noord, among others, were built under his leadership.

name: Diponegorostraat
en: Diponegoro (Yogyakarta 1785 - Makassar 1855). The aristocrat Diponegoro, a 'prince' of a Javanese principality, led the Javanese uprising against Dutch colonial rule in the Java War (1825-1830). Dutch authority wavered, but won in the end. The fighting may have cost more than 200,000 lives. Diponegoro was exiled to Celebes. He is one of Indonesia's greatest 'national heroes'.

name: Dirhampad
en: In the Valutabuurt (currency neighbourhood) of Nieuw-West an unnamed cycle path runs parallel to the Guldenpromenade. It is named after the Moroccan currency, the dirham, which gives this important cycle path the name Dirhampad.

name: Dirk Bonsstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1897-1945), born in Brandwijk, executed by firing squad at Zijpersluis.

name: Dirk de Waterduikerbrug
en: Dirk Rietveldt (1858-1940) rescued many people (perhaps as many as 74), dogs and cats from the water of Amsterdam's canals. That made him a highly respected figure in the Jordaan, and he received several medals from the city of Amsterdam for humanity. In the immediate surroundings of this bridge, three courtyards are named after men who also rescued many from drowning: Doris Rijkers, Jan Cupido and Frans Naerebout.

name: Dirk Deutekompad
en: Resistance fighter (1895-1945), member of the clandestine CPN. Arrested in July 1944 for helping Jews and transported to the Neuengamme/Buchenwald camp, where he died on 20 April 1945. In the camp he looked after a group of Jewish children, all of whom were hanged by the camp command.

name: Dirk Hartoghstraat
en: Navigator who discovered the west coast of Australia in 1616.

name: Dirk Schäferstraat
en: Composer and pianist (1873-1931), a great interpreter of Chopin.

name: Dirk Sonoystraat
en: Diederick van Sonoy. Leader of the Sea Beggars (1529-1597), a nobleman who had fled Germany, sided with Prince William of Orange and was appointed governor of West-Friesland. Under Prince Maurice he fell into disgrace.

name: Dirk van Hasseltssteeg
en: (Fragment belonging to the Dirk de Waterduikerbrug) the Jordaan, and he received several medals from the city of Amsterdam for humanity. In the immediate surroundings of this bridge, three courtyards are named after men who also rescued many from drowning: Doris Rijkers, Jan Cupido and Frans Naerebout.

name: Dirk Vreekenstraat
en: A participant in the February Strike of 1941.

name: Dirk Wittehof
en: A merchant by trade (1884-1932), and in his spare time a writer of sentimental songs (levensliedjes), which Pisuisse sang with great success.

name: Dirkshornplantsoen
en: A village south of Schagen (Noord-Holland).

name: Discusstraat
en: A throwing disc, used in discus throwing at the Greek and Roman games.

name: Disketteweg
en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

name: Displaystraat
en: As a counterpart to the street names recalling Amsterdam-Noord's former shipbuilding industry, this name refers to modern information technology.

name: Distelachterstraat
en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

name: Distelhaven
en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

name: Distelkade
en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

name: Distelkruisstraat
en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

name: Distelplein
en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

name: Distelvoorstraat
en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

name: Distelweg
en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

name: Ditlaar
en: The former farmstead of the dike reeve Ellard Ditelaar, which stood in the eighteenth century between the village of Sloten and the Slotermeer.

name: Djakartaterras
en: Also Jakarta (formerly Batavia), the capital of the Republic of Indonesia. This stretch of street was made by a break in the row of façades.

name: Djambistraat
en: A town and old residency on the east coast of Sumatra (Indonesia).

name: Doblijn
en: A corrupted spelling of the Irish port and capital Dublin, as found on sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Docklandsweg
en: A former industrial port area on the Thames in south-east London, redeveloped since the 1980s into an area for living and working. Also a district of Dublin where large-scale renewal projects have begun.

name: Doddendaal
en: A castle near Ewijk (Gelderland), probably founded in the eleventh or twelfth century. The name Doddendaal dates from 1379. The building has been altered many times. In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries its cellar served as a church for Roman Catholics.

name: Doelensluis
en: This fixed bridge takes its name from the Kloveniersdoelen. The doelen were the places where the civic militia guilds met and practised shooting at a target (doel). These doelen had their seat by the tower Swych Utrecht (where the Doelen Hotel is now). They practised on the grounds of the Old Convent of the Nuns (the Binnengasthuis site).

name: Doggersbankstraat
en: A shoal in the North Sea where in 1781 the Dutch admiral Zoutman inflicted a defeat on the British fleet.

name: Doggerstraat
en: A ship that takes its name from the place where it went fishing, the Dogger Bank. The dogger fished for herring and cod, among other things.

name: Dokter Meurerlaan
en: Rudolf J.Th. Meurer (1866-1950), Amsterdam doctor, a very well-known rowing official and for many years coach of 'Nereus'. He promoted the Bosbaan (rowing course) and founded the Amsterdam Medical Sports Examination Bureau.

name: Dolfijnhof
en: A constellation (the Dolphin).

name: Dolhaantjestraat
en: The nickname of Adrianus van Berques, a Walloon nobleman who served the Sea Beggars as admiral. He was killed in Hainaut in 1572.

name: Dolingadreef
en: A state in Grou (Friesland). State is a Frisian word for a farmstead.

name: Dollardpad
en: A nature reserve in the arm of the Wadden Sea between Groningen and Germany. The area was formed in the Middle Ages.

name: Dom H. van der Laanstraat
en: Dom van der Laan (1904-1991), architect and Benedictine monk. In 1925, with fellow students at the Technische Hogeschool in Delft, he founded the 'Bouwkundige Studiekring' (architecture study circle), which often met at the home of Granpré Molière, the founder of the Delft School.

name: Domela Nieuwenhuisstraat
en: Ferdinand Domela Nieuwenhuis (1846-1919), Lutheran minister who left the church in 1879. A Dutch popular leader, pioneer of socialism in the Netherlands and founder of the Social Democratic League. Member of the House of Representatives from 1888 to 1891. He went from socialist to anarchist, which led to a break with Troelstra and his associates. The park was laid out on the site of the Maria Magdalenakerk, demolished in 1968. Nearby, on the Nassauplein, stands his statue, made by the sculptor Johan Polet in 1931.

name: Domenico Scarlattilaan
en: Italian composer (1685-1757), choirmaster in Rome and harpsichordist at the Spanish court, who composed more than five hundred works for keyboard.

name: Domselaerstraat
en: Tobias van Domselaer (1611-1685), historian. He compiled his 'Beschrijving van Amsterdam' (description of Amsterdam), published in 1665, from notes by Cornelis Dapper and Pontanus.

name: Don Boscostraat
en: Italian priest (1815-1888) who devoted his whole life to educating neglected young people.

name: Donarstraat
en: The Germanic god of thunder.

name: Donauweg
en: The second-longest river in Europe (the Danube). It rises in the Black Forest and flows into the Black Sea.

name: Dongestraat
en: A small river in Noord-Brabant.

name: Donker Curtiusstraat
en: Dirk Donker Curtius (1792-1864), liberal statesman, at first a journalist. He campaigned for revision of the constitution and was later Minister of Justice. He was responsible for the laws on ministerial responsibility and on the right of association.

name: Doornburg
en: The Doornenburgh, a seventeenth-century house on the Vecht near Maarssen, altered in 1721 and again in the twentieth century. (Not to be confused with Doornenburg castle in the Betuwe.)

name: Dora Tamanaplein
en: South African resistance fighter (1901-1983), very active in the women's movement. A member of the women's wing of the African National Congress (ANC) and one of the leading figures of the Federation of South African Women.

name: Doris Lessingstraat
en: Doris Lessing (1919-2013) was a British writer.

name: Dorpsstraat Holysloot
en: A village, part of Amsterdam since 1921. The origin of the name is unknown; the village appears as early as 1288 under the name Hoolesloot.

name: Dorpsweg Ransdorp
en: The village of Ransdorp was an independent municipality until 1 January 1921, when the municipality, with its villages of Durgerdam, Holysloot and Schellingwoude, was added to Amsterdam.

name: Dortmuiden
en: This is the English port of Dartmouth, in a spelling found on Dutch sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Dorus Rijkershof
en: Coxswain of the lifeboat at Den Helder (1847-1928), who saved hundreds of shipwrecked people from death. The Dorus Rijkers Fund, which supports the families of lifeboatmen who die, is named after him.

name: Dostojevskisingel
en: Fyodor Mikhailovich Dostoevsky (1821-1881), one of the best-known Russian writers of the nineteenth century.

name: Dotterbloemstraat
en: The wild flower (marsh marigold), of the buttercup family.

name: Douwes Dekkerstraat
en: Eduard Douwes Dekker (1820-1887), pen name Multatuli. An Amsterdammer who went to the East Indies in 1838, where he became a colonial administrator, resigned after a conflict, and then devoted himself to writing. A forerunner of the Tachtigers (the Movement of the Eighties). His works include 'Max Havelaar' and 'Woutertje Pieterse'. The Multatuli Museum is in the house where he was born, on the Korsjespoortsteeg.

name: Dovenetelstraat
en: A plant genus (dead-nettle) of the mint family.

name: Dr. C.W. Ittmannpad
en: Cesar Willem Ittmann (1914-1945), assistant surgeon at the Binnengasthuis. He belonged to the Persoonsbewijzen-Centrale (identity card centre) group and the student resistance, and cared for sick and wounded resistance fighters. He took part in sabotage and was executed by firing squad at the former Rozenoord airfield on the Amstel.

name: Dr. E. Boekmanstraat
en: Emanuel Boekman (1889-1940), a leading social democrat and city councillor for the SDAP. From 1931 to 1940 he was alderman for education and the arts. His 1938 doctoral thesis 'Overheid en kunstbeleid' (government and arts policy) laid the foundations of post-war arts policy.

name: Dr. J.A. Ringersstraat
en: Johannes Aleidis Ringers (1885-1965), hydraulic engineer, director of Rijkswaterstaat and then an executive of the Indies railways. He was interned by the Germans during the war. After the war he was Minister of Public Works and Reconstruction in the Schermerhorn and Beel cabinets.

name: Dr. Jan van Breemenstraat
en: Jan Frans Leonard van Breemen (1874-1961), a pioneer in the fight against rheumatism. The Reumacentrum (rheumatism centre) was built on this street in 1965.

name: Dr. Samuel de Ranitzbrug
en: Doctor (1834-1913), in practice in Amsterdam from 1861. Moved by the wretched conditions of many sick Amsterdam children, in 1865 he decided to found what later became the Emma Children's Hospital. In 1873 the institution moved to the Sarphatistraat, not far from this bridge, where it stayed for 117 years.

name: Draaierweg
en: The trade name of a metal and wood worker (a turner).

name: Drachmesingel
en: The currency of Greece (the drachma).

name: Drakenstein
en: A knightly manor (ridderhofstede) near Lage Vuursche (Utrecht), from 1640.

name: Drie Burgpad
en: A former country estate on the ring dike of the Watergraafsmeer, now the Weesperzijde.

name: Driebanstraat
en: A polder in West-Friesland.

name: Driedistelstraat
en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

name: Drieharingenbrug
en: This drawbridge takes its name from the three herrings above the door of the house 'De Drie Haringen' (the three herrings) at Vierwindendwarsstraat no. 1.

name: Driehoekstraat
en: Laid out in the middle of the seventeenth century. The name (triangle street) comes from the shape of the street.

name: Driekoningenstraat
en: Named after a shop sign of the corner building on the Singel (the Three Kings). The name is mentioned as early as 1608. Before that the little street was called Lijnbaanstraat.

name: Driemondweg
en: After the village of Driemond, added to Amsterdam when the municipality of Weesperkarspel was abolished on 1 August 1966.

name: Drontermeerpad
en: One of the Veluwe border lakes (randmeren).

name: Droogbak
en: The name appears as early as the first half of the seventeenth century and probably comes from the drying of cloth by the cloth weavers.

name: Drostenburg
en: A farm south of Borculo (Gelderland).

name: Drs. P-brug
en: Drs. P (Thun, 24 August 1919 - Amsterdam, 13 June 2015), pseudonym of Heinz Hermann Polzer, was a Dutch-language lyricist of Swiss nationality. His stage name, thought up by Willem Duys, refers to the academic degree of doctorandus (abbreviated drs.) in economics that Polzer took at the Nederlandsche Economische Hoogeschool (now Erasmus University). He was also a poet, writer, cabaret artist, man of letters, composer, pianist and singer of his own songs.

name: Druivenbrug
en: The fruit (grapes), grown in the Netherlands as table grapes, in Germany, France, Spain and Italy for winemaking, and in Greece, Asia Minor and California for raisins.

name: Druivenstraat
en: The fruit (grapes), grown in the Netherlands as table grapes, in Germany, France, Spain and Italy for winemaking, and in Greece, Asia Minor and California for raisins.

name: Drusiushof
en: Joannes van den Driesche or Drusius (1550-1600), orientalist, professor in the Netherlands and England.

name: Du Perronstraat
en: Charles Edgar du Perron (1899-1940), poet, writer and critic. His works include 'Land van herkomst' (country of origin).

name: Duarte Pachecostraat
en: Portuguese navigator (died 1533), a contemporary of Columbus and Bartolomeu Dias. In 1488 he joined Dias on the island of Príncipe in the Atlantic Ocean, as Dias was returning from exploring the route to India around the Cape.

name: Dubbele Buurt
en: Originally entirely in the municipality of Haarlemmerliede en Spaarnwoude; since a boundary correction in 1963 part of it has been on Amsterdam territory.

name: Dubbelink
en: A farm north of Delden (Overijssel).

name: Dubbelinkdreef
en: A farm north of Delden (Overijssel).

name: Dubbelmondehof
en: A church village in the former Zuid-Hollandse Waard drowned in the St Elizabeth's flood of 1421.

name: Dudok de Withof
en: Corneille Abraham Adrien (Bram) Dudok de Wit (1841-1911), a champion of sport. Nicknamed the 'sports minister', he served as a race official at all sorts of competitions. At the exhibition games in Paris in 1900 (the second Olympiad) he was general delegate for the Netherlands. His brother L.C. Dudok de Wit (1843-1913), better known as Kees de Tippelaar (Kees the walker), became a symbol of recreational walking.

name: Dufaystraat
en: Guillaume Dufay (1400-1474), musician from Hainaut, a well-known fifteenth-century composer, mainly of masses.

name: Duffelhof
en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

name: Duinbeek
en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

name: Duindoornplein
en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

name: Duindoornstraat
en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

name: Duinluststraat
en: A nature reserve near Overveen/Bloemendaal, made up of woodland and dunes.

name: Duivelandstraat
en: The southern part of the Zeeland island of Schouwen-Duiveland.

name: Duivendrechtsekade
en: The village of Duivendrecht in the municipality of Ouder-Amstel. Duivendrecht comes from Doeve (a man's name) and drecht (a place where ships were hauled overland). When the Watergraafsmeer was still a lake, a ferry ran from where the village now lies to the far side, towards Oetewaal.

name: Duivendrechtselaan
en: The village of Duivendrecht in the municipality of Ouder-Amstel. Duivendrecht comes from Doeve (a man's name) and drecht (a place where ships were hauled overland). When the Watergraafsmeer was still a lake, a ferry ran from where the village now lies to the far side, towards Oetewaal.

name: Duivendrechtsevaart
en: The village of Duivendrecht in the municipality of Ouder-Amstel. Duivendrecht comes from Doeve (a man's name) and drecht (a place where ships were hauled overland). When the Watergraafsmeer was still a lake, a ferry ran from where the village now lies to the far side, towards Oetewaal.

name: Duizendschoonstraat
en: The ornamental plant (sweet william).

name: Duizendste Brug
en: On 2 April 1974 this bridge was opened as Amsterdam's thousandth bridge by alderman Han Lammers.

name: Dukdalfweg
en: Named after the wooden pile structure (a dolphin), made of an upright pile in the middle and about four raking piles, that stops ships from hitting the quayside. The word comes from Duc d'Alve, the unyielding Duke of Alba.

name: Duke Ellingtonstraat
en: Edward Kennedy (Duke) Ellington (1899-1974), American jazz composer, pianist, bandleader and arranger, known for his various styles, including jungle and mood.

name: Dulcie Septemberpad
en: Representative of the African National Congress (ANC) in France and Switzerland. She was murdered in Paris in April 1988 for her struggle against apartheid.

name: Dulongstraat
en: Pierre Dulong (1785-1838), French physicist and chemist. He discovered that the atomic heat is the same for all solid elements.

name: Durbanweg
en: A port city in South Africa. The street lies near the Afrikahaven in the western port area.

name: Durgerdammerdijk
en: Named after the village that belonged until 1921 to the municipality of Ransdorp, abolished that year. The name arose by corruption of the oldest name, IJdoringherdam: the dam at the corner of the IJ. (The polder outside the dike here has kept the name IJdoorn.) The Durgerdammerdijk is the stretch of the Waterland sea dike on which Durgerdam lies.

name: Durgerdammergouw
en: Named after the village that belonged until 1921 to the municipality of Ransdorp, abolished that year. The name arose by corruption of the oldest name, IJdoringherdam: the dam at the corner of the IJ. (The polder outside the dike here has kept the name IJdoorn.) The Durgerdammerdijk is the stretch of the Waterland sea dike on which Durgerdam lies.

name: Dusartstraat
en: Cornelis Dusart (1660-1704), painter and engraver, a pupil of Van Ostade.

name: Dwars Spinhuissteeg
en: After the nearby Spinhuis (spinning house), a house of correction for women founded in 1596. From 1833 to 1941 the building housed the police headquarters.

name: Dwarswatering
en: A former watercourse where the De Eendracht sports park is now.

name: Dwergpalmstraat
en: A kind of fan palm (dwarf palm). It is one of the few palms that also grows in Europe.

name: Dwergplanetenbaan
en: Planet-like bodies, larger than asteroids but smaller than planets. Unlike planets, they have not cleared their orbits of other objects. In our solar system Pluto, Eris, Makemake, Haumea and Ceres fall into the dwarf-planet category.

name: Dwergvinvisstraat
en: A cetacean (the minke whale).

name: Dynamostraat
en: A machine that turns mechanical power into electrical power.

name: Eastonstraat
en: Charles Easton (1864-1920), journalist and astronomer, editor-in-chief of 'Het Nieuws van den Dag'. He wrote several meteorological studies.

name: Echtenstein
en: A manor house in Emmen (Drenthe).

name: Eckeharthof
en: Meister E.J. Eckhart (1260-1329), German mystic, a Dominican friar whose teaching was condemned after his death.

name: Eclipshof
en: An eclipse is the darkening of a celestial body when it passes behind another or into its shadow.

name: Ecuplein
en: The European Currency Unit (ecu), the unit of account of the European Community, also used as a currency in its own right.

name: Edammerpad
en: Named after the Noord-Holland town (Edam).

name: Edammerstraat
en: Named after the Noord-Holland town (Edam).

name: Edenburg
en: A South African place name.

name: Edenville
en: A town in South Africa: a small farming town in the north of the Free State province.

name: Edisonstraat
en: Thomas Alva Edison (1847-1931), North American inventor of the microphone, the megaphone, the phonograph and the electric light bulb.

name: Edith Magnusstraat
en: Edith Magnus (1925-1993) belonged in the 1960s to the women's core group of the Nederlandse Vereniging tot Integratie van Homoseksualiteit (Dutch Association for the Integration of Homosexuality), today's COC. She organised the first women's national days, which meant a great deal to lesbian women.

name: Edmond Halleylaan
en: English astronomer (1656-1742), Fellow of the Royal Society, appointed 'Astronomer Royal' in 1731. He wrote on magnetism and published a chart of the Atlantic Ocean and a world map on which he improved the courses. A comet and an observatory are named after him.

name: Edmond Halleysteiger
en: English astronomer (1656-1742), Fellow of the Royal Society, appointed 'Astronomer Royal' in 1731. He wrote on magnetism and published a chart of the Atlantic Ocean and a world map on which he improved the courses. A comet and an observatory are named after him.

name: Edmund Gunterstraat
en: English astronomer (1581-1626), inventor of the pleinschaal (Gunter's scale), a kind of slide rule with logarithmic divisions. His scientific work dealt with navigation and its problems.

name: Eduard Hellendoornstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1912-1941), involved in the February Strike of 1941. One of the '18 dead of the Waalsdorpervlakte'.

name: Eduard Jacobshof
en: Amsterdam cabaret artist (1868-1914) who introduced the levenslied (the sentimental popular song) to the Netherlands.

name: Eduard Meijerstraat
en: Water polo and swimming champion (1878-1929).

name: Eduard van Beinumstraat
en: Eduard A. van Beinum (1901-1959), conductor of the Concertgebouw Orchestra from 1945 until his death, and also of the London Philharmonic Orchestra from 1949 to 1952.

name: Eduard Vetermanstraat
en: Man of letters, playwright and director (1901-1946). He adapted several of Timmermans's books for the stage.

name: Edumbe
en: A town in South Africa, in the province of KwaZulu-Natal.

name: Edward Masseystraat
en: English scientist who in 1802 developed the mechanical log, a device that shows a ship's speed. Between 1802 and 1848 he received six patents for various mechanical nautical instruments.

name: Edward Wrightstraat
en: English scholar (died 1615) whose findings were particularly important for navigation. In 1599 he published 'Certaine errors in navigation'.

name: Eef Kamerbeekstraat
en: Evert Kamerbeek (1934-2008), athlete, eleven times Dutch decathlon champion from 1954.

name: Eemlandstraat
en: A region in the north-east of the province of Utrecht, in the basin of the river Eem.

name: Eemsstraat
en: The sea inlet between Delfzijl and Germany (the mouth of the river Ems).

name: Eendenstraat
en: The water bird (the duck).

name: Eendrachtstraat
en: The water between Tholen and Noord-Brabant.

name: Eenhoornhof
en: A constellation (the Dolphin).

name: Eensgevonden
en: A South African place name.

name: Eerste Amstelvlietpad
en: Historic country house (estate) on the Amsteldijk. It was built after 1721 by Gerrit Nieuwenhuizen, who originally called it Meerhuizen. It has been known as Amstelvliet since 1784. It was demolished in or after 1916.

name: Eerste Anjeliersdwarsstraat
en: An anjelier (carnation) is a flower belonging to the pink family.

name: Eerste Atjehstraat
en: The northern part of the Indonesian island of Sumatra (Aceh), known above all for the Aceh War (1873-1904), with which the name of General Van Heutsz is linked.

name: Eerste Bloemdwarsstraat
en: Many streets and canals in the Jordaan are named after flowers. In this expansion of 1612, the Bloemgracht is probably the oldest canal. The canal ran to the Bolwerk de Bloem (later called Rijkeroord), after which it is named. From 1614 to 1878 the windmill 'De Blom' stood on the bastion; it was then moved to the Haarlemmerweg near the Nieuwpoortkade.

name: Eerste Boerhaavestraat
en: Hermannus Boerhaave (1668-1738), professor of medicine at Leiden, internationally renowned. The street name Boerhaavestraat (Eerste to Vierde) has changed quite often: set as Boerhaavestraat on 15 November 1876, changed to Eerste Boerhaavestraat on 15 November 1882, a change reversed on 10 December 1884. On 13 October 1897 the street was extended under the same name, and finally on 19 February 1908 it was split into today's Eerste and Tweede Boerhaavestraat. The Tweede, Derde and Vierde Boerhaavestraat named in 1882 were replaced by the names Deymanstraat, Ruyschstraat and Blasiusstraat.

name: Eerste Boomdwarsstraat
en: In this part of the Jordaan, streets are named after flowers, shrubs and trees. In the seventeenth century, the street was also called Lindeboomstraat.

name: Eerste Breeuwersstraat
en: A trade name. A breeuwer (caulker) sealed the seams between the planks of a ship's hull. In the seventeenth century many caulkers lived in the Eerste Breeuwersstraat (formerly Breeuwersstraat), working at the shipyards on the Prinseneiland and Realeneiland. In 1895 the parallel street was given the same name, which made the additions Eerste and Tweede necessary.

name: Eerste Ceramstraat
en: An island in Indonesia.

name: Eerste Coehoornstraat
en: Menno Baron van Coehoorn (1641-1704), fortress builder, engineer-general of fortifications.

name: Eerste Constantijn Huygensstraat
en: Poet and prose writer (1596-1687), whose works include 'Hofwijck' and epigrams (sneldichten). He was secretary to several successive stadholders. Before 1894 parts of these streets were called Eerste and Tweede Bilderdijkstraat (council decisions of 15 May 1878 and 19 December 1883).

name: Eerste Disteldwarsstraat
en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

name: Eerste Egelantiersdwarsstraat
en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

name: Eerste Goudsbloemdwarsstraat
en: The flower (the marigold), of the daisy family.

name: Eerste Helmersstraat
en: Jan Frederik Helmers (1767-1813), Amsterdam broker who devoted himself to letters. His works include 'De Hollandsche Natie' (1813). The second part of the Eerste Helmersstraat lay in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel until 1896 and was then called Hofdijkstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 9 May 1890). The start of this street was originally a short side street of the Nassaukade called Sophiapark.

name: Eerste Hugo de Grootstraat
en: Humanist (1584-1645), founder of international law. As a leader of the Remonstrants he was drawn into church disputes and imprisoned at Loevestein on the orders of Prince Maurice. He escaped from there in a book chest in 1621.

name: Eerste Jacob van Campenstraat
en: Architect (1595-1659), designer of the city hall on the Dam, now the Royal Palace, though he was not allowed to finish the work. Van Campen also built the Heiligewegspoort in 1636, and a palace in Rijswijk for Prince Frederik Hendrik in 1657. The split into Eerste and Tweede came after the stretch of street between them was sold to the Heineken brewery in 1930.

name: Eerste Jan Steenstraat
en: Painter (1626-1679), mostly of domestic scenes: merry, untidy interiors. That gave rise to the expression 'a Jan Steen household' (een huishouden van Jan Steen).

name: Eerste Jan van der Heijdenstraat
en: Painter and engineer (1637-1712), inventor of the fire engine with a hose and of a new model of street lamp. Painter of portraits and townscapes.

name: Eerste Keucheniusstraat
en: Levinus W.C. Keuchenius (1822-1893), Anti-Revolutionary statesman and fierce opponent of the state school. Minister of the Colonies from 1888 to 1890.

name: Eerste Kostverlorenkade
en: After the Kostverlorenwetering, dug in 1413 to give a shorter waterway to the Haarlem and Leiden lakes. According to some, the name Kostverloren (cost lost) comes from the heavy legal costs of this channel, which was a bone of contention between Amsterdam and Haarlem until 1609. The name Kostverloren occurs in several places in the Netherlands.

name: Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat
en: The southern European ornamental tree (the laurel).

name: Eerste Leeghwaterstraat
en: Jan Adriaanszoon Leeghwater (1575-1650), hydraulic engineer. As overseer and millwright he worked on many land reclamations, including the Beemster. He drew up the first plan to drain the Haarlemmermeer.

name: Eerste Leliedwarsstraat
en: All these streets are named after the oldest of them, the Oude Leliestraat, already mentioned in 1560. It takes its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' (in the white lily) on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Torensluis). After 1612 the name passed to the canal dug in line with it, and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets in the Jordaan.

name: Eerste Lindendwarsstraat
en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

name: Eerste Looiersdwarsstraat
en: The tanneries and the hide trade, after which this street and nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal ring are named, were at first sited outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came inside the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after these long-flourishing trades, starting with the Runstraat (run is tanbark) and the Huidenstraat (hides street). After 1658 the tanneries spread to land east of the Vijzelgracht, where the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat are now. Before it was filled in, the Derde Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision of 1 June 1898).

name: Eerste Marnixdwarsstraat
en: Philips of Marnix, Lord of Sint-Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and adviser of Prince William of Orange, drafter of the Compromise of Nobles (1568), and possibly the poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was laid out after 1850 where the city ramparts had stood, which were levelled between 1820 and 1840.

name: Eerste Marnixplantsoen
en: Philips of Marnix, Lord of Sint-Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and adviser of Prince William of Orange, drafter of the Compromise of Nobles (1568), and possibly the poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was laid out after 1850 where the city ramparts had stood, which were levelled between 1820 and 1840.

name: Eerste Nassaustraat
en: Named after our royal house of Orange-Nassau. Before it was named in 1879, the quay was called Buitensingel.

name: Eerste Oosterparkstraat
en: Named after the nearby Oosterpark, and originally (council decision of 15 November 1882) named Eerste, Tweede and Derde Parkstraat. The Eerste Oosterparkstraat was earlier called Oetgenspad, after Frans Hendriks Oetgens, a sixteenth-century burgomaster over whose land several paths were laid. Until 1895 the street name applied as far as the Linnaeusstraat. In that year the stretch along the park was given the park's name.

name: Eerste Passeerdersdwarsstraat
en: Passeren is the preparing and working of Spanish leather. When this kind of leatherwork was banned in central Amsterdam in 1631, the passeerderij settled here, next to the tanneries already there.

name: Eerste Ringdijkstraat
en: After its position relative to the Watergraafsmeer. Before the municipality of Watergraafsmeer was annexed, the Ooster Ringdijk was called Noorder- and Zuider-Ringdijk. The Eerste Ringdijkstraat was then called Schoollaan, and earlier still the name Dielemanstraat seems to have been used. A Tweede Ringdijkstraat (formerly Dijklaan) has since disappeared entirely through demolition.

name: Eerste Rozendwarsstraat
en: The flower (the rose).

name: Eerste Schinkelstraat
en: The name recalls the old roadside inn Schinkelhaven. Before 1922 the street was part of the Schinkelkade.

name: Eerste Sweelinckstraat
en: Jan Pieterszoon Sweelinck (1562-1621), a musician of great renown and organist of the Oude Kerk. He wrote many compositions on the psalms and love songs. Before 1896 part of the Tweede Sweelinckstraat lay in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel as the Tweede Hoedemakersdwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 22 August 1890).

name: Eerste Tuindwarsstraat
en: Tuin (garden) here means a yard or enclosed space. The street name comes from the Stadstimmertuin (the city's carpentry yard, the Stadswerf), which lay here from 1612 to 1660 (by the Lijnbaansgracht) and to which the street led.

name: Eerste Van der Helststraat
en: Bartholomeus van der Helst (1612-1670), painter of militia and regents' group portraits.

name: Eerste Van Swindenstraat
en: Jean Henri van Swinden (1746-1823), philosopher, mathematician and physicist, professor at Franeker and from 1785 in Amsterdam. He sat on the commission that fixed the metre, after which he worked out the metric system introduced in the Netherlands in 1816.

name: Eerste Vogelstraat
en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

name: Eerste Weteringdwarsstraat
en: The streets lie in the Weteringbuurt. The names recall the Wetering, which originally flowed from outside into the Spui; the Boerenwetering is a remnant of it. The Schans was once the rampart on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century the walls and ramparts were demolished. Parts were turned into promenades (Eerste and Tweede Weteringplantsoen), and a road was built that was at first called the Schans along its whole length but later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat. The Nieuwe Weteringstraat was laid out on the site freed by the demolition of the flour and bread factory. In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries this was the paving yard.

name: Eerste Weteringplantsoen
en: The streets lie in the Weteringbuurt. The names recall the Wetering, which originally flowed from outside into the Spui; the Boerenwetering is a remnant of it. The Schans was once the rampart on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century the walls and ramparts were demolished. Parts were turned into promenades (Eerste and Tweede Weteringplantsoen), and a road was built that was at first called the Schans along its whole length but later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat. The Nieuwe Weteringstraat was laid out on the site freed by the demolition of the flour and bread factory. In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries this was the paving yard.

name: Eerstegeluk
en: A South African place name.

name: Eeuwige Jeugdlaan
en: Probably named after the legendary spring, the 'Fountain of Eternal Youth'. The legend says that whoever drank from the fountain would look young. The avenue also borders the Jeugdland neighbourhood, built between 1995 and 1998, and the name can be derived from that too.

name: Efua Sutherlandstraat
en: Efua Theodora Sutherland-Morgue (1924-1996), Ghanaian writer, actress and social worker, head of the Ghana Experimental Theatre. In 1961 she founded the literary magazine 'Okyeame', and she was a researcher at the university's Institute of African Studies in Ghana. She contributed greatly to awareness of Ghanaian culture.

name: Egelantiersgracht
en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

name: Egelantiersstraat
en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

name: Egeldonk
en: A farm in Zundert (Noord-Brabant). In Noord-Brabant the ending donk is common and means a small rise.

name: Egelenburg
en: A former country house south-east of Heiloo (Noord-Holland), built by the lords of Warmenhuizen.

name: Egellelie
en: The egellelie is a plant native to the Cape in South Africa.

name: Egelskopstraat
en: A marsh plant (bur-reed) that grows well in small ponds.

name: Eggertstraat
en: Willem Eggert, Lord of Purmerland and Ilpendam (1340-1417), a very wealthy Amsterdammer, schepen (alderman) of the city and one of the founders of the Nieuwe Kerk. Before 1865 the street was called Ellendigesteeg (miserable alley).

name: Egidiusstraat
en: The person addressed in an anonymous medieval lament.

name: EGoli
en: eGoli is the Zulu name for Johannesburg, the largest city in South Africa, in the province of Gauteng. Literally: city of gold. Forty per cent of the world's gold has been found in or around this city.

name: Egstraat
en: The farm implement (a harrow). When first laid out, the street was part of the Zaaiersweg (council decision of 30 January 1924).

name: Ehrlichstraat
en: Paul Ehrlich (1854-1915), German physician who in 1910 discovered salvarsan, an arsenic preparation against syphilis. He received the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1908.

name: Eierlandstraat
en: The northern part of Texel, originally a separate dune island, later joined to Texel by a sand dike, after which the Eierland polder was formed by enclosing the mudflats. Extensive nature reserves lie on both the sea side and the Wadden side. The Eierlandse Gat (between Texel and Vlieland) is a seal reserve.

name: Eiger
en: A mountain peak in Switzerland, 3970 metres high.

name: Eijkmanstraat
en: Christiaan Eijkman (1858-1930), physician and bacteriologist, professor at Utrecht University. He discovered the cause of beriberi and received the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1929.

name: Eikenplein
en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

name: Eikenweg
en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

name: Eilandsgracht
en: This neighbourhood once had many tanneries, where the hides of elk (elanden), deer, bears and so on were worked.

name: Einthovenstraat
en: Willem Einthoven (1860-1927), Leiden professor of physiology and heart specialist, inventor of the string galvanometer. He received the Nobel Prize in 1924.

name: Eisdenstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Eisingastraat
en: Eise Eisinga (1744-1828), Frisian amateur astronomer. He built a planetarium that still exists in Franeker.

name: Ekangala
en: A village in South Africa, in the KwaNdebele area (formerly Transvaal) in the province of Mpumalanga.

name: EKapa
en: A South African name for Cape Town (colloquial).

name: Ekingenstraat
en: A church village on Noord-Beveland (Zeeland) drowned in 1532.

name: Eksteenfontein
en: A South African place name.

name: Eksterstraat
en: The bird (the magpie).

name: Elandsgracht
en: This neighbourhood once had many tanneries, where the hides of elk (elanden), deer, bears and so on were worked.

name: Elandsstraat
en: This neighbourhood once had many tanneries, where the hides of elk (elanden), deer, bears and so on were worked.

name: Elbaweg
en: An Italian island in the Mediterranean. Napoleon was exiled to Elba in 1814.

name: Elberveld
en: A South African place name.

name: Elckerlijcstraat
en: A fifteenth-century morality play (Everyman), attributed to Petrus van Diest. Its full title is 'Den spieghel der Salicheyt van Elckerlijc'.

name: Eldorado
