en: Spanish for 'the gilded one', after a myth about an initiation ritual of the Muisca people of Colombia, in which a new chief had himself covered entirely in gold dust and swam in a mythical lake. The legend slowly changed from a person into a land of gold, sought for centuries by conquistadors, the French, the English and the Dutch.

name: Elegaststraat
en: A character from the Middle Dutch chivalric romance 'Karel ende Elegast'.

name: Elektronstraat
en: The smallest quantity of negative electricity, one of the building blocks of the atom.

name: Elementenstraat
en: The unit (cell) in a galvanic battery.

name: Elfendansstraat
en: The name refers to the poem 'Elvendans' (elves' dance) by Jacqueline E. van der Waals (1868-1922), included in the collection 'Nieuwe Verzen' (1909).

name: Elim
en: (Fragment) to Park Frankendael.

name: Elisabeth Adriaansestraat
en: Elisabeth (Betsy) Adriaanse (Roermond, 1906 - Chur, 1939) was a pioneer as a lawyer and a campaigner for women's suffrage.

name: Elisabeth Boddaertstraat
en: Jonkvrouw Elisabeth Boddaert (1867-1948) founded homes for neglected children in the Netherlands.

name: Elisabeth Samsonstraat
en: Surinamese businesswoman (1715-1771) who belonged to the class of fairly well-off free mulattoes (people of mixed descent). Unlike many whites in the colony, she could read and write. She lived as an equal with the white Carl Otto Creutz. In the slave society, despite racist opposition, she won herself an important position.

name: Elisabeth van Dorpstraat
en: Elisabeth (Lizzy) van Dorp (Arnhem, 5 September 1872 - Banyubiru, 6 September 1945) was a pioneer as a lawyer, economist and politician, and a campaigner for women's suffrage.

name: Elisabeth Wolffstraat
en: Elisabeth Wolff, née Bekker (Betje Wolff) (1738-1804), writer. With Aagje Deken she wrote, among others, 'Sara Burgerhart' and 'Willem Leevend'.

name: Eliza van Calcarstraat
en: Eliza Carolina Ferdinanda van Calcar-Schiotling (1822-1904), educator and writer. In 'De dubbele roeping der vrouw' (the double calling of woman) she argued for education for women.

name: Elizabeth Anscombestraat
en: Elizabeth Anscombe (1919-2001) was a British analytic philosopher.

name: Elizabeth Cady Stantonplein
en: American activist (1815-1902) who campaigned for women's suffrage in the United States. She extended her activism to Europe too, and in 1888 helped found the International Council of Women.

name: Ella Fitzgeraldstraat
en: Ella Jane Fitzgerald (1917-1996), regarded as one of the most important American jazz singers in history. Her hallmarks included a range of four octaves, clear diction and a gift for scat singing.

name: Ellert Vlieropstraat
en: A captain of the Beggars' fleet who fought at the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

name: Elpermeer
en: A nature reserve in the Grollo forestry (Drenthe).

name: Elpermeerpad
en: A nature reserve in the Grollo forestry (Drenthe).

name: Elsje Christiaensbrug
en: Elsje Christiaens was an 18-year-old Danish girl who was strangled on the Dam in 1664 because she had killed her landlady with an axe. She was hanged on the gallows field.

name: Elsrijkdreef
en: A former farm in Amstelveen.

name: Elstarstraat
en: A Dutch apple variety, yellow-green with a red blush, bred from a cross of Golden Delicious and Ingrid Marie.

name: Elzenhagensingel
en: The name of a farm on the Buikslotermeerdijk, demolished in 1964.

name: Elzenstraat
en: The tree (the alder).

name: Emanuel van Meterenstraat
en: Southern Netherlandish merchant and historian (1535-1612), whose works include 'Historie der Nederlandscher oorlogen' (history of the Netherlands wars).

name: Emanzana
en: A nature reserve in South Africa, east of Johannesburg, known for its sulphur spring, which the area's first inhabitants called Emanzana. The Zulu name Emanzana means 'healing water'.

name: Emfuleni
en: A municipality in South Africa, in the province of Gauteng. The Zulu name means 'place where there are many rivers'. The municipality got the name because it lies beside the Vaal river.

name: Emilie Knappertstraat
en: The founder of social work in the Netherlands (1860-1952).

name: Emmalaan
en: Adelheid Emma Wilhelmina Theresia of Waldeck-Pyrmont (1858-1934), second wife of King Willem III, Queen Regent from 1890 to 1898, and mother of Queen Wilhelmina.

name: Emmaplein
en: Adelheid Emma Wilhelmina Theresia of Waldeck-Pyrmont (1858-1934), second wife of King Willem III, Queen Regent from 1890 to 1898, and mother of Queen Wilhelmina.

name: Emmastraat
en: Adelheid Emma Wilhelmina Theresia of Waldeck-Pyrmont (1858-1934), second wife of King Willem III, Queen Regent from 1890 to 1898, and mother of Queen Wilhelmina.

name: Emmeline Pankhurststraat
en: English campaigner for women's suffrage (1858-1928), among other things head of the English society for women's suffrage. In London she gave public lectures and organised protest marches. She was arrested several times for her militancy. Pankhurst died in 1928, the year the women of Great Britain got the vote.

name: Emmikhovenstraat
en: An area in the Land van Altena (Noord-Brabant) drowned in the St Elizabeth's flood.

name: Emmy Andriessestraat
en: Photographer (1914-1953). During the Second World War she joined a group of photographers later known as 'De Ondergedoken Camera' (the hidden camera) and made a photo report of the Hunger Winter in Amsterdam. After the war she concentrated mainly on portrait photography.

name: Empangeni
en: A town in South Africa, in the province of KwaZulu-Natal.

name: Endumeni
en: A town in South Africa, formerly Dundee, in the province of KwaZulu-Natal. The Zulu name means 'place of the thunderstorm'; lightning often strikes the Endumeni hill.

name: Engcobo
en: A town in South Africa, in the Eastern Cape province.

name: Enge Kerksteeg
en: After the Oude Kerk, which the alleys lead to from the Warmoesstraat, part of which was originally called Kerkstraat.

name: Enge Lombardsteeg
en: After the nearby lommerd, or Bank van Lening (pawnshop), founded in 1614.

name: Engelsesteeg
en: The alley was already called this in the sixteenth century. There used to be many inns here, which shows it was a popular neighbourhood, perhaps particularly with English sailors.

name: Enkeldoorn
en: A South African place name.

name: Enkhuizerplein
en: The Noord-Holland town of Enkhuizen.

name: Enkhuizerstraat
en: The Noord-Holland town of Enkhuizen.

name: Ennemaborg
en: A late-medieval Groningen borg (fortified manor) near Midwolde (Groningen), restored around 1700. In its present form a stately country house.

name: Enneüs Heermabrug
en: This bridge is named after Enneüs Heerma (1944-1999).

name: Ereprijsstraat
en: The plant.

name: Eversdal
en: A South African place name.

name: Fresiastraat
en: The plant.

name: Gaandeweg
en: The name belongs to the theme 'Sociaal en tevreden wonen' (Social and contented living) for the G-buurt Grunder/Grubbehoeve.

name: Galantstraat
en: The name belongs to the theme 'Sociaal en tevreden wonen' (Social and contented living) for the G-buurt Grunder/Grubbehoeve.

name: Ganzebloemstraat
en: The flower (the marigold), of the daisy family.

name: Ganzenweg
en: The water bird (the duck).

name: Gedempte Begijnensloot
en: The hof (courtyard), founded in the fourteenth century, was built to house beguines (lay sisters). The Begijnhof, together with the Sint Luciënklooster, was originally surrounded entirely by water. Behind the houses of the Kalverstraat ran a ditch, the Begijnensloot, which led from the Spui, not yet filled in at the time, to the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal. This ditch was neglected, and so what remained of it was filled in in 1865. It was given the name Gedempte Begijnensloot, a name made official by a council decision in 1914.

name: Glitterstraat
en: The name belongs to the theme 'Sociaal en tevreden wonen' (Social and contented living) for the G-buurt Grunder/Grubbehoeve.

name: Goed Geluimd hof
en: The name belongs to the theme 'Sociaal en tevreden wonen' (Social and contented living) for the G-buurt Grunder/Grubbehoeve.

name: Goudsbloemstraat
en: The flower (the marigold), of the daisy family.

name: Grimbergenstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

name: Grote Bickersstraat
en: These streets are on the Bickerseiland. This island was originally owned by Dr Johan Bicker (1591-1653), a shipbuilder and merchant, and a schepen (magistrate) and burgomaster of Amsterdam, who bought it in 1631. The streets later laid out on the island automatically took the name of its founder.

name: Grote Wittenburgerstraat
en: One of the three eastern islands (with Kattenburg and Oostenburg), laid out in the second half of the seventeenth century and built up with shipyards and houses from the start. One of the first yards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. This is very probably where the name Wittenburg comes from.

name: Hagedoornplein
en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

name: Hamontstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Hardwareweg
en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

name: Hechtelstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Herentalsstraat
en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

name: Het Breed
en: These names were given for the meaning of the word (broad field), as a counterpart to Het Hoogt and Het Laagt.

name: Heusdenstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Heverleestraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

name: Hoendiepstraat
en: A canal in the province of Groningen.

name: Hoogte Kadijk
en: When a great deal of land had built up through silting outside the old sea dike (St. Antoniesdijk), a summer dike, or quay dike (kadijk), was built. It was originally called the new sea dike, but that name later fell out of use. When this new dike was raised further, people spoke of the Laagte (low part) and the Hoogte (high part) of the Kadijk. Until 1943 the Tussen Kadijken was called Korte Kerkstraat. This is because it lies in line with the Plantage Kerklaan, although it has never been connected to it.

en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

name: Tweede Looiersdwarsstraat
en: The tanneries and the hide trade, after which this street and nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal ring are named, were at first sited outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came inside the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after these long-flourishing trades, starting with the Runstraat (run is tanbark) and the Huidenstraat (hides street). After 1658 the tanneries spread to land east of the Vijzelgracht, where the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat are now. Before it was filled in, the Derde Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision of 1 June 1898).

name: Tweede Marnixplantsoen
en: Philips of Marnix, Lord of Sint-Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and adviser of Prince William of Orange, drafter of the Compromise of Nobles (1568), and possibly the poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was laid out after 1850 where the city ramparts had stood, which were levelled between 1820 and 1840.

name: Tweede Nassaustraat
en: Named after our royal house of Orange-Nassau. Before it was named in 1879, the quay was called Buitensingel.

name: Tweede Oosterparkstraat
en: Named after the nearby Oosterpark, and originally (council decision of 15 November 1882) named Eerste, Tweede and Derde Parkstraat. The Eerste Oosterparkstraat was earlier called Oetgenspad, after Frans Hendriks Oetgens, a sixteenth-century burgomaster over whose land several paths were laid. Until 1895 the street name applied as far as the Linnaeusstraat. In that year the stretch along the park was given the park's name.

name: Tweede Passeerdersdwarsstraat
en: Passeren is the preparing and working of Spanish leather. When this kind of leatherwork was banned in central Amsterdam in 1631, the passeerderij settled here, next to the tanneries already there.

name: Tweede Rozendwarsstraat
en: The flower (the rose).

name: Tweede Schinkelstraat
en: The name recalls the old roadside inn Schinkelhaven. Before 1922 the street was part of the Schinkelkade.

name: Tweede Sweelinckstraat
en: Jan Pieterszoon Sweelinck (1562-1621), a musician of great renown and organist of the Oude Kerk. He wrote many compositions on the psalms and love songs. Before 1896 part of the Tweede Sweelinckstraat lay in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel as the Tweede Hoedemakersdwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 22 August 1890).

name: Tweede Tuindwarsstraat
en: Tuin (garden) here means a yard or enclosed space. The street name comes from the Stadstimmertuin (the city's carpentry yard, the Stadswerf), which lay here from 1612 to 1660 (by the Lijnbaansgracht) and to which the street led.

name: Tweede Van der Helststraat
en: Bartholomeus van der Helst (1612-1670), painter of militia and regents' group portraits.

name: Tweede van Swindenstraat
en: Jean Henri van Swinden (1746-1823), philosopher, mathematician and physicist, professor at Franeker and from 1785 in Amsterdam. He sat on the commission that fixed the metre, after which he worked out the metric system introduced in the Netherlands in 1816.

name: Tweede Weteringdwarsstraat
en: The streets lie in the Weteringbuurt. The names recall the Wetering, which originally flowed from outside into the Spui; the Boerenwetering is a remnant of it. The Schans was once the rampart on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century the walls and ramparts were demolished. Parts were turned into promenades (Eerste and Tweede Weteringplantsoen), and a road was built that was at first called the Schans along its whole length but later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat. The Nieuwe Weteringstraat was laid out on the site freed by the demolition of the flour and bread factory. In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries this was the paving yard.
